                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "# Requirements Document — Multi-Platform Streaming\n\n## Introduction\n\nThis spec extends Invisible A/V Booth with the ability to stream simultaneously to multiple platforms (YouTube and Facebook) from a single OBS source. It introduces platform-specific API integrations for broadcast lifecycle management (create, go live, end), a configurable metadata template system with multiple named templates for titles and descriptions, an RTMP relay layer for fan-out delivery, and a \"Manage Streams\" UI for per-platform stream control during a live session.\n\nThis spec depends on the foundational platform delivered by the `livestream-control-system` spec (authentication, dashboard, OBS widget, session manifest, event bus, notification system). It modifies the existing OBS streaming flow and extends the session manifest with new template capabilities.\n\nThis spec supersedes the single `streamTitleTemplate` field stored in `device_connections.metadata` (original spec Requirement 9). That field is replaced by the `metadata_templates` table. The existing `SessionManifestService.interpolate()` method is reworked to support multiple templates and the new `{verseText}` token. This spec extends the `SessionManifest` interface with two new fields: `titleTemplateId` and `descriptionTemplateId` (see Req 4.8). This spec also modifies the post-login navigation for ADMIN users (original spec Requirement 5.3): ADMIN users are redirected to the new Admin Index Page (`/admin`) instead of the Dashboard Selection Screen.\n\nRecording controls (Start/Stop Recording) remain unchanged in the OBS widget and are unaffected by this spec. The \"Manage Streams\" button coexists alongside the existing recording button.\n\nThis spec introduces a breaking change to the `ConnectionStatus` model: the boolean `healthy` field is replaced by a four-value `status` field (`\"healthy\"` | `\"degraded\"` | `\"unhealthy\"` | `\"inactive\"`). All existing `ConnectionStatus` usages (e.g., the OBS widget's `{ label: \"OBS\", healthy: obsState.connected }`) must be migrated to the new `status` field. The OBS widget's connection list expands from one entry (\"OBS\") to three (\"OBS\", \"Relay\", \"Stream\").\n\nSee `docs/architecture-decisions/001-multi-platform-streaming.md` for the architectural decision record on the hybrid relay approach.\n\n---\n\n## Glossary\n\n- **Platform**: A streaming destination service (e.g., YouTube, Facebook). Each platform has its own API integration, OAuth credentials, and RTMP ingest URL.\n- **PlatformConfig**: The stored configuration for a streaming platform, including OAuth tokens (encrypted), platform-specific settings, and enabled status. Stored in a new `streaming_platforms` database table.\n- **Broadcast**: A platform-specific live video object created via the platform's API before streaming begins. YouTube calls this a `liveBroadcast` + `liveStream`; Facebook calls it a `LiveVideo`. The backend abstracts both behind a common interface.\n- **RTMP Relay**: A local `node-media-server` instance that accepts OBS's RTMP stream and makes it available for per-destination FFmpeg forwarding processes. Starts on backend startup and runs for the lifetime of the backend process.\n- **Relay Forwarder**: An individual FFmpeg child process that reads from the local RTMP relay and forwards the stream (via `-c copy`, no re-encoding) to a single platform's RTMP ingest URL.\n- **MetadataTemplate**: A named, admin-configured format string used to generate stream titles or descriptions. Contains placeholder tokens (e.g., `{Speaker}`, `{Title}`, `{Scripture}`, `{verseText}`) that are interpolated with SessionManifest values at stream start time.\n- **TemplateCategory**: Either `title` or `description`. Title templates and description templates are independent — a user selects one of each (description may be \"None\").\n- **ManageStreamsModal**: The modal UI that replaces the simple Start/Stop Stream buttons, allowing per-platform stream control during a live session.\n- **AdminIndexPage**: The landing page for ADMIN users at `/admin`, listing links to all admin management sections and the dashboard chooser.\n- **No Source**: A platform status indicating that OBS has disconnected from the RTMP relay while FFmpeg forwarders were active. The platform broadcast may still be alive on the platform side, but no video data is being delivered. Transitions to \"Recovering\" when OBS reconnects.\n- **Recovering**: A platform status indicating that OBS has reconnected to the relay and the backend is verifying via the platform's API that the broadcast is still active. Transitions to \"Streaming\" on success or \"Error\" if the broadcast has ended.\n\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n### Requirement 1: Streaming Platform Configuration\n\n**User Story:** As an administrator, I want to configure streaming platform connections (YouTube, Facebook) through the admin UI, so that the system can create broadcasts and stream to those platforms without manual setup each time.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL store streaming platform configurations in a `streaming_platforms` database table with fields: `id`, `platformType` (e.g., `\"youtube\"`, `\"facebook\"`), `label`, `enabled`, `encryptedAccessToken`, `encryptedRefreshToken`, `tokenExpiresAt`, `platformMetadata` (JSON string for platform-specific data such as YouTube channel ID or Facebook page ID), and `createdAt`. THE `platformType` field SHALL have a unique constraint — only one configuration per platform type is allowed.\n2. THE Backend SHALL encrypt OAuth tokens at rest using the same AES-256-GCM pattern and `DEVICE_SECRET_KEY` used for device connection passwords.\n3. THE Backend SHALL expose REST endpoints for reading, updating, enabling/disabling, and deleting streaming platform configurations; all endpoints SHALL require the ADMIN role.\n4. THE Frontend SHALL provide a unified streaming platform management page at `/admin/platforms` using a two-panel layout (list + detail) matching the Device Management pattern. The left panel lists configured platforms with their connected account name (truncated with ellipsis); the right panel shows platform-specific settings. Platform-specific detail components SHALL be separate files for modularity.\n5. THE admin page SHALL include an \"Add Connection\" button with a dropdown offering: YouTube, Facebook Page, and Facebook Profile. Selecting an option initiates the OAuth 2.0 authorization flow for that platform with the appropriate scopes. FOR Facebook Profile, only `publish_video` is requested (no Page selection screen). FOR Facebook Page, `publish_video`, `pages_manage_posts`, and `pages_read_engagement` are requested. OAuth setup MUST be performed from a browser on the machine running the backend, because the OAuth callback URL uses `localhost` (Google and Facebook reject non-public domains like `invisible.av`). If a public domain is configured, OAuth can be performed from any device. This is a one-time admin task documented in `docs/setup.md`.\n6. WHEN a platform is connected, THE admin page detail panel SHALL display the connected account name (YouTube channel name, Facebook page name, or Facebook profile name) and a \"Disconnect\" button. FOR Facebook Page connections, after OAuth, THE Backend SHALL fetch the list of Pages the admin manages; if multiple Pages exist, THE admin page SHALL display a Page selector dropdown. IF the admin manages only one Page, it SHALL be auto-selected. FOR Facebook Profile connections, the user's profile is used directly (no Page selection needed). The `targetType` (`\"page\"` or `\"user\"`) and associated ID SHALL be stored in `platformMetadata`.\n7. THE Backend SHALL validate stored OAuth tokens on startup by making a lightweight API call to each enabled platform; IF a token is invalid or expired, THE Backend SHALL attempt to refresh it (YouTube only — Facebook Page tokens are long-lived). IF refresh fails, THE Backend SHALL emit a Banner-level notification: \"{Platform} authorization expired — an admin needs to reconnect.\" FOR Facebook Page connections, THE Backend SHALL additionally validate that the stored Page ID is still accessible; IF the Page is inaccessible, THE Backend SHALL emit a Banner-level notification: \"Facebook Page '{Page Name}' is no longer accessible — an admin needs to reconnect.\"\n8. THE Backend SHALL expose OAuth callback endpoints (`GET /api/auth/callback/youtube` and `GET /api/auth/callback/facebook`) that receive the authorization code from the platform, exchange it for access and refresh tokens, encrypt and store the tokens in the `streaming_platforms` table, and redirect back to the admin platforms page with a success or failure query parameter. AFTER storing tokens, THE Backend SHALL call `reloadPlatforms()` on the `StreamingPlatformService` so the frontend receives updated platform readiness without a server restart.\n9. FOR YouTube, THE admin page detail panel SHALL include a \"Default Privacy\" setting with options: `public`, `unlisted` (default), and `private`. This value SHALL be stored in `platformMetadata` and used when creating broadcasts (Req 6.4). FOR Facebook Profile connections, THE admin page SHALL include a \"Default Privacy\" setting with options: `Public` (EVERYONE), `Friends` (ALL_FRIENDS), and `Only Me` (SELF, default). FOR Facebook Page connections, privacy is displayed as read-only \"Public (Pages are always public)\".\n10. THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL display the privacy setting alongside the platform name for any platform that has privacy configured (e.g., \"YouTube (Unlisted)\", \"Facebook (Only Me)\"). FOR AvVolunteer users, this is display-only. FOR ADMIN and AvPowerUser users, THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL allow privacy override per-broadcast (not persisted to admin configuration).\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 2: OAuth Token Lifecycle and Prerequisites\n\n**User Story:** As a system operator, I want OAuth tokens to refresh automatically without any manual intervention, so that streaming works reliably every week without an admin needing to re-authorize before each service.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. FOR YouTube, THE Backend SHALL store the OAuth 2.0 refresh token and use it to silently obtain new access tokens when the current access token expires (typically 1 hour); this refresh SHALL require no user interaction.\n2. FOR Facebook, THE Backend SHALL obtain a long-lived Page access token during the initial OAuth flow; this token does not expire under normal conditions and requires no refresh cycle.\n3. WHEN a token refresh fails (e.g., user revoked access, Google Cloud project suspended), THE Backend SHALL mark the platform as unhealthy, emit a Banner-level notification identifying the affected platform, and exclude that platform from the stream start flow until an admin reconnects.\n4. THE Backend SHALL attempt token refresh proactively (before expiry) rather than waiting for an API call to fail; for YouTube, THE Backend SHALL refresh the access token when it is within 5 minutes of expiry.\n5. THE Backend SHALL NOT store plaintext tokens in logs, error messages, or API responses.\n6. THE Backend SHALL require the following environment variables for OAuth: `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID`, `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `FACEBOOK_APP_ID`, `FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET`. IF any are missing at startup and the corresponding platform is enabled, THE Backend SHALL log a clear error identifying the missing variable(s). These values come from the Google Cloud Console and Facebook Developer portal respectively.\n7. `docs/setup.md` SHALL document the external prerequisites for each platform: (a) YouTube: create a Google Cloud project, enable the YouTube Data API v3, create OAuth 2.0 credentials (Web application type), leave Authorized JavaScript Origins blank (server-side flow), and configure the authorized redirect URI to `https://localhost/api/auth/callback/youtube`. (b) Facebook: create a Facebook App, add the Facebook Login and Live Video API products, and configure the Valid OAuth Redirect URI to `https://localhost/api/auth/callback/facebook`. `docs/setup.md` SHALL note that OAuth connection must be performed from a browser on the backend machine itself (localhost), because Google and Facebook reject non-public domains like `invisible.av`. This is a one-time setup step; after tokens are stored, all other admin and volunteer operations work from any device on the network via `invisible.av`. If a public domain is available, it can be used instead of `localhost` by updating the redirect URIs in the respective developer consoles and setting `APP_URL` in `.env`.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 3: Named Metadata Templates\n\n**User Story:** As an administrator, I want to create multiple named title and description templates, so that volunteers can choose the appropriate format for different types of services (e.g., with or without a scripture reference).\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL store metadata templates in a `metadata_templates` database table with fields: `id`, `name` (admin-provided display name, e.g., \"Speaker and Title\"), `category` (`\"title\"` or `\"description\"`), `formatString` (the template with placeholder tokens), `roleMinimum` (`\"AvVolunteer\"` | `\"AvPowerUser\"` | `\"ADMIN\"` — the minimum role required to see this template; follows the same hierarchy as all other RBAC in the system), and `createdAt`.\n2. THE Backend SHALL support the following placeholder tokens in templates: `{Date}`, `{Speaker}`, `{Title}`, `{Scripture}`, `{verseText}`. `{Date}` is always today's ISO 8601 date. `{Scripture}` resolves to the formatted reference (e.g., \"John 3:16-17\"). `{verseText}` resolves to the full KJV text of the referenced verse(s), formatted per Requirement 9.\n3. WHEN formatting the `{Scripture}` token, IF the stored scripture reference starts at verse 0, THE Backend SHALL display the range starting at verse 1 (e.g., a stored range of Psalm 23:0-2 displays as `Psalm 23:1-2`). IF the stored reference is a single verse 0 with no verseEnd, THE Backend SHALL display `Psalm 23` (chapter only, no verse number).\n4. THE Backend SHALL expose REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting metadata templates; all endpoints SHALL require the ADMIN role.\n5. THE Frontend SHALL provide a template management page at `/admin/templates` accessible only to ADMIN users. The page SHALL display two side-by-side lists (fixed height, independently scrollable): \"Title Templates\" on the left and \"Description Templates\" on the right. Each list item SHALL show the template's display name, its `roleMinimum` as a muted badge (e.g., \"AvVolunteer\"), and Edit and Delete buttons. The \"None\" description template SHALL appear in the description list without Edit or Delete buttons (system-managed, no role badge displayed). Each list SHALL have a \"Create\" button for adding new templates.\n6. DELETING a template SHALL require a ConfirmationModal showing the template's display name and full format string before proceeding.\n7. CREATING or EDITING a template SHALL open a modal containing: a Name field (text input), a Role Minimum dropdown (`AvVolunteer` / `AvPowerUser` / `ADMIN`), and a Format String field. The format string field SHALL be a single-line input for title templates and a multi-line textarea for description templates.\n8. THE template create/edit modal SHALL use a two-step validate-then-save flow: (a) the modal initially shows a \"Validate\" button (not \"Save\"), (b) tapping \"Validate\" runs validation checks, (c) if no blocking errors exist the button changes to \"Save\", (d) any edit to the Name, Format String, or Role Minimum fields (input event with actual data change) reverts the button back to \"Validate\".\n9. VALIDATION SHALL check: (a) unknown placeholder tokens in the format string — BLOCKER; (b) duplicate format string (case-sensitive comparison with all whitespace runs — spaces, tabs, newlines — collapsed to a single space and leading/trailing whitespace trimmed, against all other templates in the same category, excluding self when editing) — BLOCKER, message: \"Duplicate of {existingTemplateName}\"; (c) non-unique name within the same category — BLOCKER; (d) if `roleMinimum` is `AvVolunteer` and another template in the same category already has `roleMinimum: AvVolunteer` — WARNING (amber), message: \"Volunteers will see multiple {title/description} templates and must choose between them.\" Blockers are shown as red errors; warnings are shown as amber. The \"Save\" button SHALL NOT appear while any blocker exists.\n10. IF a template contains `{verseText}` or `{Scripture}` and the SessionManifest has no scripture reference, THE Backend SHALL substitute `[No Scripture]` for `{Scripture}` and `[No Verse Text]` for `{verseText}`.\n11. AT LEAST one title template SHALL exist in the system; THE Backend SHALL reject deletion of the last remaining title template.\n12. ON first startup, IF the `metadata_templates` table is empty, THE Backend SHALL auto-create a default title template with name `\"Speaker and Title\"`, category `\"title\"`, `roleMinimum: \"AvVolunteer\"`, and formatString `\"{Date} – {Speaker} – {Title}\"`. This follows the same bootstrap pattern as the admin user auto-creation.\n13. THE system SHALL represent \"None\" (no description template) as a built-in template with category `\"description\"`, name `\"None\"`, `roleMinimum: \"AvVolunteer\"`, and an empty formatString (`\"\"`). This template is auto-created during the seed step alongside the default title template. Using an empty-string template instead of a null `descriptionTemplateId` eliminates null checks throughout the interpolation and persistence paths. The \"None\" template SHALL NOT be deletable or editable by admins — it is system-managed.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 4: Template Selection and Unified Field Collection\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want to select a title template and an optional description template before entering metadata, so that I only see the input fields that are actually needed for my chosen templates.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Frontend SHALL present two dropdowns (side-by-side on wide viewports, stacked on narrow viewports) for template selection in the SessionManifestModal: one labeled \"Title Format\" for title templates and one labeled \"Description Format\" for description templates. Both dropdowns SHALL always be visible regardless of how many options exist. THE Frontend SHALL fetch the list of available templates via REST (`GET /api/templates`) when the SessionManifestModal opens (not pushed via Socket.io); the backend filters by the authenticated user's role derived from the JWT. If an admin modifies templates while the modal is open, the volunteer sees the previous list until the modal is closed and reopened. THE Frontend SHALL filter templates by the authenticated user's role — a user sees only templates with `roleMinimum` at or below their role in the hierarchy (ADMIN > AvPowerUser > AvVolunteer). The description dropdown SHALL always include the \"None\" option. Auto-select logic: IF exactly one non-\"None\" title template is visible to the user, THE Frontend SHALL auto-select it. IF exactly one non-\"None\" description template is visible to the user, THE Frontend SHALL auto-select it (not \"None\"). IF zero non-\"None\" description templates are visible, THE Frontend SHALL auto-select \"None\". IF two or more non-\"None\" templates are visible in either category, THE Frontend SHALL leave that dropdown unselected.\n2. UNTIL both dropdowns have a selection (title is required; description may be \"None\" which is itself a valid selection), THE Frontend SHALL NOT display metadata input fields; instead, THE Frontend SHALL display a message in muted text: \"Select title and description formats above to continue\".\n3. AFTER both templates are selected, THE Frontend SHALL compute the union of all unique placeholder tokens across both selected templates and present one input field per unique token. If both the title and description templates reference `{Title}`, the user sees one Title input — not two.\n4. `{Scripture}` and `{verseText}` SHALL share a single scripture reference input. If either token appears in any selected template, the scripture reference picker SHALL be shown exactly once.\n5. `{Date}` SHALL NOT produce an input field — it is always auto-populated by the backend.\n6. WHEN the user switches between templates, THE Frontend SHALL preserve all previously entered field values. Switching from a template that uses `{Scripture}` to one that does not SHALL NOT clear the scripture reference — it remains available if the user switches back.\n7. THE Frontend SHALL disable the Save button until all required fields for the selected templates have values. A field is required if its corresponding token appears in either selected template (excluding `{Date}`).\n8. THE selected template IDs (`titleTemplateId` and `descriptionTemplateId`) SHALL be included in the SessionManifest and persisted to the backend alongside other manifest fields. This ensures template selections survive page refreshes and are visible to all connected clients.\n9. THE Frontend SHALL store the most recently used template IDs in localStorage (keyed per device, not per user). WHEN the SessionManifestModal opens and no templates are selected in the current SessionManifest, THE Frontend SHALL pre-select the last-used templates from localStorage. This eliminates the template selection step for repeat use on the same device.\n10. THE `BUS_SESSION_MANIFEST_UPDATED` event payload SHALL be expanded to include `interpolatedDescription` and `manifestReady` alongside the existing `interpolatedStreamTitle`. When the description template is \"None\" (empty formatString), `interpolatedDescription` SHALL be an empty string. `manifestReady` SHALL be `true` when a title template is selected and all tokens referenced by the selected templates (excluding `{Date}`) have non-empty values in the manifest; `false` otherwise. Both interpolated values and `manifestReady` are pre-computed by the backend so all subscribers and the frontend read the same result.\n11. THE OBS Widget metadata preview row SHALL display the interpolated title (existing behavior) and, when a description template other than \"None\" is selected, a truncated single-line preview of the interpolated description below it. Tapping the description preview SHALL open an Ionic popover showing the full multi-line description with line breaks preserved. This uses the same popover pattern already established for the title preview (tap-to-expand). The description preview row SHALL display \"No description\" in muted text when the \"None\" template is selected.\n12. THE stream start confirmation modal (Req 6.7) SHALL show both the interpolated title (in the existing visually distinct block) and the interpolated description (if not empty) below it, so the volunteer can verify all metadata before going live. The description in the confirmation modal SHALL show the full text with line breaks preserved (no truncation), since this is the last verification step.\n13. IF a selected template ID in the SessionManifest or localStorage cache references a template that no longer exists or that is not visible to the current user's role (e.g., admin deleted it, or changed its `roleMinimum` above the user's role), THE Frontend SHALL clear that selection and show the template dropdown in its unselected state. THE Backend SHALL treat a missing template ID as if no template is selected and substitute placeholders in the interpolated output.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 5: RTMP Relay Infrastructure\n\n**User Story:** As a system architect, I want a local RTMP relay that accepts OBS's stream and fans it out to multiple destinations independently, so that one platform's failure does not affect others.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL start a `node-media-server` instance as the local RTMP relay on backend startup, listening on a configurable port (default: `1935`, configurable via `RELAY_PORT` environment variable). The relay runs for the lifetime of the backend process — it is not started/stopped per streaming session.\n2. THE relay SHALL accept exactly one inbound RTMP stream from OBS at the path `/live/stream`.\n3. THE Backend SHALL spawn one FFmpeg child process per active streaming destination; each process SHALL read from the local relay and forward to the platform's RTMP ingest URL using `-c copy` (no re-encoding).\n4. WHEN a single FFmpeg forwarder process exits unexpectedly, THE Backend SHALL NOT terminate other active forwarders; THE Backend SHALL capture the FFmpeg process's stderr output, log it, and immediately attempt auto-recovery: (a) emit a Banner-level notification: \"{Platform} stream interrupted — attempting to reconnect…\", (b) wait 2 seconds, then respawn the FFmpeg process with the same RTMP ingest URL, (c) after the new process has been alive for 5 seconds, poll the platform's API to verify the broadcast is still active and accepting data — if the API confirms the broadcast is active, consider recovery successful and auto-clear the Banner; if the API reports the broadcast has ended, treat recovery as failed and transition to step (e), (d) if the new process exits before the 5-second verification window, retry with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s) up to 3 retries or 45 seconds total (whichever comes first), (e) if all retries are exhausted or the API reports the broadcast has ended, transition the platform status to \"Error\", update the Banner to a permanent message: \"{Platform} stream failed — tap Start to create a new stream\", and stop retrying. The volunteer can manually restart the platform from the ManageStreamsModal (which creates a new broadcast). The platform broadcast is not explicitly ended by the backend during auto-recovery — YouTube's `enableAutoStop` and Facebook's auto-end will handle cleanup if recovery fails and the volunteer does not manually restart.\n5. THE Backend SHALL configure OBS (via `obs-websocket` `SetStreamServiceSettings`) to stream to `rtmp://localhost:{RELAY_PORT}/live/stream` on OBS connection (not just on stream start), ensuring OBS is always pointed at the relay whenever the system is running. Before starting the OBS stream, THE Backend SHALL read back the current settings via `GetStreamServiceSettings` and verify they point at the relay; IF they have been changed externally (e.g., someone opened OBS and modified the settings), THE Backend SHALL auto-correct them and log a warning.\n6. IF the relay fails to start (e.g., port already in use), THE Backend SHALL log a clear error message identifying the port conflict and SHALL NOT attempt to start platform streams. THE Backend SHALL emit a Banner-level notification: \"RTMP relay failed to start — check server logs.\"\n7. IF the relay crashes during operation, THE Backend SHALL detect the failure and attempt to restart the relay up to 3 times with 5-second delays. IF a restart succeeds, THE Backend SHALL emit a Banner-level notification that auto-clears: \"RTMP relay recovered.\" OBS's built-in reconnect logic will re-establish the connection to the relay once it is back. IF all 3 restart attempts fail, THE Backend SHALL emit a persistent Banner: \"RTMP relay is down — streaming is unavailable. Check server logs.\" and SHALL NOT attempt further restarts until the backend is restarted.\n8. FFmpeg SHALL be a documented prerequisite in `docs/setup.md`; THE Backend SHALL verify FFmpeg is available on the system PATH at startup and log a clear error if it is not found. IF FFmpeg is not found, THE Backend SHALL also emit a persistent Banner-level notification: \"FFmpeg is not installed — streaming is unavailable. Contact an administrator.\"\n9. WHEN the backend process exits (gracefully or via crash), THE relay and all FFmpeg child processes SHALL be cleaned up. The backend SHALL register signal handlers (`SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`) to terminate child processes on shutdown. For crash scenarios, FFmpeg processes are orphaned but will self-terminate when their RTMP input source (the relay) disappears.\n10. WHEN OBS disconnects from the relay while FFmpeg forwarder processes are active (detected via the relay's publisher disconnect event, not via FFmpeg process behavior), THE Backend SHALL immediately transition all active platform statuses to \"No Source\" (distinct from \"Streaming\", \"Error\", or \"Idle\"). THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL display \"No Source — OBS has disconnected. Streams will resume automatically when OBS reconnects.\" for each affected platform with no action button. The volunteer's primary recovery path is the OBS reconnect flow (the existing OBS disconnect Modal from the original spec); the ManageStreamsModal's \"No Source\" state is informational only. FFmpeg forwarder processes SHALL be left running during \"No Source\" (they will stall but not exit immediately); IF an FFmpeg process does exit while in \"No Source\" state, THE Backend SHALL NOT trigger the auto-recovery logic from Req 5.4 — recovery is deferred until OBS reconnects. WHEN OBS reconnects to the relay and data resumes, THE Backend SHALL transition each platform from \"No Source\" to \"Recovering\" and poll the platform's API to verify the broadcast is still active. IF the API confirms the broadcast is active, THE Backend SHALL transition the platform to \"Streaming\" and auto-clear any related Banner. IF the API reports the broadcast has ended (e.g., YouTube's `enableAutoStop` fired during the gap), THE Backend SHALL transition the platform to \"Error\" with message \"{Platform} broadcast ended during disconnect — tap Start to create a new stream.\"\n11. THE OBS Widget's `WidgetContainer` SHALL display a \"Relay\" connection status indicator alongside the existing \"OBS\" indicator. The relay indicator SHALL use a four-state model: (a) green solid dot (`healthy`) — relay is running and OBS is connected to it; popover text: \"Relay: Healthy\", (b) grey solid dot (`inactive`) — relay is running but OBS is not connected to it (normal pre-stream state); popover text: \"Relay: Waiting for OBS\", (c) red blinking dot (`unhealthy`) — relay has failed to start or has crashed and recovery failed; popover text: \"Relay: Failed\", (d) grey solid dot (`inactive`) — no streaming platforms are configured or enabled (relay is running but unused); popover text: \"Relay: No platforms configured\". The grey dot SHALL use `color-text-muted` (`#A0A0A0`) which has a verified ~5.3:1 contrast ratio against `color-bg`. WHEN the relay is in the `unhealthy` state, THE \"Manage Streams\" button SHALL be disabled with sub-label \"Streaming unavailable\".\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 6: Multi-Platform Stream Start Flow\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want to select which platforms to stream to when starting a stream, so that I can broadcast to YouTube and Facebook simultaneously with a single action.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. WHEN the user taps \"Manage Streams\" (replacing the previous \"Start Stream\" button), THE Frontend SHALL open the ManageStreamsModal. The \"Manage Streams\" button coexists alongside the existing Start/Stop Recording button in the OBS widget.\n2. IF no platforms are configured and enabled, THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL display a message: \"No streaming platforms configured. Contact an administrator.\"\n3. THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL list all configured and enabled platforms with their current status (Idle, Starting, Streaming, Stopping, No Source, Recovering, Error) and available actions. WHILE a platform is in \"Starting\" status, THE modal SHALL display a step-level progress indicator for that platform (e.g., \"Creating broadcast…\", \"Connecting…\", \"Waiting for platform…\") so the volunteer knows the system is working and not frozen. WHILE a platform is in \"Recovering\" status, THE modal SHALL display a spinner with \"Verifying stream…\"\n4. WHEN the user initiates \"Start All\" or starts an individual platform, THE Backend SHALL read the current manifest and interpolated strings from its own `SessionManifestService` (the frontend does not send manifest data with start commands — the backend is the authority) and execute the following sequence per platform in parallel (all platforms start simultaneously; each platform's sequence is independent): (a) create the broadcast via the platform's API with the interpolated title and description (for YouTube, set `contentDetails.enableAutoStart: true` and `contentDetails.enableAutoStop: true`), (b) obtain the RTMP ingest URL, (c) ensure OBS is streaming to the relay (configure OBS stream settings and start OBS stream if not already streaming) — this step is a shared prerequisite: it executes once regardless of how many platforms are starting, and all platform sequences wait for it to complete before proceeding to step (d), (d) spawn an FFmpeg forwarder process for that platform. `enableAutoStart` lets YouTube auto-transition to live when it detects incoming data, eliminating the fragile manual transition polling. `enableAutoStop` lets YouTube auto-end the broadcast ~1 minute after data stops, serving as a safety net if the explicit end-broadcast API call (Req 7.4) fails. The tradeoff: crash recovery always creates a new broadcast rather than reconnecting to the existing one, because `enableAutoStop` ends the broadcast before a volunteer would realistically notice and respond. This is acceptable — the volunteer experience is the same either way (tap \"Start Stream\" in the ManageStreamsModal).\n5. IF a platform broadcast creation fails, THE Backend SHALL skip that platform, continue with remaining platforms, and emit a Banner-level notification identifying the failed platform and the reason.\n6. THE \"Start All\" button SHALL be disabled (greyed out) when all configured platforms are already streaming or when a start sequence is already in progress.\n7. BEFORE starting any platform stream, THE Frontend SHALL display a ConfirmationModal: \"Start streaming to {platform list}?\" with confirm label \"Go Live\" and cancel label \"Cancel\". The platform list SHALL use each platform's `label` field from `streaming_platforms`, formatted as \"{label}\" for one platform and \"{label1} and {label2}\" for two.\n8. THE \"Manage Streams\" button SHALL be disabled unless the SessionManifest contains at least the fields required by the selected templates; THE button sub-label SHALL follow the priority order defined in Req 12.4.\n9. IF any step in the platform start sequence does not complete within 30 seconds, THE Backend SHALL transition that platform's status to \"Error\" with a descriptive timeout message and continue with remaining platforms."
                }

                  {
                    "Text": "# Requirements Document — Multi-Platform Streaming\n\n## Introduction\n\nThis spec extends Invisible A/V Booth with the ability to stream simultaneously to multiple platforms (YouTube and Facebook) from a single OBS source. It introduces platform-specific API integrations for broadcast lifecycle management (create, go live, end), a configurable metadata template system with multiple named templates for titles and descriptions, an RTMP relay layer for fan-out delivery, and a \"Manage Streams\" UI for per-platform stream control during a live session.\n\nThis spec depends on the foundational platform delivered by the `livestream-control-system` spec (authentication, dashboard, OBS widget, session manifest, event bus, notification system). It modifies the existing OBS streaming flow and extends the session manifest with new template capabilities.\n\nThis spec supersedes the single `streamTitleTemplate` field stored in `device_connections.metadata` (original spec Requirement 9). That field is replaced by the `metadata_templates` table. The existing `SessionManifestService.interpolate()` method is reworked to support multiple templates and the new `{verseText}` token. This spec extends the `SessionManifest` interface with two new fields: `titleTemplateId` and `descriptionTemplateId` (see Req 4.8). This spec also modifies the post-login navigation for ADMIN users (original spec Requirement 5.3): ADMIN users are redirected to the new Admin Index Page (`/admin`) instead of the Dashboard Selection Screen.\n\nRecording controls (Start/Stop Recording) remain unchanged in the OBS widget and are unaffected by this spec. The \"Manage Streams\" button coexists alongside the existing recording button.\n\nThis spec introduces a breaking change to the `ConnectionStatus` model: the boolean `healthy` field is replaced by a four-value `status` field (`\"healthy\"` | `\"degraded\"` | `\"unhealthy\"` | `\"inactive\"`). All existing `ConnectionStatus` usages (e.g., the OBS widget's `{ label: \"OBS\", healthy: obsState.connected }`) must be migrated to the new `status` field. The OBS widget's connection list expands from one entry (\"OBS\") to three (\"OBS\", \"Relay\", \"Stream\").\n\nSee `docs/architecture-decisions/001-multi-platform-streaming.md` for the architectural decision record on the hybrid relay approach.\n\n---\n\n## Glossary\n\n- **Platform**: A streaming destination service (e.g., YouTube, Facebook). Each platform has its own API integration, OAuth credentials, and RTMP ingest URL.\n- **PlatformConfig**: The stored configuration for a streaming platform, including OAuth tokens (encrypted), platform-specific settings, and enabled status. Stored in a new `streaming_platforms` database table.\n- **Broadcast**: A platform-specific live video object created via the platform's API before streaming begins. YouTube calls this a `liveBroadcast` + `liveStream`; Facebook calls it a `LiveVideo`. The backend abstracts both behind a common interface.\n- **RTMP Relay**: A local `node-media-server` instance that accepts OBS's RTMP stream and makes it available for per-destination FFmpeg forwarding processes. Starts on backend startup and runs for the lifetime of the backend process.\n- **Relay Forwarder**: An individual FFmpeg child process that reads from the local RTMP relay and forwards the stream (via `-c copy`, no re-encoding) to a single platform's RTMP ingest URL.\n- **MetadataTemplate**: A named, admin-configured format string used to generate stream titles or descriptions. Contains placeholder tokens (e.g., `{Speaker}`, `{Title}`, `{Scripture}`, `{verseText}`) that are interpolated with SessionManifest values at stream start time.\n- **TemplateCategory**: Either `title` or `description`. Title templates and description templates are independent — a user selects one of each (description may be \"None\").\n- **ManageStreamsModal**: The modal UI that replaces the simple Start/Stop Stream buttons, allowing per-platform stream control during a live session.\n- **AdminIndexPage**: The landing page for ADMIN users at `/admin`, listing links to all admin management sections and the dashboard chooser.\n- **No Source**: A platform status indicating that OBS has disconnected from the RTMP relay while FFmpeg forwarders were active. The platform broadcast may still be alive on the platform side, but no video data is being delivered. Transitions to \"Recovering\" when OBS reconnects.\n- **Recovering**: A platform status indicating that OBS has reconnected to the relay and the backend is verifying via the platform's API that the broadcast is still active. Transitions to \"Streaming\" on success or \"Error\" if the broadcast has ended.\n\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n### Requirement 1: Streaming Platform Configuration\n\n**User Story:** As an administrator, I want to configure streaming platform connections (YouTube, Facebook) through the admin UI, so that the system can create broadcasts and stream to those platforms without manual setup each time.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL store streaming platform configurations in a `streaming_platforms` database table with fields: `id`, `platformType` (e.g., `\"youtube\"`, `\"facebook\"`), `label`, `enabled`, `encryptedAccessToken`, `encryptedRefreshToken`, `tokenExpiresAt`, `platformMetadata` (JSON string for platform-specific data such as YouTube channel ID or Facebook page ID), and `createdAt`. THE `platformType` field SHALL have a unique constraint — only one configuration per platform type is allowed.\n2. THE Backend SHALL encrypt OAuth tokens at rest using the same AES-256-GCM pattern and `DEVICE_SECRET_KEY` used for device connection passwords.\n3. THE Backend SHALL expose REST endpoints for reading, updating, enabling/disabling, and deleting streaming platform configurations; all endpoints SHALL require the ADMIN role.\n4. THE Frontend SHALL provide a unified streaming platform management page at `/admin/platforms` using a two-panel layout (list + detail) matching the Device Management pattern. The left panel lists configured platforms with their connected account name (truncated with ellipsis); the right panel shows platform-specific settings. Platform-specific detail components SHALL be separate files for modularity.\n5. THE admin page SHALL include an \"Add Connection\" button with a dropdown offering: YouTube, Facebook Page, and Facebook Profile. Selecting an option initiates the OAuth 2.0 authorization flow for that platform with the appropriate scopes. FOR Facebook Profile, only `publish_video` is requested (no Page selection screen). FOR Facebook Page, `publish_video`, `pages_manage_posts`, and `pages_read_engagement` are requested. OAuth setup MUST be performed from a browser on the machine running the backend, because the OAuth callback URL uses `localhost` (Google and Facebook reject non-public domains like `invisible.av`). If a public domain is configured, OAuth can be performed from any device. This is a one-time admin task documented in `docs/setup.md`.\n6. WHEN a platform is connected, THE admin page detail panel SHALL display the connected account name (YouTube channel name, Facebook page name, or Facebook profile name) and a \"Disconnect\" button. FOR Facebook Page connections, after OAuth, THE Backend SHALL fetch the list of Pages the admin manages; if multiple Pages exist, THE admin page SHALL display a Page selector dropdown. IF the admin manages only one Page, it SHALL be auto-selected. FOR Facebook Profile connections, the user's profile is used directly (no Page selection needed). The `targetType` (`\"page\"` or `\"user\"`) and associated ID SHALL be stored in `platformMetadata`.\n7. THE Backend SHALL validate stored OAuth tokens on startup by making a lightweight API call to each enabled platform; IF a token is invalid or expired, THE Backend SHALL attempt to refresh it (YouTube only — Facebook Page tokens are long-lived). IF refresh fails, THE Backend SHALL emit a Banner-level notification: \"{Platform} authorization expired — an admin needs to reconnect.\" FOR Facebook Page connections, THE Backend SHALL additionally validate that the stored Page ID is still accessible; IF the Page is inaccessible, THE Backend SHALL emit a Banner-level notification: \"Facebook Page '{Page Name}' is no longer accessible — an admin needs to reconnect.\"\n8. THE Backend SHALL expose OAuth callback endpoints (`GET /api/auth/callback/youtube` and `GET /api/auth/callback/facebook`) that receive the authorization code from the platform, exchange it for access and refresh tokens, encrypt and store the tokens in the `streaming_platforms` table, and redirect back to the admin platforms page with a success or failure query parameter. AFTER storing tokens, THE Backend SHALL call `reloadPlatforms()` on the `StreamingPlatformService` so the frontend receives updated platform readiness without a server restart.\n9. FOR YouTube, THE admin page detail panel SHALL include a \"Default Privacy\" setting with options: `public`, `unlisted` (default), and `private`. This value SHALL be stored in `platformMetadata` and used when creating broadcasts (Req 6.4). FOR Facebook Profile connections, THE admin page SHALL include a \"Default Privacy\" setting with options: `Public` (EVERYONE), `Friends` (ALL_FRIENDS), and `Only Me` (SELF, default). FOR Facebook Page connections, privacy is displayed as read-only \"Public (Pages are always public)\".\n10. THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL display the privacy setting alongside the platform name for any platform that has privacy configured (e.g., \"YouTube (Unlisted)\", \"Facebook (Only Me)\"). FOR AvVolunteer users, this is display-only. FOR ADMIN and AvPowerUser users, THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL allow privacy override per-broadcast (not persisted to admin configuration).\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 2: OAuth Token Lifecycle and Prerequisites\n\n**User Story:** As a system operator, I want OAuth tokens to refresh automatically without any manual intervention, so that streaming works reliably every week without an admin needing to re-authorize before each service.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. FOR YouTube, THE Backend SHALL store the OAuth 2.0 refresh token and use it to silently obtain new access tokens when the current access token expires (typically 1 hour); this refresh SHALL require no user interaction.\n2. FOR Facebook, THE Backend SHALL obtain a long-lived Page access token during the initial OAuth flow; this token does not expire under normal conditions and requires no refresh cycle.\n3. WHEN a token refresh fails (e.g., user revoked access, Google Cloud project suspended), THE Backend SHALL mark the platform as unhealthy, emit a Banner-level notification identifying the affected platform, and exclude that platform from the stream start flow until an admin reconnects.\n4. THE Backend SHALL attempt token refresh proactively (before expiry) rather than waiting for an API call to fail; for YouTube, THE Backend SHALL refresh the access token when it is within 5 minutes of expiry.\n5. THE Backend SHALL NOT store plaintext tokens in logs, error messages, or API responses.\n6. THE Backend SHALL require the following environment variables for OAuth: `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID`, `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `FACEBOOK_APP_ID`, `FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET`. IF any are missing at startup and the corresponding platform is enabled, THE Backend SHALL log a clear error identifying the missing variable(s). These values come from the Google Cloud Console and Facebook Developer portal respectively.\n7. `docs/setup.md` SHALL document the external prerequisites for each platform: (a) YouTube: create a Google Cloud project, enable the YouTube Data API v3, create OAuth 2.0 credentials (Web application type), leave Authorized JavaScript Origins blank (server-side flow), and configure the authorized redirect URI to `https://localhost/api/auth/callback/youtube`. (b) Facebook: create a Facebook App, add the Facebook Login and Live Video API products, and configure the Valid OAuth Redirect URI to `https://localhost/api/auth/callback/facebook`. `docs/setup.md` SHALL note that OAuth connection must be performed from a browser on the backend machine itself (localhost), because Google and Facebook reject non-public domains like `invisible.av`. This is a one-time setup step; after tokens are stored, all other admin and volunteer operations work from any device on the network via `invisible.av`. If a public domain is available, it can be used instead of `localhost` by updating the redirect URIs in the respective developer consoles and setting `APP_URL` in `.env`.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 3: Named Metadata Templates\n\n**User Story:** As an administrator, I want to create multiple named title and description templates, so that volunteers can choose the appropriate format for different types of services (e.g., with or without a scripture reference).\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL store metadata templates in a `metadata_templates` database table with fields: `id`, `name` (admin-provided display name, e.g., \"Speaker and Title\"), `category` (`\"title\"` or `\"description\"`), `formatString` (the template with placeholder tokens), `roleMinimum` (`\"AvVolunteer\"` | `\"AvPowerUser\"` | `\"ADMIN\"` — the minimum role required to see this template; follows the same hierarchy as all other RBAC in the system), and `createdAt`.\n2. THE Backend SHALL support the following placeholder tokens in templates: `{Date}`, `{Speaker}`, `{Title}`, `{Scripture}`, `{verseText}`. `{Date}` is always today's ISO 8601 date. `{Scripture}` resolves to the formatted reference (e.g., \"John 3:16-17\"). `{verseText}` resolves to the full KJV text of the referenced verse(s), formatted per Requirement 9.\n3. WHEN formatting the `{Scripture}` token, IF the stored scripture reference starts at verse 0, THE Backend SHALL display the range starting at verse 1 (e.g., a stored range of Psalm 23:0-2 displays as `Psalm 23:1-2`). IF the stored reference is a single verse 0 with no verseEnd, THE Backend SHALL display `Psalm 23` (chapter only, no verse number).\n4. THE Backend SHALL expose REST endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting metadata templates; all endpoints SHALL require the ADMIN role.\n5. THE Frontend SHALL provide a template management page at `/admin/templates` accessible only to ADMIN users. The page SHALL display two side-by-side lists (fixed height, independently scrollable): \"Title Templates\" on the left and \"Description Templates\" on the right. Each list item SHALL show the template's display name, its `roleMinimum` as a muted badge (e.g., \"AvVolunteer\"), and Edit and Delete buttons. The \"None\" description template SHALL appear in the description list without Edit or Delete buttons (system-managed, no role badge displayed). Each list SHALL have a \"Create\" button for adding new templates.\n6. DELETING a template SHALL require a ConfirmationModal showing the template's display name and full format string before proceeding.\n7. CREATING or EDITING a template SHALL open a modal containing: a Name field (text input), a Role Minimum dropdown (`AvVolunteer` / `AvPowerUser` / `ADMIN`), and a Format String field. The format string field SHALL be a single-line input for title templates and a multi-line textarea for description templates.\n8. THE template create/edit modal SHALL use a two-step validate-then-save flow: (a) the modal initially shows a \"Validate\" button (not \"Save\"), (b) tapping \"Validate\" runs validation checks, (c) if no blocking errors exist the button changes to \"Save\", (d) any edit to the Name, Format String, or Role Minimum fields (input event with actual data change) reverts the button back to \"Validate\".\n9. VALIDATION SHALL check: (a) unknown placeholder tokens in the format string — BLOCKER; (b) duplicate format string (case-sensitive comparison with all whitespace runs — spaces, tabs, newlines — collapsed to a single space and leading/trailing whitespace trimmed, against all other templates in the same category, excluding self when editing) — BLOCKER, message: \"Duplicate of {existingTemplateName}\"; (c) non-unique name within the same category — BLOCKER; (d) if `roleMinimum` is `AvVolunteer` and another template in the same category already has `roleMinimum: AvVolunteer` — WARNING (amber), message: \"Volunteers will see multiple {title/description} templates and must choose between them.\" Blockers are shown as red errors; warnings are shown as amber. The \"Save\" button SHALL NOT appear while any blocker exists.\n10. IF a template contains `{verseText}` or `{Scripture}` and the SessionManifest has no scripture reference, THE Backend SHALL substitute `[No Scripture]` for `{Scripture}` and `[No Verse Text]` for `{verseText}`.\n11. AT LEAST one title template SHALL exist in the system; THE Backend SHALL reject deletion of the last remaining title template.\n12. ON first startup, IF the `metadata_templates` table is empty, THE Backend SHALL auto-create a default title template with name `\"Speaker and Title\"`, category `\"title\"`, `roleMinimum: \"AvVolunteer\"`, and formatString `\"{Date} – {Speaker} – {Title}\"`. This follows the same bootstrap pattern as the admin user auto-creation.\n13. THE system SHALL represent \"None\" (no description template) as a built-in template with category `\"description\"`, name `\"None\"`, `roleMinimum: \"AvVolunteer\"`, and an empty formatString (`\"\"`). This template is auto-created during the seed step alongside the default title template. Using an empty-string template instead of a null `descriptionTemplateId` eliminates null checks throughout the interpolation and persistence paths. The \"None\" template SHALL NOT be deletable or editable by admins — it is system-managed.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 4: Template Selection and Unified Field Collection\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want to select a title template and an optional description template before entering metadata, so that I only see the input fields that are actually needed for my chosen templates.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Frontend SHALL present two dropdowns (side-by-side on wide viewports, stacked on narrow viewports) for template selection in the SessionManifestModal: one labeled \"Title Format\" for title templates and one labeled \"Description Format\" for description templates. Both dropdowns SHALL always be visible regardless of how many options exist. THE Frontend SHALL fetch the list of available templates via REST (`GET /api/templates`) when the SessionManifestModal opens (not pushed via Socket.io); the backend filters by the authenticated user's role derived from the JWT. If an admin modifies templates while the modal is open, the volunteer sees the previous list until the modal is closed and reopened. THE Frontend SHALL filter templates by the authenticated user's role — a user sees only templates with `roleMinimum` at or below their role in the hierarchy (ADMIN > AvPowerUser > AvVolunteer). The description dropdown SHALL always include the \"None\" option. Auto-select logic: IF exactly one non-\"None\" title template is visible to the user, THE Frontend SHALL auto-select it. IF exactly one non-\"None\" description template is visible to the user, THE Frontend SHALL auto-select it (not \"None\"). IF zero non-\"None\" description templates are visible, THE Frontend SHALL auto-select \"None\". IF two or more non-\"None\" templates are visible in either category, THE Frontend SHALL leave that dropdown unselected.\n2. UNTIL both dropdowns have a selection (title is required; description may be \"None\" which is itself a valid selection), THE Frontend SHALL NOT display metadata input fields; instead, THE Frontend SHALL display a message in muted text: \"Select title and description formats above to continue\".\n3. AFTER both templates are selected, THE Frontend SHALL compute the union of all unique placeholder tokens across both selected templates and present one input field per unique token. If both the title and description templates reference `{Title}`, the user sees one Title input — not two.\n4. `{Scripture}` and `{verseText}` SHALL share a single scripture reference input. If either token appears in any selected template, the scripture reference picker SHALL be shown exactly once.\n5. `{Date}` SHALL NOT produce an input field — it is always auto-populated by the backend.\n6. WHEN the user switches between templates, THE Frontend SHALL preserve all previously entered field values. Switching from a template that uses `{Scripture}` to one that does not SHALL NOT clear the scripture reference — it remains available if the user switches back.\n7. THE Frontend SHALL disable the Save button until all required fields for the selected templates have values. A field is required if its corresponding token appears in either selected template (excluding `{Date}`).\n8. THE selected template IDs (`titleTemplateId` and `descriptionTemplateId`) SHALL be included in the SessionManifest and persisted to the backend alongside other manifest fields. This ensures template selections survive page refreshes and are visible to all connected clients.\n9. THE Frontend SHALL store the most recently used template IDs in localStorage (keyed per device, not per user). WHEN the SessionManifestModal opens and no templates are selected in the current SessionManifest, THE Frontend SHALL pre-select the last-used templates from localStorage. This eliminates the template selection step for repeat use on the same device.\n10. THE `BUS_SESSION_MANIFEST_UPDATED` event payload SHALL be expanded to include `interpolatedDescription` and `manifestReady` alongside the existing `interpolatedStreamTitle`. When the description template is \"None\" (empty formatString), `interpolatedDescription` SHALL be an empty string. `manifestReady` SHALL be `true` when a title template is selected and all tokens referenced by the selected templates (excluding `{Date}`) have non-empty values in the manifest; `false` otherwise. Both interpolated values and `manifestReady` are pre-computed by the backend so all subscribers and the frontend read the same result.\n11. THE OBS Widget metadata preview row SHALL display the interpolated title (existing behavior) and, when a description template other than \"None\" is selected, a truncated single-line preview of the interpolated description below it. Tapping the description preview SHALL open an Ionic popover showing the full multi-line description with line breaks preserved. This uses the same popover pattern already established for the title preview (tap-to-expand). The description preview row SHALL display \"No description\" in muted text when the \"None\" template is selected.\n12. THE stream start confirmation modal (Req 6.7) SHALL show both the interpolated title (in the existing visually distinct block) and the interpolated description (if not empty) below it, so the volunteer can verify all metadata before going live. The description in the confirmation modal SHALL show the full text with line breaks preserved (no truncation), since this is the last verification step.\n13. IF a selected template ID in the SessionManifest or localStorage cache references a template that no longer exists or that is not visible to the current user's role (e.g., admin deleted it, or changed its `roleMinimum` above the user's role), THE Frontend SHALL clear that selection and show the template dropdown in its unselected state. THE Backend SHALL treat a missing template ID as if no template is selected and substitute placeholders in the interpolated output.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 5: RTMP Relay Infrastructure\n\n**User Story:** As a system architect, I want a local RTMP relay that accepts OBS's stream and fans it out to multiple destinations independently, so that one platform's failure does not affect others.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL start a `node-media-server` instance as the local RTMP relay on backend startup, listening on a configurable port (default: `1935`, configurable via `RELAY_PORT` environment variable). The relay runs for the lifetime of the backend process — it is not started/stopped per streaming session.\n2. THE relay SHALL accept exactly one inbound RTMP stream from OBS at the path `/live/stream`.\n3. THE Backend SHALL spawn one FFmpeg child process per active streaming destination; each process SHALL read from the local relay and forward to the platform's RTMP ingest URL using `-c copy` (no re-encoding).\n4. WHEN a single FFmpeg forwarder process exits unexpectedly, THE Backend SHALL NOT terminate other active forwarders; THE Backend SHALL capture the FFmpeg process's stderr output, log it, and immediately attempt auto-recovery: (a) emit a Banner-level notification: \"{Platform} stream interrupted — attempting to reconnect…\", (b) wait 2 seconds, then respawn the FFmpeg process with the same RTMP ingest URL, (c) after the new process has been alive for 5 seconds, poll the platform's API to verify the broadcast is still active and accepting data — if the API confirms the broadcast is active, consider recovery successful and auto-clear the Banner; if the API reports the broadcast has ended, treat recovery as failed and transition to step (e), (d) if the new process exits before the 5-second verification window, retry with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s) up to 3 retries or 45 seconds total (whichever comes first), (e) if all retries are exhausted or the API reports the broadcast has ended, transition the platform status to \"Error\", update the Banner to a permanent message: \"{Platform} stream failed — tap Start to create a new stream\", and stop retrying. The volunteer can manually restart the platform from the ManageStreamsModal (which creates a new broadcast). The platform broadcast is not explicitly ended by the backend during auto-recovery — YouTube's `enableAutoStop` and Facebook's auto-end will handle cleanup if recovery fails and the volunteer does not manually restart.\n5. THE Backend SHALL configure OBS (via `obs-websocket` `SetStreamServiceSettings`) to stream to `rtmp://localhost:{RELAY_PORT}/live/stream` on OBS connection (not just on stream start), ensuring OBS is always pointed at the relay whenever the system is running. Before starting the OBS stream, THE Backend SHALL read back the current settings via `GetStreamServiceSettings` and verify they point at the relay; IF they have been changed externally (e.g., someone opened OBS and modified the settings), THE Backend SHALL auto-correct them and log a warning.\n6. IF the relay fails to start (e.g., port already in use), THE Backend SHALL log a clear error message identifying the port conflict and SHALL NOT attempt to start platform streams. THE Backend SHALL emit a Banner-level notification: \"RTMP relay failed to start — check server logs.\"\n7. IF the relay crashes during operation, THE Backend SHALL detect the failure and attempt to restart the relay up to 3 times with 5-second delays. IF a restart succeeds, THE Backend SHALL emit a Banner-level notification that auto-clears: \"RTMP relay recovered.\" OBS's built-in reconnect logic will re-establish the connection to the relay once it is back. IF all 3 restart attempts fail, THE Backend SHALL emit a persistent Banner: \"RTMP relay is down — streaming is unavailable. Check server logs.\" and SHALL NOT attempt further restarts until the backend is restarted.\n8. FFmpeg SHALL be a documented prerequisite in `docs/setup.md`; THE Backend SHALL verify FFmpeg is available on the system PATH at startup and log a clear error if it is not found. IF FFmpeg is not found, THE Backend SHALL also emit a persistent Banner-level notification: \"FFmpeg is not installed — streaming is unavailable. Contact an administrator.\"\n9. WHEN the backend process exits (gracefully or via crash), THE relay and all FFmpeg child processes SHALL be cleaned up. The backend SHALL register signal handlers (`SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`) to terminate child processes on shutdown. For crash scenarios, FFmpeg processes are orphaned but will self-terminate when their RTMP input source (the relay) disappears.\n10. WHEN OBS disconnects from the relay while FFmpeg forwarder processes are active (detected via the relay's publisher disconnect event, not via FFmpeg process behavior), THE Backend SHALL immediately transition all active platform statuses to \"No Source\" (distinct from \"Streaming\", \"Error\", or \"Idle\"). THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL display \"No Source — OBS has disconnected. Streams will resume automatically when OBS reconnects.\" for each affected platform with no action button. The volunteer's primary recovery path is the OBS reconnect flow (the existing OBS disconnect Modal from the original spec); the ManageStreamsModal's \"No Source\" state is informational only. FFmpeg forwarder processes SHALL be left running during \"No Source\" (they will stall but not exit immediately); IF an FFmpeg process does exit while in \"No Source\" state, THE Backend SHALL NOT trigger the auto-recovery logic from Req 5.4 — recovery is deferred until OBS reconnects. WHEN OBS reconnects to the relay and data resumes, THE Backend SHALL transition each platform from \"No Source\" to \"Recovering\" and poll the platform's API to verify the broadcast is still active. IF the API confirms the broadcast is active, THE Backend SHALL transition the platform to \"Streaming\" and auto-clear any related Banner. IF the API reports the broadcast has ended (e.g., YouTube's `enableAutoStop` fired during the gap), THE Backend SHALL transition the platform to \"Error\" with message \"{Platform} broadcast ended during disconnect — tap Start to create a new stream.\"\n11. THE OBS Widget's `WidgetContainer` SHALL display a \"Relay\" connection status indicator alongside the existing \"OBS\" indicator. The relay indicator SHALL use a four-state model: (a) green solid dot (`healthy`) — relay is running and OBS is connected to it; popover text: \"Relay: Healthy\", (b) grey solid dot (`inactive`) — relay is running but OBS is not connected to it (normal pre-stream state); popover text: \"Relay: Waiting for OBS\", (c) red blinking dot (`unhealthy`) — relay has failed to start or has crashed and recovery failed; popover text: \"Relay: Failed\", (d) grey solid dot (`inactive`) — no streaming platforms are configured or enabled (relay is running but unused); popover text: \"Relay: No platforms configured\". The grey dot SHALL use `color-text-muted` (`#A0A0A0`) which has a verified ~5.3:1 contrast ratio against `color-bg`. WHEN the relay is in the `unhealthy` state, THE \"Manage Streams\" button SHALL be disabled with sub-label \"Streaming unavailable\".\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 6: Multi-Platform Stream Start Flow\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want to select which platforms to stream to when starting a stream, so that I can broadcast to YouTube and Facebook simultaneously with a single action.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. WHEN the user taps \"Manage Streams\" (replacing the previous \"Start Stream\" button), THE Frontend SHALL open the ManageStreamsModal. The \"Manage Streams\" button coexists alongside the existing Start/Stop Recording button in the OBS widget.\n2. IF no platforms are configured and enabled, THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL display a message: \"No streaming platforms configured. Contact an administrator.\"\n3. THE ManageStreamsModal SHALL list all configured and enabled platforms with their current status (Idle, Starting, Streaming, Stopping, No Source, Recovering, Error) and available actions. WHILE a platform is in \"Starting\" status, THE modal SHALL display a step-level progress indicator for that platform (e.g., \"Creating broadcast…\", \"Connecting…\", \"Waiting for platform…\") so the volunteer knows the system is working and not frozen. WHILE a platform is in \"Recovering\" status, THE modal SHALL display a spinner with \"Verifying stream…\"\n4. WHEN the user initiates \"Start All\" or starts an individual platform, THE Backend SHALL read the current manifest and interpolated strings from its own `SessionManifestService` (the frontend does not send manifest data with start commands — the backend is the authority) and execute the following sequence per platform in parallel (all platforms start simultaneously; each platform's sequence is independent): (a) create the broadcast via the platform's API with the interpolated title and description (for YouTube, set `contentDetails.enableAutoStart: true` and `contentDetails.enableAutoStop: true`), (b) obtain the RTMP ingest URL, (c) ensure OBS is streaming to the relay (configure OBS stream settings and start OBS stream if not already streaming) — this step is a shared prerequisite: it executes once regardless of how many platforms are starting, and all platform sequences wait for it to complete before proceeding to step (d), (d) spawn an FFmpeg forwarder process for that platform. `enableAutoStart` lets YouTube auto-transition to live when it detects incoming data, eliminating the fragile manual transition polling. `enableAutoStop` lets YouTube auto-end the broadcast ~1 minute after data stops, serving as a safety net if the explicit end-broadcast API call (Req 7.4) fails. The tradeoff: crash recovery always creates a new broadcast rather than reconnecting to the existing one, because `enableAutoStop` ends the broadcast before a volunteer would realistically notice and respond. This is acceptable — the volunteer experience is the same either way (tap \"Start Stream\" in the ManageStreamsModal).\n5. IF a platform broadcast creation fails, THE Backend SHALL skip that platform, continue with remaining platforms, and emit a Banner-level notification identifying the failed platform and the reason.\n6. THE \"Start All\" button SHALL be disabled (greyed out) when all configured platforms are already streaming or when a start sequence is already in progress.\n7. BEFORE starting any platform stream, THE Frontend SHALL display a ConfirmationModal: \"Start streaming to {platform list}?\" with confirm label \"Go Live\" and cancel label \"Cancel\". The platform list SHALL use each platform's `label` field from `streaming_platforms`, formatted as \"{label}\" for one platform and \"{label1} and {label2}\" for two.\n8. THE \"Manage Streams\" button SHALL be disabled unless the SessionManifest contains at least the fields required by the selected templates; THE button sub-label SHALL follow the priority order defined in Req 12.4.\n9. IF any step in the platform start sequence does not complete within 30 seconds, THE Backend SHALL transition that platform's status to \"Error\" with a descriptive timeout message and continue with remaining platforms."
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
