                    "Text": "# Requirements Document — Video Control and Preview\n\n## Introduction\n\nThis spec extends Invisible A/V Booth with real-time video preview and camera control capabilities. It introduces two major features: (1) a live OBS stream preview widget that allows volunteers to see exactly what is being broadcast, and (2) an NDI/VISCA camera control system with live preview, PTZ controls, AI tracking toggles, and preset management.\n\nThis spec depends on the foundational platform delivered by the `livestream-control-system` spec (authentication, dashboard, widget grid, event bus, notification system) and the `multi-platform-streaming` spec (RTMP relay, OBS streaming state, `ConnectionStatus` model). It adds two new widgets to the dashboard grid and introduces a new Camera Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) on the backend.\n\nVideo preview streams are delivered via dedicated WebSocket connections (separate from the command/event Socket.io connection) using fragmented MP4 (fMP4) with MediaSource Extensions (MSE) in the browser. This achieves sub-500ms latency on a LAN, which is critical for camera PTZ control where delays cause operator overshoot. The server uses FFmpeg for transcoding/remuxing; hardware-accelerated encoding (VA-API, QSV, NVENC) is auto-detected at startup and used when available. Preview resolution defaults to 720p (configurable via code constant) since dashboard widgets render at far smaller dimensions — sending 1080p would waste bandwidth and CPU for no visual benefit.\n\nNo FFmpeg transcoding process is spawned unless at least one client is subscribed to that stream. Processes are torn down after the last subscriber disconnects (with a short grace period to avoid thrashing on page refresh).\n\n---\n\n## Glossary\n\n- **fMP4 (Fragmented MP4)**: A variant of the MP4 container format that splits the media into small independently-decodable fragments, enabling low-latency streaming via progressive download or WebSocket delivery.\n- **MSE (MediaSource Extensions)**: A browser API that allows JavaScript to feed media segments to a `<video>` element for playback, enabling custom streaming protocols without browser plugin support.\n- **Preview Stream**: A real-time video (and optionally audio) feed delivered from the backend to the dashboard for monitoring purposes. Not the same as the broadcast stream sent to platforms.\n- **NDI (Network Device Interface)**: A royalty-free IP video protocol by Vizrt for high-quality, low-latency video transport over LAN. Used for both receiving camera video feeds and sending PTZ control commands.\n- **VISCA (Video System Control Architecture)**: A serial/IP camera control protocol originally by Sony, now an industry standard for PTZ camera control. Supports absolute/relative positioning, speed control, preset store/recall, and position inquiry.\n- **PTZ (Pan/Tilt/Zoom)**: The three mechanical axes of camera movement. Pan is horizontal rotation, tilt is vertical rotation, zoom is optical magnification.\n- **Camera HAL (Hardware Abstraction Layer)**: The backend service that normalizes NDI and VISCA protocol differences behind a common interface, so widgets and presets operate protocol-agnostically.\n- **Dead-Man's Switch**: A safety mechanism where continuous PTZ movement requires periodic keepalive signals from the client. If keepalives stop (e.g., network drop), the backend automatically issues a stop command to prevent runaway camera movement. The timeout is tuned for WiFi tablet use (not wired assumptions).\n- **Virtual Joystick**: A circular touch zone for pan/tilt control where distance from center determines speed and angle determines direction. More natural for touch interfaces than discrete D-pad buttons, supports diagonal movement inherently, and provides proportional speed control.\n- **Adaptive Speed**: PTZ movement speed that automatically scales inversely with zoom level — slower when zoomed in (fine control), faster when zoomed out (coarse re-framing).\n- **Preview WebSocket**: A dedicated WebSocket endpoint (separate from the Socket.io command connection) used exclusively for binary video stream delivery. One endpoint per source (OBS, each camera).\n- **Fan-Out**: The server pattern of running a single FFmpeg transcode per source and distributing the output to all subscribed WebSocket clients, avoiding redundant transcoding.\n- **Hardware Encoder Probe**: A one-time startup check that queries FFmpeg for available hardware-accelerated encoders (VA-API, QSV, NVENC) and caches the result for the lifetime of the process.\n\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n### Requirement 1: Video Preview Infrastructure\n\n**User Story:** As a system architect, I want a shared infrastructure for delivering real-time video previews to dashboard widgets, so that both OBS and camera previews use the same efficient delivery mechanism without duplicating transcoding logic.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL expose dedicated WebSocket endpoints for video preview streams, separate from the Socket.io command connection. Each video source (OBS relay, each camera) SHALL have its own WebSocket endpoint path (e.g., `/preview/obs`, `/preview/camera/{cameraId}`).\n2. THE Backend SHALL transcode/remux source video into fragmented MP4 format using FFmpeg, with flags `-movflags frag_keyframe+empty_moov+default_base_moof` to enable immediate playback without requiring the full file header.\n3. THE Backend SHALL define a code constant `PREVIEW_RESOLUTION` defaulting to `{ width: 1280, height: 720 }`. FFmpeg SHALL scale the source to this resolution for all preview streams. This is configurable by changing the constant — no runtime UI is provided.\n4. THE Backend SHALL probe FFmpeg's available encoders at startup (once, cached for process lifetime) by executing `ffmpeg -encoders`. IF a hardware encoder is detected (in priority order: `h264_vaapi`, `h264_qsv`, `h264_nvenc`), THE Backend SHALL use it for all preview transcoding. IF no hardware encoder is available, THE Backend SHALL fall back to `libx264` with `-preset ultrafast`.\n5. THE Backend SHALL log at INFO level which encoder was selected at startup (e.g., \"Video preview using hardware encoder: h264_vaapi\" or \"Video preview using software encoder: libx264 ultrafast\").\n6. THE Backend SHALL NOT spawn an FFmpeg process for a preview source until at least one WebSocket client connects to that source's endpoint. WHEN the last WebSocket client disconnects, THE Backend SHALL wait a grace period of 3 seconds before terminating the FFmpeg process. IF a new client connects within the grace period, the existing process continues without interruption.\n7. THE Backend SHALL fan out the FFmpeg output to all connected WebSocket clients for that source. A single FFmpeg process per source serves all subscribers — multiple clients watching the same preview do NOT spawn multiple transcoding processes.\n8. THE Frontend SHALL use the `MediaSource` API (MSE) to receive fMP4 chunks over WebSocket and feed them to a `<video>` element for playback. THE Frontend SHALL handle `MediaSource` buffer management: segments older than 2 seconds SHALL be removed from the SourceBuffer to prevent memory growth and keep preview latency under 500ms. If the buffer grows beyond 3 seconds (e.g., due to a processing stall), THE Frontend SHALL seek the video element to the live edge to prevent stale frames from accumulating. This is critical for tap-to-center accuracy — the volunteer must see the camera's current position, not where it was seconds ago.\n9. WHEN an FFmpeg preview process exits unexpectedly, THE Backend SHALL attempt to restart it after a 2-second delay if subscribers are still connected. IF the process fails to start 3 consecutive times, THE Backend SHALL close all subscriber WebSocket connections with a descriptive close reason and stop retrying until a new client connects.\n10. THE Backend SHALL verify FFmpeg is available on the system PATH at startup (shared check with the multi-platform-streaming spec's relay requirement). IF FFmpeg is not found, preview functionality SHALL be unavailable and widgets SHALL display an appropriate error state.\n11. WHEN the backend process exits (gracefully via SIGTERM/SIGINT or crash), all FFmpeg preview processes SHALL be terminated. Signal handlers SHALL ensure child process cleanup on graceful shutdown.\n12. THE Preview WebSocket endpoints SHALL require authentication. The client SHALL include the JWT token as a query parameter (`?token=...`) when establishing the WebSocket connection. THE Backend SHALL validate the token before accepting the connection. Invalid or expired tokens SHALL result in immediate connection closure with code 4401.\n13. THE Backend SHALL verify the NDI SDK is available at startup by attempting to dynamically import the `grandiose` native module (via `import()` with try/catch — NOT a static import or hard dependency in `package.json`). This ensures `npm install` succeeds on machines without C++ build tools or the NDI SDK. IF the module fails to load, THE Backend SHALL log a clear ERROR message: \"NDI SDK not available — camera video preview and NDI PTZ control are disabled. Install the NDI SDK to enable camera features.\" THE Backend SHALL emit a persistent Banner-level notification with the same message. Camera features that depend on NDI (video preview, NDI PTZ control) SHALL be unavailable. VISCA-only camera control (no video preview) SHALL remain functional. The rest of the system (OBS, streaming, lower thirds) SHALL be unaffected. This follows the same graceful degradation pattern as missing FFmpeg.\n14. THE Backend SHALL enforce a maximum of `MAX_PREVIEW_STREAMS` (code constant, default: 4) simultaneous FFmpeg preview processes. WHEN the limit is reached and a new preview connection is requested, THE Backend SHALL close the WebSocket with code 4503 and reason \"Server busy — too many active previews.\" Preview FFmpeg processes SHALL run at lower OS scheduling priority than streaming FFmpeg forwarders (the live stream must never be starved by preview transcoding).\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 2: OBS Stream Preview Widget\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want to see and hear what OBS is currently streaming directly on my dashboard, so that I can immediately confirm that changes I make (lower thirds, scene switches) are reflected in the live output.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Frontend SHALL render an \"OBS Preview\" widget on the dashboard that displays a live video feed of the OBS output. The widget SHALL be registered with widgetId `\"obs-preview\"` and seeded at 2×2 in the dashboard grid.\n2. THE widget SHALL connect to the preview WebSocket endpoint `/preview/obs` when mounted and disconnect when unmounted. Connection establishment SHALL follow the authentication pattern defined in Req 1.12.\n3. THE widget's `WidgetContainer` SHALL display a single connection status indicator labeled \"Feed\" with the following states: (a) green solid dot (`healthy`) — receiving video frames from the preview WebSocket, (b) grey solid dot (`inactive`) — no active stream or recording in OBS (no feed available), (c) red blinking dot (`unhealthy`) — OBS is streaming/recording but the preview WebSocket connection has failed or frames have stopped arriving for more than 3 seconds.\n4. WHEN OBS is neither streaming nor recording, THE widget SHALL display a centered message \"No Active Stream or Recording\" on a dark background. THE widget SHALL NOT attempt to connect to the preview WebSocket in this state.\n5. WHEN OBS is streaming or recording (or both), THE Backend SHALL make the OBS preview stream available. THE Backend SHALL source the preview from the RTMP relay's output (same source used for platform forwarding). IF OBS is only recording (not streaming to the relay), THE Backend SHALL source the preview from OBS's virtual output or replay buffer via `obs-websocket` media output capabilities; IF this is not available, THE widget SHALL display \"Preview unavailable — start streaming to enable\" in the inactive state.\n6. THE video element SHALL use `object-fit: contain` to preserve the source aspect ratio without stretching. THE video SHALL be centered both horizontally and vertically within the widget's content area. IF the video is portrait (taller than wide relative to the widget), it SHALL be height-constrained with horizontal centering. IF landscape, it SHALL be width-constrained with vertical centering. Black letterbox/pillarbox areas SHALL use the widget's background color (`color-surface`).\n7. THE widget SHALL overlay a mute/unmute button in the bottom-right corner of the video area. The button SHALL be a 48×48px (3rem × 3rem) touch target with a semi-transparent background (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`). The button SHALL display a speaker icon (muted) or speaker-wave icon (unmuted) using Ionicons (`volume-mute` / `volume-high`).\n8. Audio SHALL be muted by default on initial load. WHEN the page is refreshed, audio SHALL reset to muted. The mute state SHALL NOT be persisted across sessions. WHEN the user taps the mute button, audio SHALL toggle between muted and unmuted.\n9. WHEN the user taps anywhere on the video area EXCEPT the mute button, THE Frontend SHALL open a large modal titled \"Stream Preview\". The modal SHALL display the same live video stream at a larger size (filling the modal content area with the same `object-fit: contain` centering behavior). The modal SHALL include the same mute/unmute button (bottom-right, same styling) and a dismiss button. Audio state SHALL be shared between the widget and modal views — unmuting in the modal keeps audio unmuted when the modal is closed.\n10. THE modal SHALL continue receiving the same WebSocket stream (not open a second connection). WHEN the modal is dismissed, playback continues in the widget without interruption or reconnection.\n11. WHEN the preview WebSocket connection is lost while the widget is visible, THE widget SHALL display a brief \"Reconnecting...\" overlay on the video and attempt to reconnect with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, up to 10s max). WHEN reconnection succeeds, playback resumes automatically.\n12. THE widget SHALL NOT consume CPU or network resources when it is not on the active dashboard. WHEN the dashboard containing this widget is navigated away from, the WebSocket connection SHALL be closed.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 3: Camera Hardware Abstraction Layer\n\n**User Story:** As a system architect, I want a protocol-agnostic camera control interface that abstracts NDI and VISCA differences, so that widgets and presets operate identically regardless of which protocol the camera uses.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL define a `CameraControlInterface` that normalizes PTZ operations across NDI and VISCA protocols. The interface SHALL expose the following operations: `panTiltSpeed(panSpeed: number, tiltSpeed: number)` for continuous relative movement (speed range: -1.0 to 1.0, 0.0 = stop), `panTiltAbsolute(pan: number, tilt: number)` for absolute positioning (range: -1.0 to 1.0, 0.0 = center), `zoomAbsolute(zoom: number)` for absolute zoom (range: 0.0 to 1.0, 0.0 = wide, 1.0 = telephoto), `focusAuto()` to enable auto-focus, `focusManual(position: number)` to set manual focus (range: 0.0 to 1.0), `stop()` to halt all movement immediately, and `inquirePosition()` returning `{ pan, tilt, zoom, focus, autoFocus }` (or partial results if the protocol doesn't support inquiry for a given axis).\n2. THE Backend SHALL implement the `CameraControlInterface` for NDI using the NDI SDK's PTZ functions (via `grandiose` or equivalent Node.js native bindings): `NDIlib_recv_ptz_pan_tilt_speed` for continuous movement, `NDIlib_recv_ptz_pan_tilt` for absolute positioning, `NDIlib_recv_ptz_zoom` for zoom, `NDIlib_recv_ptz_auto_focus` and `NDIlib_recv_ptz_focus` for focus control.\n3. THE Backend SHALL implement the `CameraControlInterface` for VISCA over IP using raw TCP/UDP socket communication: `Pan_TiltDrive` with direction and speed bytes for continuous movement, `AbsolutePosition` command for absolute pan/tilt, `CAM_Zoom Direct` for zoom, `CAM_Focus Auto/Manual/Direct` for focus, and inquiry commands (`CAM_PanTiltPosInq`, `CAM_ZoomPosInq`, `CAM_FocusPosInq`, `CAM_FocusAFModeInq`) for position queries.\n4. THE Backend SHALL support per-camera protocol selection configured by the admin during device setup (Req 7). Each camera configuration SHALL specify `controlProtocol: \"ndi\" | \"visca\"` and the necessary connection parameters (NDI source name for NDI; IP address and port for VISCA, defaulting to port 5500).\n5. THE Backend SHALL probe the camera on the selected protocol at connection time to verify the camera responds. FOR NDI, this means checking `NDIlib_recv_ptz_is_supported()` after connecting to the NDI source. FOR VISCA, this means sending a `CAM_PowerInq` command and verifying a valid response. IF the probe fails, THE Backend SHALL mark the camera as unreachable and emit a Banner-level notification: \"Camera '{label}' is not responding on {protocol}. Check connection settings.\"\n6. THE Backend SHALL define a camera feature set as a set of toggleable capabilities: `pan`, `tilt`, `zoom`, `focus`, `ai-tracking`, `ai-tracking-zoom-disable`, `ai-tracking-tilt-disable`. Each camera's enabled features are configured by the admin (Req 7). THE Frontend SHALL hide or disable controls for features that are not enabled on the active camera.\n7. THE Backend SHALL maintain a `CameraService` that manages all configured cameras. The service SHALL: (a) connect to each enabled camera on startup, (b) poll position data at a regular interval (every 2 seconds via VISCA inquiry; for NDI-only cameras, track last-commanded values as authoritative state), (c) broadcast state updates to subscribed frontend clients via Socket.io, (d) handle reconnection with exponential backoff if a camera becomes unreachable.\n8. FOR NDI-only cameras (without VISCA inquiry capability), THE Backend SHALL maintain authoritative position state based on commands issued through the system. THE Backend SHALL log a warning at startup: \"Camera '{label}' uses NDI-only control — position state is based on commanded values and may drift if the camera is controlled externally.\" The admin UI (Req 7) SHALL display this limitation when NDI-only is selected.\n9. WHEN using VISCA position inquiry, THE Backend SHALL handle cameras that do not support specific inquiry commands gracefully. IF an inquiry returns an error or timeout, THE Backend SHALL mark that axis as \"unknown\" in the state and log a DEBUG-level message. The UI SHALL display the last known value (or hide the indicator) for unknown axes.\n10. THE Backend SHALL implement adaptive pan/tilt speed: the effective speed sent to the camera SHALL be scaled inversely with the current zoom level. The formula SHALL be `effectiveSpeed = requestedSpeed * (1.0 - zoomLevel * ADAPTIVE_SPEED_DAMPING)` where `ADAPTIVE_SPEED_DAMPING` is a code constant defaulting to `0.7`. At full wide (zoom 0.0), speed is 100% of requested; at full telephoto (zoom 1.0), speed is 30% of requested. A global cap `MAX_EFFECTIVE_SPEED` (code constant, default: `0.6`) SHALL clamp the final effective speed regardless of zoom level, preventing violent camera whips at wide angles when the joystick is fully deflected. The camera HAL implementation for each protocol is responsible for mapping the normalized float speed (0.0–1.0) to camera-native speed units (e.g., VISCA 1–24 speed steps). Cameras that reject a speed command (NAK) SHALL be retried once at 50% speed; if still rejected, the command is dropped and a DEBUG-level log is emitted.\n11. THE Backend SHALL implement a dead-man's switch for continuous PTZ movement. WHEN a `cts:camera:ptz:move:start` command is received, THE Backend SHALL begin continuous movement and expect `cts:camera:ptz:move:keepalive` events every 200ms from the client. IF no keepalive arrives within 750ms, THE Backend SHALL issue a stop command to the camera. The 750ms timeout (vs. the 200ms send interval) provides a 3.5× safety margin to absorb WiFi micro-dropouts and tablet JS thread jank without false-triggering on a healthy connection. THE Frontend SHALL send `cts:camera:ptz:move:stop` on touch release. This protects against network drops causing runaway camera movement.\n12. THE Backend SHALL expose camera state via Socket.io using the established SocketModule pattern. Events: `stc:camera:state` (position, connection status, features, active preset), `cts:camera:ptz:move:start`, `cts:camera:ptz:move:keepalive`, `cts:camera:ptz:move:stop`, `cts:camera:zoom:set`, `cts:camera:focus:auto`, `cts:camera:focus:set`, `cts:camera:preset:activate`. All event name constants SHALL be defined in `packages/shared/src/constants/socketEvents.ts`. THE `stc:camera:state` payload SHALL include per camera: `{ cameraId, connected, position: { pan, tilt, zoom, focus } | null, autoFocus, aiTracking, disableTilt, disableZoom, activePresetId: string | null, features: string[], presets: CameraPreset[] }`. THE `emitInitialState` handler SHALL send the state for all configured cameras. THE Backend SHALL also include `ndiAvailable: boolean` at the top level so the frontend knows whether NDI features are operational.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 4: NDI Camera Video Preview\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want to see a real-time preview of what the camera sees directly on my dashboard, so that I can frame shots accurately without needing a separate monitor.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Backend SHALL receive the NDI video feed from each configured camera using the NDI SDK (via `grandiose` or equivalent Node.js native bindings) and transcode it to fMP4 for WebSocket delivery using the shared preview infrastructure (Req 1). The NDI source name used for video reception SHALL be the same source configured for PTZ control.\n2. THE Frontend SHALL render a \"Camera\" widget on the dashboard that displays the live camera video feed. The widget SHALL be registered with widgetId `\"camera\"` and support multiple instances (one per configured camera). WHEN multiple cameras are configured, THE widget SHALL include a dropdown selector at the top of the widget allowing the volunteer to switch between cameras. Only one camera feed is active per widget instance at a time. WHEN only one camera is configured, the dropdown SHALL be hidden. WHEN multiple cameras are configured, THE widget SHALL default to the first camera by sort order (alphabetical by label). The selected camera SHALL be persisted in localStorage (keyed by widget instance) so the volunteer returns to the same camera on page refresh.\n3. THE widget's `WidgetContainer` SHALL display a single connection status indicator labeled \"Camera\" with states: (a) green solid dot (`healthy`) — connected to the camera and receiving video frames, (b) grey solid dot (`inactive`) — camera is disabled or not configured, (c) red blinking dot (`unhealthy`) — camera is configured but unreachable or video frames have stopped arriving for more than 3 seconds.\n4. THE widget SHALL use `ResizeObserver` (per the established pattern) to detect its available size. THE widget SHALL operate in two display modes based on size: (a) **Compact mode** — widget shows video preview only, filling the entire content area; tapping the video opens the full control modal. (b) **Expanded mode** — widget shows video preview in a 2×2-cell-equivalent area alongside PTZ controls (defined in Req 5).\n5. THE threshold for switching between compact and expanded mode SHALL be determined by whether the video can fit in a 2×2-cell-equivalent space AND sufficient room remains for all control elements (pan/tilt pad, zoom slider, presets list, toggle buttons) at their minimum touch target sizes.\n6. IN compact mode, THE video element SHALL use `object-fit: contain` with horizontal and vertical centering, identical to the OBS preview widget behavior. The video SHALL expand to fill the widget content area.\n7. IN expanded mode, THE video element SHALL occupy a fixed portion of the widget (left side), using `object-fit: contain` with centering. The remaining space SHALL be used for controls (Req 5).\n8. WHEN the user taps the video in compact mode, THE Frontend SHALL open a large modal titled \"Camera Control\" containing the full-size video preview and all PTZ controls (Req 5). The modal SHALL share the same WebSocket stream (no duplicate connection).\n9. WHEN the camera is unreachable, THE widget SHALL display a centered message \"Camera Offline\" on a dark background in place of the video. WHEN the widget first loads and no frame has been received yet (initial connection in progress), THE widget SHALL display \"Connecting...\" centered on the dark background (`color-surface`). This is the state before any camera has ever connected — distinct from the camera-switch freeze-frame behavior in Req 4.10.\n10. WHEN the user switches cameras via the dropdown selector, THE Frontend SHALL disconnect from the current camera's preview WebSocket and connect to the newly selected camera's endpoint. The transition SHALL display a \"Connecting...\" message centered on the video area while the new stream initializes. THE widget SHALL hold the last frame of the previous camera (frozen) beneath the \"Connecting...\" overlay until the first frame of the new camera arrives, to avoid a jarring black flash.\n11. THE widget SHALL NOT consume bandwidth for cameras that are not currently selected in the dropdown. Only the active camera's video stream is subscribed to.\n12. THE video preview in this widget does NOT include audio. Camera preview is video-only (unlike the OBS preview which includes audio toggle).\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 5: Camera PTZ Controls\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want intuitive pan/tilt/zoom controls for the camera with tap-to-center on the video, so that I can frame shots quickly and accurately during a live service.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE PTZ controls SHALL be visible in the camera widget when in expanded mode (Req 4.4b) and always visible in the full-screen \"Camera Control\" modal. The controls layout SHALL match the following arrangement: video preview on the left; virtual joystick, zoom slider, and toggle buttons on the right; preset list below or beside the zoom slider (space permitting).\n2. THE pan/tilt control SHALL be a virtual joystick — a circular touch zone where the user drags from center to indicate direction and speed. The joystick area SHALL have a minimum diameter of 7.5rem (120px at base) to provide adequate touch area. The distance from center to the edge of the joystick determines speed (0.0 at center to 1.0 at edge). The angle determines direction, naturally supporting diagonal movement. A visible indicator dot SHALL track the user's finger position within the joystick bounds. The joystick SHALL be styled as a circular area with a subtle border (`color-border`) and the indicator dot using `color-primary`. The joystick SHALL respond identically to mouse events (mousedown/mousemove/mouseup) for development and non-touch admin use.\n3. WHEN the user touches and drags within the joystick area, THE Frontend SHALL emit `cts:camera:ptz:move:start` with the calculated pan/tilt speed values (derived from angle and distance) and begin sending `cts:camera:ptz:move:keepalive` every 200ms with updated speed values as the finger moves. WHEN the user lifts their finger, THE Frontend SHALL emit `cts:camera:ptz:move:stop`. Movement is continuous for the duration of the touch — not discrete steps. THE Frontend SHALL apply a dead-zone of 15% of the joystick radius — finger positions within this zone are treated as (0, 0) and do not initiate movement. THE Frontend SHALL quantize speed values to 0.05 increments (rounding to nearest) and only emit a keepalive if the quantized value differs from the last-sent value. This prevents servo jitter from finger tremor. On socket reconnect during an active move session, THE Backend SHALL treat the reconnection as an implicit stop (speed = 0, 0). The client must initiate a fresh `cts:camera:ptz:move:start` to resume movement — stale keepalives from a previous session are ignored.\n4. THE zoom control SHALL be an absolute-position slider oriented vertically (telephoto at top, wide at bottom). The slider SHALL have a minimum height/width of 36px for the track touch target. The slider's current value SHALL reflect the camera's actual zoom position (synced via polling per Req 3.7b). WHEN the user drags the slider, THE Frontend SHALL emit `cts:camera:zoom:set` with the absolute zoom value (0.0 to 1.0).\n5. THE Frontend SHALL display the following toggle buttons, each with a 36px (2.25rem) tall footprint: (a) **AI Tracking** — toggles the camera's AI auto-tracking mode, (b) **Disable Tilt** — when enabled, constrains AI tracking to pan-only (no tilt), (c) **Disable Zoom** — when enabled, constrains AI tracking to exclude zoom adjustments, (d) **Auto Focus** — toggles between auto-focus and manual focus mode. Toggles SHALL use the established Ionic toggle component pattern.\n6. THE Auto Focus toggle and the manual focus control SHALL be visible only to ADMIN and AvPowerUser roles. AvVolunteer users SHALL NOT see focus controls.\n7. WHEN Auto Focus is enabled, THE manual focus control SHALL be greyed out (disabled) and non-interactive. WHEN Auto Focus is disabled, a focus slider (horizontal, 36px tall) SHALL allow manual focus adjustment. THE slider SHALL emit `cts:camera:focus:set` with the absolute focus value (0.0 to 1.0).\n8. WHEN AI Tracking is enabled, THE Disable Tilt and Disable Zoom toggles SHALL become visible. WHEN AI Tracking is disabled, THE Disable Tilt and Disable Zoom toggles SHALL be hidden.\n9. WHEN the controls are visible (expanded mode or modal), THE user SHALL be able to tap on the video preview to command the camera to center on the tapped point. THE Frontend SHALL calculate the tap coordinates as a proportional offset from the center of the video element (range: -1.0 to 1.0 on each axis) and emit a `cts:camera:ptz:tap-to-center` event with the offset values. THE Backend SHALL calculate the target absolute pan/tilt position using: `targetPan = currentPan + (tapOffsetX * horizontalFovFraction)`, `targetTilt = currentTilt + (tapOffsetY * verticalFovFraction)`, where `horizontalFovFraction` and `verticalFovFraction` are derived from the camera's configured field-of-view at the current zoom level. THE Backend SHALL then issue an absolute pan/tilt command to the camera.\n10. THE camera's field-of-view parameters (`fovWideAngle`) SHALL be configured per camera by the admin (Req 7). THE Backend SHALL estimate the effective FOV at the current zoom level using: `effectiveFov = fovWideAngle * (1.0 - zoomLevel)`. This is an approximation — the volunteer can tap again or use the D-pad for fine adjustment.\n11. WHEN Disable Tilt is enabled and the user taps on the video, THE Backend SHALL only adjust the pan axis (horizontal); the tilt value SHALL remain unchanged.\n12. WHEN AI Tracking is enabled and the user taps on the video, THE Frontend SHALL display a Toast notification: \"Tap-to-center is disabled when AI Tracking is active.\" The tap SHALL be ignored (no command sent to the camera).\n13. ALL toggle states (AI Tracking, Disable Tilt, Disable Zoom, Auto Focus) SHALL be maintained by the backend `CameraService` and broadcast to all connected clients. Toggling on one tablet SHALL immediately reflect on all other tablets viewing the same camera.\n14. THE virtual joystick and zoom slider SHALL respect the camera's enabled feature set (Req 3.6). IF `pan` is not in the feature set, horizontal joystick movement SHALL be ignored. IF `tilt` is not in the feature set, vertical joystick movement SHALL be ignored. IF both `pan` and `tilt` are disabled, the joystick SHALL be hidden. IF `zoom` is not in the feature set, the zoom slider SHALL be hidden. IF `focus` is not in the feature set, focus controls SHALL be hidden regardless of role. IF `ai-tracking` is not in the feature set, the AI Tracking toggle and its sub-toggles SHALL be hidden.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 6: Camera Presets\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want to activate saved camera presets with a single tap, so that I can quickly frame standard shots (pulpit, choir, wide) without manually positioning the camera.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE Frontend SHALL display a preset list in the camera controls area (expanded mode and modal). The list SHALL show up to 3 presets visible at a time with vertical scrolling if more presets exist. Each preset row SHALL display the preset name and an \"Activate\" button with a 36px (2.25rem) tall footprint.\n2. WHEN the user taps \"Activate\" on a preset, THE Frontend SHALL emit `cts:camera:preset:activate` with the preset ID. THE button SHALL immediately change to \"Activating...\" and become disabled while the backend executes the preset.\n3. THE Backend SHALL activate a preset by determining the recall strategy based on the preset's `storedOnCamera` flag: (a) IF `storedOnCamera: true`, THE Backend SHALL issue the camera's native preset recall command (VISCA preset recall with speed parameter, or `NDIlib_recv_ptz_recall_preset` with speed). (b) IF `storedOnCamera: false`, THE Backend SHALL issue absolute position commands from the stored database values: a combined `panTiltAbsolute(pan, tilt)` command plus `zoomAbsolute(zoom)`, plus `focusManual(position)` if auto-focus is off and a focus value is stored. These commands execute simultaneously on the camera — no sequential motion risk.\n4. THE Backend SHALL also apply toggle states from the preset: Auto Focus (on/off), AI Tracking (on/off), Disable Tilt (on/off), Disable Zoom (on/off). These are applied via the appropriate camera control commands after the position commands.\n5. WHEN preset activation completes successfully (position commands acknowledged or timeout-based reasonable delay for cameras that don't ACK), THE Backend SHALL broadcast the updated camera state and active preset ID to all clients. THE Frontend SHALL change the button to \"Activated\" (disabled) for the active preset.\n6. IF a preset has been activated AND no manual changes have been made to any PTZ axis or toggle since activation, THE \"Activate\" button for that preset SHALL remain disabled showing \"Activated\". WHEN the user makes any manual change (D-pad movement, zoom slider, toggle, or tap-to-center), THE active preset indicator SHALL clear and all \"Activate\" buttons SHALL return to their enabled state.\n7. THE system SHALL NOT attempt to detect whether the camera's current position matches a preset after server restart. On fresh startup, no preset is marked as active — all buttons show \"Activate\".\n8. IF preset activation fails (camera unreachable, command timeout of 10 seconds, or command error), THE Backend SHALL emit a Toast-level notification: \"Failed to activate preset '{name}' — camera may be unreachable.\" THE button SHALL revert to \"Activate\" (enabled) so the user can retry. The 10-second timeout accommodates mechanical PTZ cameras that may take several seconds to traverse from one extreme to another.\n9. THE Backend SHALL store presets in a `camera_presets` database table with fields: `id`, `cameraId` (foreign key to the camera device), `name`, `sortOrder` (integer for display ordering), `storedOnCamera` (boolean), `cameraPresetSlot` (integer, nullable — the onboard slot number if stored on camera), `pan` (float, nullable), `tilt` (float, nullable), `zoom` (float, nullable), `focus` (float, nullable), `autoFocus` (boolean), `aiTracking` (boolean), `disableTilt` (boolean), `disableZoom` (boolean), and `createdAt`.\n10. NULLABLE position fields (pan, tilt, zoom, focus) indicate that the value could not be captured during preset creation (e.g., camera doesn't support inquiry for that axis). WHEN activating a preset, THE Backend SHALL skip any axis with a null value — the camera retains its current position on that axis.\n11. PRESETS are admin-managed (created/edited/deleted via the admin camera configuration page, Req 7). Volunteers can only activate presets — they cannot create, edit, or delete them.\n12. THE preset list SHALL be ordered by `sortOrder` ascending. If two presets have the same `sortOrder`, they SHALL be sub-sorted by `name` alphabetically.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 7: Camera Admin Configuration\n\n**User Story:** As an administrator, I want to add and configure cameras through the admin UI — including connection settings, feature toggles, and presets — so that volunteers have a ready-to-use camera control experience.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE admin Device Management page (`/admin/devices`) SHALL support a new device type `\"camera\"`. WHEN adding a camera, the admin SHALL provide: label, NDI source name (for video feed and NDI PTZ control), control protocol (`\"ndi\"` | `\"visca\"`), VISCA IP address and port (required if protocol is `\"visca\"`, default port 5500), and wide-angle field of view in degrees (`fovWideAngle`, used for tap-to-center calculations, defaulting to 60°). IF the NDI SDK is not available (Req 1.13), THE admin page SHALL display a warning: \"NDI SDK not installed — only VISCA control is available (no video preview).\" `docs/setup.md` SHALL document NDI SDK installation as a prerequisite for camera video preview and NDI PTZ control.\n2. THE admin device detail panel for cameras SHALL display a \"Features\" section with toggles for each capability: `pan`, `tilt`, `zoom`, `focus`, `ai-tracking`, `ai-tracking-tilt-disable`, `ai-tracking-zoom-disable`. All toggles SHALL default to enabled for a new camera. Disabling a feature hides or disables the corresponding control in the volunteer-facing widget.\n3. WHEN the admin selects `\"ndi\"` as the control protocol, THE detail panel SHALL display an informational note: \"NDI-only control does not support position inquiry. Zoom slider and tap-to-center will use last-commanded values, which may drift if the camera is controlled externally. Consider pairing with VISCA for accurate position feedback.\"\n4. WHEN the admin saves a camera configuration, THE Backend SHALL attempt to probe the camera on the selected protocol (per Req 3.5). THE admin page SHALL display the probe result: success (green checkmark with \"Connected\") or failure (red X with the error reason). Probe failure SHALL NOT prevent saving — the admin may be configuring a camera that is currently offline.\n5. THE admin device detail panel for cameras SHALL include a \"Presets\" section listing all configured presets for that camera. Each preset row SHALL display: name, sort order, and whether it's stored on camera (badge: \"On Camera\" or \"Software Only\"). Action buttons: Edit, Delete. An \"Add Preset\" button SHALL be available below the list.\n6. WHEN the admin taps \"Add Preset\" or \"Edit\" on a preset, THE Frontend SHALL open a modal titled \"Configure Preset\" (for new) or \"Edit Preset: {name}\" (for existing). The modal SHALL contain: (a) a Name text input, (b) a Sort Order number input, (c) a \"Store on Camera\" toggle with a camera slot number input (visible when toggled on), (d) the same PTZ controls as the volunteer widget (virtual joystick, zoom slider, toggle buttons including focus) so the admin can position the camera interactively, (e) a live video preview of the camera showing the current framing, (f) a \"Capture Position\" button.\n7. WHEN the admin taps \"Capture Position\", THE Backend SHALL poll the camera's current position values and store them in the preset. The following values SHALL be captured: Pan position (from VISCA inquiry or last-commanded NDI value), Tilt position (same), Zoom position (same), Focus position (only if Auto Focus is off; gracefully returns null if inquiry fails), Auto Focus state (from the toggle in the modal), AI Tracking state (from the toggle), Disable Tilt state (from the toggle), Disable Zoom state (from the toggle). THE Frontend SHALL display a brief \"Captured\" confirmation on the button.\n8. IF a position value cannot be captured (inquiry fails or NDI-only without commanded history), THE value SHALL be stored as null. THE admin SHALL be informed which values were captured vs. null via a summary display (e.g., \"Pan: -0.32, Tilt: 0.15, Zoom: 0.45, Focus: N/A\").\n9. WHEN \"Store on Camera\" is toggled on and a slot number is provided, THE Backend SHALL write the preset to the camera's onboard storage using the appropriate command (VISCA `preset_set` or `NDIlib_recv_ptz_store_preset`). IF the write fails, THE Backend SHALL display an error in the modal and revert the \"Store on Camera\" toggle.\n10. THE admin SHALL be able to delete presets with a confirmation dialog: \"Delete preset '{name}'? This cannot be undone.\" IF the preset is stored on camera, the deletion SHALL only remove it from the database — the camera's onboard memory is not cleared (to avoid accidentally erasing a preset that may be used by other control systems).\n11. THE Backend SHALL expose REST endpoints for camera preset CRUD operations: `GET /api/cameras/{cameraId}/presets`, `POST /api/cameras/{cameraId}/presets`, `PUT /api/cameras/{cameraId}/presets/{presetId}`, `DELETE /api/cameras/{cameraId}/presets/{presetId}`. All endpoints SHALL require the ADMIN role.\n12. WHEN a camera's presets are modified (created, edited, deleted), THE Backend SHALL broadcast the updated preset list to all connected clients via Socket.io so volunteer widgets reflect changes immediately without page refresh.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 8: Dashboard Seed Script Updates\n\n**User Story:** As a developer, I want the seed-dashboard script to include the new video preview widgets at appropriate sizes, so that a fresh installation has a functional default layout.\n\n#### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. THE `seed-dashboard.ts` script SHALL be updated to include the OBS Preview widget with widgetId `\"obs-preview\"`, positioned at 2×2 (colSpan: 2, rowSpan: 2) in the dashboard grid, with `roleMinimum: \"AvVolunteer\"`.\n2. THE `seed-dashboard.ts` script SHALL be updated to include the Camera widget with widgetId `\"camera\"`, positioned at 6×4 (colSpan: 6, rowSpan: 4) in the dashboard grid, with `roleMinimum: \"AvVolunteer\"`. At 6×4, the camera widget has sufficient space for the video preview (2×2 equivalent area) plus all PTZ controls in expanded mode.\n3. THE seed script SHALL place widgets to avoid overlap with existing widgets (OBS controls at 3×2, Lower Thirds at 3×2). THE exact grid positions (col, row) SHALL be chosen to produce a logical layout — suggested: OBS controls at (0,0), Lower Thirds at (3,0), OBS Preview at (6,0), Camera at (0,2).\n4. THE seed script SHALL remain idempotent — running it multiple times SHALL NOT create duplicate widgets. Each widget SHALL be checked by `dashboardId` + `widgetId` before insertion, matching the existing pattern.\n\n---\n\n## Accepted Risks\n\nThe following risks have been evaluated and explicitly accepted for this release:\n\n### Risk 1: NDI-Only Position Drift\n\nFor NDI-only cameras (no VISCA inquiry), the system tracks position based on commands issued through the system. If the camera is moved externally (physical joystick, another control system), the backend's position model drifts from reality. Tap-to-center and preset capture may produce incorrect results. This is accepted because: (a) the admin UI clearly warns about this limitation when NDI-only is selected, (b) activating a preset re-anchors to absolute values, and (c) the volunteer can always use the joystick for fine correction after tap-to-center. The mitigation is to recommend VISCA pairing for cameras that may be controlled externally.\n\n### Risk 2: Camera Widget at 6×4 Dominates the Dashboard\n\nThe camera widget occupies 60% of horizontal and 67% of vertical grid space at the seeded 6×4 size. This leaves limited room for other widgets (OBS controls, lower thirds, OBS preview). This is accepted because: (a) the camera operator is typically a dedicated role — they need the camera widget as their primary interface, (b) widgets can be rearranged via admin configuration for different dashboard layouts (e.g., a \"camera operator\" dashboard vs. a \"stream manager\" dashboard), and (c) compact mode is available for smaller widget placements.\n\n### Risk 3: Multi-Client PTZ Command Conflicts\n\nWhen two clients send conflicting PTZ commands to the same camera simultaneously, the behavior is last-writer-wins with non-deterministic arrival order. This matches the precedent set in `livestream-control-system` Requirement 22 (Concurrent Command Non-Determinism). Both clients receive the reconciled state via normal Socket.io broadcast. This is accepted because: (a) the typical deployment has one camera operator per camera, and (b) conflicting commands are self-correcting (the volunteer sees the result and adjusts).\n\n### Risk 4: Preview WebSocket JWT Expiry on Long Sessions\n\nPreview WebSocket connections authenticate via JWT query parameter. If the JWT expires mid-session (default 8h), the connection will be closed with code 4401. The volunteer must refresh the page to re-authenticate. This is accepted because: (a) services rarely exceed 3 hours, (b) the 30-day \"Remember me\" option covers multi-service days, and (c) the reconnection logic will surface the issue clearly (exponential backoff with \"Reconnecting...\" overlay, eventually showing unhealthy indicator).\n\n### Risk 5: FFmpeg Cold-Start Latency\n\nThe on-demand FFmpeg spawning means the first client to view a preview source experiences 2-5 seconds of delay before video appears (process spawn + source negotiation + first keyframe). This is accepted because: (a) the 3-second grace period prevents thrashing on page refresh, (b) the \"Connecting...\" transitional state sets expectations, and (c) once running, subsequent clients get instant video via fan-out. A future optimization could pre-warm FFmpeg for cameras that have presets configured.\n\n### Risk 6: OBS Record-Only Preview May Not Be Available\n\nWhen OBS is recording but not streaming (not sending to the relay), the preview requires OBS virtual output support which may not be configured. If unavailable, the widget shows \"Preview unavailable — start streaming to enable.\" This is accepted because: (a) the primary use case is live streaming (where preview always works via the relay), (b) record-only without streaming is rare in this environment, and (c) the message clearly explains the situation."
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    },

        "message_id": "a7c47cb2-484f-4128-9e88-8674cf9def8d",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "The spec has been expanded since my initial write. I can see several additions that were made (either by you or a subsequent editing pass). Here's my review:\n\n## What's Been Added/Changed (compared to my initial write)\n\n**Good additions I notice:**\n\n1. **Req 1.8 — Buffer management detail** — Excellent. The 2-second buffer trim, 3-second seek-to-live-edge, and the explicit rationale tying it to tap-to-center accuracy. This is a real-world concern that my original missed.\n\n2. **Req 1.13 — NDI SDK graceful degradation** — Very solid. Dynamic import with try/catch, graceful fallback to VISCA-only, clear messaging, and system continues to function. This correctly identifies NDI native bindings as the primary install-time risk.\n\n3. **Req 1.14 — MAX_PREVIEW_STREAMS cap** — Good safeguard. The lower OS priority for preview vs. streaming FFmpeg is an important detail.\n\n4. **Req 3.10 — MAX_EFFECTIVE_SPEED cap and NAK retry** — Smart addition. The global speed cap prevents camera whips, and the NAK retry at 50% handles cameras with different speed range support.\n\n5. **Req 3.11 — Dead-man's switch timeout 750ms** — Changed from my original 500ms with clear rationale (3.5× safety margin for WiFi jank). Good call — 500ms was too aggressive for tablets.\n\n6. **Req 3.12 — Full `stc:camera:state` payload definition** — Including `ndiAvailable: boolean` for frontend feature gating. This was implicit before, now explicit.\n\n7. **Req 4.2 — Camera dropdown localStorage persistence and hide-when-single** — Practical UX polish.\n\n8. **Req 4.9/4.10 — Connecting state and freeze-frame transition** — Nice UX detail. The distinction between \"never connected\" and \"switching cameras\" avoids confusion.\n\n9. **Req 5.2/5.3 — Virtual joystick replacing D-pad** — Major UX improvement over my original D-pad. The proportional speed from distance-from-center is much more natural on a touch device, and diagonal movement is inherent rather than requiring simultaneous button presses.\n\n10. **Req 5.3 — Dead-zone (15%), speed quantization (0.05), and stale-session handling** — These prevent real problems: finger tremor jitter, servo hunting, and ghost movements after reconnect.\n\n11. **Req 6.8 — Preset timeout 10s** — Changed from 5s with rationale about mechanical PTZ traverse time. Correct — some cameras take 6-8 seconds for a full-range move.\n\n12. **Req 7.1 — NDI SDK unavailability warning in admin** — Consistent with Req 1.13.\n\n13. **Accepted Risks section** — This is a mature engineering addition. Each risk is clearly stated with rationale for acceptance and mitigation strategy.\n\n14. **Glossary addition — Virtual Joystick** — Matches the Req 5 change from D-pad.\n\n## Issues/Suggestions\n\n1. **Req 5.1 still references \"D-pad\"** in the layout description (\"pan/tilt pad\" — minor). Actually, looking more carefully, it says \"virtual joystick\" — this is fine.\n\n2. **Req 5.9 still says \"D-pad movement\"** as part of what clears active preset — this should be \"joystick movement\" for consistency. Actually, this is in **Req 6.6**, not 5.9. Let me check:\n\n> \"WHEN the user makes any manual change (D-pad movement, zoom slider, toggle, or tap-to-center)\"\n\nThis reference to \"D-pad\" in Req 6.6 should be updated to \"joystick movement\" since the control was changed to a virtual joystick.\n\n3. **Req 5.10** references \"D-pad\" in the last sentence: \"the volunteer can tap again or use the D-pad for fine adjustment.\" — should be \"the joystick\".\n\n4. **No mention of focus dropdown for preset focus points** — In the original discussion, you mentioned \"the ability to choose (from a dropdown) a specific focus point, if any are available (disabled dropdown otherwise).\" I don't see this reflected in the spec. The focus control is described as a slider (absolute 0.0–1.0), but not the named focus point dropdown. Was this intentionally dropped, or should it be added?\n\n5. **Multi-camera architecture in Req 4.2** — It says \"support multiple instances (one per configured camera)\" but then says the widget has a dropdown to switch between cameras. These are subtly different patterns. Is it one widget instance with a dropdown (user picks which camera), or one widget instance *per camera*? The spec should clarify: it appears to be **one widget with a dropdown** (not multiple widget instances), which aligns with the bandwidth discussion (\"only pulling two streams max at a time\" = OBS + one camera).\n\n---\n\nWant me to apply fixes for issues #2, #3, and #5? And should we add the focus-point dropdown (#4), or was that intentionally deferred?"
          }
        ]
      }
    },

      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "ToolResults",

            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "tooluse_s306wkZMfuFZIx8SdIyUXH",
              "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "# Design Document — Lower Thirds\n\n## Overview\n\nThis document extends the existing system design with a lower-third overlay capability. It covers the architecture, interfaces, data models, animation state machine, component specifications, and socket communication required to display animated lower-third graphics on a livestream via OBS.\n\nThis is an extension document — it references and builds on the original design docs at `.kiro/specs/livestream-control-system/design.md` and `.kiro/specs/multi-platform-streaming/design.md`. Patterns, conventions, and components defined there remain authoritative unless explicitly superseded here.\n\n### What This Release Adds\n\n- Static HTML overlay wrapper (`packages/overlay/lower-thirds.html`) for OBS `file://` loading\n- Overlay React page (`/overlay/lower-thirds`) with Aspect Ratio Jail and animation engine\n- Unauthenticated `/overlay` Socket.io namespace for display commands\n- `LowerThirdService` — backend state management, auto-dismiss timers, transition locks\n- `LowerThirdModule` — Socket.io gateway module for dashboard ↔ backend communication\n- Overlay namespace handler — backend ↔ overlay communication\n- Lower-third widget with swipe-to-reveal action pattern\n- Extension of `metadata_templates` table for lower-third templates\n- `POST /api/overlay/logs` — unauthenticated, rate-limited logging endpoint for the overlay\n- Blue Rhombus animation style (entrance, exit, push-up, force-clear)\n- Scripture pagination protocol (measure-on-add, cached page breaks, 10s timeout fallback)\n\n### Breaking Changes\n\n- **`metadata_templates` table**: `category` CHECK constraint expanded from `('title', 'description')` to `('title', 'description', 'lower_third')`. Two new nullable columns added: `lowerThirdType TEXT` and `autoDismissMs INTEGER`.\n- **`MetadataTemplateDao`**: `TemplateCategory` type expanded. New methods for lower-third queries.\n- **Admin Templates Page**: Third section added for lower-third templates.\n\n### Steering Document Updates Required\n\nThis spec introduces patterns not yet documented in the steering doc. The following updates are required during implementation:\n\n- **§3 (Interfaces & Boundaries)**: Add `file://` and `/overlay` namespace boundaries\n- **§6 (Logging)**: Add `\"overlay\"` as a third `source` value\n- **§7 (Event Naming)**: Add `sto:` and `ots:` prefix rows; add overlay namespace exception note\n- **§10 (Responsive Sizing)**: Clarify rem applies to dashboard; overlay uses `cqw`/`cqh`\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Extended Topology\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n  subgraph OBS [OBS Studio]\n    BrowserSource[Browser Source — file://overlay/lower-thirds.html]\n    StaticWrapper[Static Wrapper — manages iFrame lifecycle]\n    OverlayPage[Overlay Page — /overlay/lower-thirds]\n    StaticWrapper --> OverlayPage\n  end\n\n  subgraph Frontend [packages/frontend]\n    LowerThirdWidget[Lower Third Widget — new]\n    AdminTemplates[Admin Templates Page — modified]\n    OverlayRoute[\"/overlay/lower-thirds route — new, outside ProtectedRoutes\"]\n  end\n\n  subgraph Backend [packages/backend]\n    LowerThirdService[LowerThirdService — new]\n    LowerThirdModule[LowerThirdModule — new socket module]\n    OverlayNamespace[\"/overlay namespace — new, unauthenticated\"]\n    SessionManifestService[SessionManifestService — existing]\n    MetadataTemplateDao[MetadataTemplateDao — modified]\n    EventBus[EventBus]\n    OverlayLogRoute[POST /api/overlay/logs — new, unauthenticated, rate-limited]\n  end\n\n  subgraph Storage\n    AppDB[(SQLite app.db)]\n    TemplatesTable[(metadata_templates — modified)]\n    KJV[(kjv table — existing)]\n  end\n\n  BrowserSource -->|file://| StaticWrapper\n  StaticWrapper -->|iFrame + postMessage| OverlayRoute\n  OverlayPage -->|Socket.io /overlay| OverlayNamespace\n  OverlayPage -->|POST /api/overlay/logs| OverlayLogRoute\n\n  LowerThirdWidget -->|Socket.io default ns| LowerThirdModule\n  LowerThirdModule --> LowerThirdService\n  OverlayNamespace --> LowerThirdService\n\n  LowerThirdService --> MetadataTemplateDao\n  LowerThirdService --> KJV\n  MetadataTemplateDao --> TemplatesTable\n\n  EventBus -->|bus:session:manifest:updated| LowerThirdService\n  EventBus -->|bus:lower-third:state:changed| LowerThirdModule\n  LowerThirdService -->|bus:lower-third:state:changed| EventBus\n```\n\n### Key Architectural Decisions\n\n**Two-layer overlay (static wrapper + iFrame)**: The static HTML file is loaded via `file://` in OBS, making it immune to frontend/backend availability at OBS startup time. The iFrame loads the React page only when the frontend signals readiness via postMessage. This eliminates the need to refresh the OBS browser source after system startup.\n\n**Unauthenticated `/overlay` namespace**: The overlay page runs in OBS with no user interaction — there's no way to log in. The `/overlay` namespace accepts connections without JWT but only emits display commands and accepts phase reports. No control commands are accepted on this namespace. The namespace enforces single-client: new connections forcibly disconnect the previous client.\n\n**No Staged section — Preview Dialog instead**: Rather than a persistent \"Staged\" queue, the volunteer sees a Preview Dialog before activation. This reduces widget complexity (two sections instead of three), provides a clear confirmation step, and eliminates the confusion of \"what does staged mean?\" The preview is ephemeral — dismissing the dialog cancels the action.\n\n**Swipe-to-reveal actions**: Each row shows one primary button. Secondary actions are revealed by swiping. This reduces visual clutter while maintaining discoverability. The pattern is consistent across all rows.\n\n**Force Clear bypasses everything**: The emergency clear action skips animation, ignores transition locks, and immediately hides the overlay. This is the \"wrong content on screen\" panic button.\n\n**Backend owns all state**: The overlay is a pure renderer. The dashboard is a pure controller. The backend is the single source of truth.\n\n**5-second fallback timeout**: If the overlay doesn't report phase completion, the backend advances state and notifies the dashboard. This prevents permanent lock-up from a crashed overlay.\n\n---\n\n## Backend Services\n\n### LowerThirdService (New)\n\n```typescript\ninterface LowerThirdService {\n  // Library management\n  getLibrary(): LowerThirdItem[];\n  addToLibrary(input: AddLowerThirdInput): Result<LowerThirdItem, string>;\n  removeFromLibrary(itemId: string): Result<void, string>;\n  editLibraryItem(itemId: string, patch: EditLowerThirdInput): Result<LowerThirdItem, string>;\n\n  // Activation (directly from library)\n  activate(itemId: string): Result<void, string>;\n  dismissActive(): Result<void, string>;\n  forceClear(): void; // always succeeds, bypasses lock\n\n  // Pagination (scripture)\n  pageNext(): Result<void, string>;\n  pagePrevious(): Result<void, string>;\n\n  // Phase tracking (called by overlay namespace handler)\n  reportPhase(phase: AnimationPhase): void;\n  reportPages(itemId: string, pages: PageBreakdown): void;\n\n  // Overlay connection\n  setOverlayConnected(connected: boolean): void;\n  getPendingMeasurements(): LowerThirdItem[];\n  handleResolutionReport(data: ResolutionReport): void;\n\n  // State\n  getFullState(): LowerThirdState;\n  isTransitionLocked(): boolean;\n\n  destroy(): void;\n}\n```\n\n**Constructor dependencies**: `MetadataTemplateDao`, `Database` (for KJV queries), `SessionManifestService`.\n"
                }

              "status": "success"

              "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "**EventBus subscriptions**: `BUS_SESSION_MANIFEST_UPDATED` — recomputes template-derived library items.\n\n**EventBus emissions**: `BUS_LOWER_THIRD_STATE_CHANGED` — emitted on any state change.\n\n### Animation State Machine\n\n```\n                ┌────────────────────────────────────┐\n                │                                    │\n                ▼                                    │\n  ┌────────┐  show   ┌─────────┐  overlay   ┌─────────┐\n  │ hidden │────────▶│ showing │──reports──▶│ visible │\n  └────────┘         └─────────┘            └─────────┘\n       ▲                                        │\n       │                                        │ dismiss / auto-dismiss\n       │              ┌───────────┐             │\n       └──────────────│ dismissing│◀────────────┘\n          overlay     └───────────┘\n          reports\n\n  Force Clear: ANY state ──────────────────────▶ hidden (instant)\n```\n\n**Transition lock**: Locked when phase is `showing` or `dismissing`. Unlocked when `visible` or `hidden`. Force Clear bypasses the lock.\n\n**Push-up**: `visible` → `showing` directly (no `dismissing` step). Overlay handles internally.\n\n**5-second fallback**: If overlay doesn't report within 5s, backend advances phase and emits warning notification.\n\n### Core Types\n\n```typescript\ntype LowerThirdType = \"Title\" | \"TitleSubtitle\" | \"Scripture\";\ntype AnimationPhase = \"hidden\" | \"showing\" | \"visible\" | \"dismissing\";\ntype LowerThirdStyle = \"blue_rhombus\";\n\ninterface LowerThirdItem {\n  id: string;\n  type: LowerThirdType;\n  style: LowerThirdStyle;\n  content: TitleContent | TitleSubtitleContent | ScriptureContent;\n  autoDismissMs: number | null;\n  source: \"template\" | \"volunteer\";\n  templateId: string | null;\n  templateName: string | null;\n  used: boolean;\n  createdAt: string;\n  pages: PageBreakdown | null;\n}\n\ninterface TitleContent {\n  title: string;\n}\ninterface TitleSubtitleContent {\n  title: string;\n  subtitle: string;\n}\ninterface ScriptureContent {\n  reference: ScriptureReference;\n  formattedReference: string;\n  verses: VerseData[]; // always populated after successful add (Req 3.10 ensures KJV data exists)\n}\ninterface VerseData {\n  verseNumber: number;\n  text: string;\n}\n\ninterface PageBreakdown {\n  totalPages: number;\n  currentPage: number;\n  pages: PageInfo[];\n}\ninterface PageInfo {\n  pageNumber: number;\n  startVerse: number;\n  endVerse: number;\n}\n\ninterface LowerThirdState {\n  active: LowerThirdItem | null;\n  library: LowerThirdItem[];\n  phase: AnimationPhase;\n  autoDismissAt: string | null;\n  overlayConnected: boolean;\n  overlayResolutionCorrect: boolean;\n  transitionLocked: boolean;\n}\n\ninterface AddLowerThirdInput {\n  type: LowerThirdType;\n  content: TitleContent | TitleSubtitleContent | { reference: ScriptureReference };\n  autoDismissMs?: number;\n}\n\ninterface EditLowerThirdInput {\n  content?: TitleContent | TitleSubtitleContent | { reference: ScriptureReference };\n  autoDismissMs?: number;\n}\n```\n"

                    "Text": "**EventBus subscriptions**: `BUS_SESSION_MANIFEST_UPDATED` — recomputes template-derived library items.\n\n**EventBus emissions**: `BUS_LOWER_THIRD_STATE_CHANGED` — emitted on any state change.\n\n### Animation State Machine\n\n```\n                ┌────────────────────────────────────┐\n                │                                    │\n                ▼                                    │\n  ┌────────┐  show   ┌─────────┐  overlay   ┌─────────┐\n  │ hidden │────────▶│ showing │──reports──▶│ visible │\n  └────────┘         └─────────┘            └─────────┘\n       ▲                                        │\n       │                                        │ dismiss / auto-dismiss\n       │              ┌───────────┐             │\n       └──────────────│ dismissing│◀────────────┘\n          overlay     └───────────┘\n          reports\n\n  Force Clear: ANY state ──────────────────────▶ hidden (instant)\n```\n\n**Transition lock**: Locked when phase is `showing` or `dismissing`. Unlocked when `visible` or `hidden`. Force Clear bypasses the lock.\n\n**Push-up**: `visible` → `showing` directly (no `dismissing` step). Overlay handles internally.\n\n**5-second fallback**: If overlay doesn't report within 5s, backend advances phase and emits warning notification.\n\n### Core Types\n\n```typescript\ntype LowerThirdType = \"Title\" | \"TitleSubtitle\" | \"Scripture\";\ntype AnimationPhase = \"hidden\" | \"showing\" | \"visible\" | \"dismissing\";\ntype LowerThirdStyle = \"blue_rhombus\";\n\ninterface LowerThirdItem {\n  id: string;\n  type: LowerThirdType;\n  style: LowerThirdStyle;\n  content: TitleContent | TitleSubtitleContent | ScriptureContent;\n  autoDismissMs: number | null;\n  source: \"template\" | \"volunteer\";\n  templateId: string | null;\n  templateName: string | null;\n  used: boolean;\n  createdAt: string;\n  pages: PageBreakdown | null;\n}\n\ninterface TitleContent {\n  title: string;\n}\ninterface TitleSubtitleContent {\n  title: string;\n  subtitle: string;\n}\ninterface ScriptureContent {\n  reference: ScriptureReference;\n  formattedReference: string;\n  verses: VerseData[]; // always populated after successful add (Req 3.10 ensures KJV data exists)\n}\ninterface VerseData {\n  verseNumber: number;\n  text: string;\n}\n\ninterface PageBreakdown {\n  totalPages: number;\n  currentPage: number;\n  pages: PageInfo[];\n}\ninterface PageInfo {\n  pageNumber: number;\n  startVerse: number;\n  endVerse: number;\n}\n\ninterface LowerThirdState {\n  active: LowerThirdItem | null;\n  library: LowerThirdItem[];\n  phase: AnimationPhase;\n  autoDismissAt: string | null;\n  overlayConnected: boolean;\n  overlayResolutionCorrect: boolean;\n  transitionLocked: boolean;\n}\n\ninterface AddLowerThirdInput {\n  type: LowerThirdType;\n  content: TitleContent | TitleSubtitleContent | { reference: ScriptureReference };\n  autoDismissMs?: number;\n}\n\ninterface EditLowerThirdInput {\n  content?: TitleContent | TitleSubtitleContent | { reference: ScriptureReference };\n  autoDismissMs?: number;\n}\n```\n"
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }

                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Frontend — Dashboard\n\n### Zustand Slice\n\n```typescript\ninterface LowerThirdSlice {\n  lowerThirdState: LowerThirdState;\n  setLowerThirdState: (state: LowerThirdState) => void;\n}\n```\n\n### Widget: `LowerThirdWidget`\n\n```\nWidgetContainer (title: \"Lower Thirds\", connections: [{ label: \"Overlay\", status }])\n├── ActiveSection\n│   ├── ActiveRow (dismiss button visible, swipe-left for Force Clear)\n│   │   ├── CountdownIndicator (if auto-dismiss)\n│   │   └── StatusOverlay (\"Dismissing...\", blocks interaction)\n│   └── PaginationRow (if paginated scripture)\n├── LibrarySection\n│   ├── TemplateItems (sorted by name)\n│   │   └── Row (Show button visible, swipe-left for Go Live, swipe-right for Go Live)\n│   └── VolunteerItems (sorted by creation time)\n│       └── Row (Show button visible, swipe-left for Edit/Delete, swipe-right for Go Live)\n├── EmptyStates (\"Nothing active\", \"No items available\")\n├── AddButton (dropdown → type → input dialog)\n└── PreviewDialog (modal: content preview + Cancel/Go Live)\n```\n\n### Swipe-to-Reveal Implementation\n\nEach row uses a swipeable container (e.g., CSS `transform: translateX()` with touch event handlers). Actions are revealed as icon+label buttons (icon on top, label below, 2.5rem × 2.5rem). Only one row may be swiped open at a time — opening a new row closes the previous.\n\n### Widget Registration and Connection Indicator\n\nThe widget is registered with `widgetId: \"lower-thirds\"`, configurable per-dashboard via `widget_configurations`.\n\n**Connection indicator state derivation** (from `LowerThirdState` → `ConnectionStatus`):\n\n- `healthy`: `overlayConnected === true && overlayResolutionCorrect === true`\n- `degraded`: `overlayConnected === true && overlayResolutionCorrect === false`\n- `unhealthy`: `overlayConnected === false`\n- `inactive`: no lower-third templates exist in the database (checked via DAO on initial load)\n\n---\n\n## Frontend — Overlay Page\n\n### Route Registration\n\n```typescript\n// Outside ProtectedRoutes — no auth wrapper, no layout\n<Route path=\"/overlay/lower-thirds\" element={<LowerThirdOverlay />} />\n```\n\n### Component: `LowerThirdOverlay`\n\n- Connects to `/overlay` namespace (no auth)\n- Waits for `document.fonts.ready` before sending `overlay-ready` postMessage\n- Sends heartbeat postMessages every 5s to parent (static wrapper health check)\n- Renders Aspect Ratio Jail + active lower-third\n- Handles all STO commands, reports phases via OTS\n- Measures scripture in hidden container on `measure` command\n- When receiving `STO_LOWER_THIRD_SHOW` for a scripture item with no cached pages, measures first, reports pages via `OTS_LOWER_THIRD_PAGES`, then animates\n- A `show` command cancels any in-progress measurement for a different item (the measured item is no longer relevant)\n- 15-second disconnect timeout for stuck graphic prevention (configurable via `OVERLAY_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` env var, default 15000)\n- Logs via `POST /api/overlay/logs`\n- Force Clear: immediately sets `display: none`, reports `hidden`\n\n### Animation Implementation\n\n**Entrance**: Rhombus `scaleY(0→1)` from center (~200ms) → plate+text unfold right (~400ms)\n\n**Exit**: Rhombus slides right as traveling curtain (~600ms) → rhombus `scaleY(1→0)` to center (~200ms)\n\n**Push-up**: Container `overflow: hidden`, old `translateY(-100%)` + new `translateY(0)` (~300ms), plate height transitions\n\n**Force Clear**: `display: none` — instant, no animation\n\n### Aspect Ratio Jail CSS\n\n```css\n.aspect-ratio-jail {\n  position: absolute;\n  inset: 0;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: flex-end;\n  justify-content: flex-start;\n  aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;\n  max-width: 100vw;\n  max-height: 100vh;\n  margin: auto;\n  container-type: size;\n  container-name: overlay;"
                }
              ],
              "status": "success"
            }

      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "AssistantMessage",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "cddf7735-dd84-4a58-a642-c99ef9a8ced5",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Now let me write the design doc section by section:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "tooluse_OTCynmUyObotHN1j9LHzks",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Create design.md with intro, architecture, and database schema",
                "command": "create",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/design.md",
                "content": "# Design Document — Video Control and Preview\n\n## Overview\n\nThis document extends the existing system design with real-time video preview and NDI/VISCA camera control capabilities. It covers the preview streaming infrastructure, OBS preview widget, Camera HAL abstraction, camera control widget with virtual joystick, preset management, and admin configuration.\n\nThis is an extension document — it references and builds on the designs at `.kiro/specs/livestream-control-system/design.md` and `.kiro/specs/multi-platform-streaming/design.md`. Patterns, conventions, and components defined there remain authoritative unless explicitly superseded here.\n\n### What This Release Adds\n\n- Preview WebSocket infrastructure (fMP4 over dedicated WebSocket, MSE playback, fan-out)\n- FFmpeg hardware encoder auto-detection (VA-API, QSV, NVENC) with software fallback\n- OBS Preview widget (`obs-preview`) — 2×2, live stream/recording preview with audio toggle\n- `CameraControlInterface` — protocol-agnostic PTZ abstraction (NDI + VISCA implementations)\n- `CameraService` — manages camera connections, state polling, dead-man's switch\n- Camera widget (`camera`) — 6×4, live preview with virtual joystick PTZ controls\n- Camera preset system — database-stored with optional onboard camera mirroring\n- Admin camera device type with feature toggles, preset configuration modal\n- `CameraSocketModule` — Socket.io gateway for PTZ commands and state broadcast\n- NDI SDK dynamic loading with graceful degradation\n\n### Breaking Changes\n\n- **`device_connections` table**: `deviceType` CHECK constraint expanded to include `\"camera\"`. New nullable columns for camera-specific config: `controlProtocol`, `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, `ndiSourceName`, `fovWideAngle`, `features`.\n- **New table**: `camera_presets` for preset storage.\n- **`seed-dashboard.ts`**: Two new widget entries (OBS Preview at 2×2, Camera at 6×4); existing widget positions adjusted to avoid overlap.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Extended Topology\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n  subgraph Frontend [packages/frontend]\n    ObsPreviewWidget[OBS Preview Widget]\n    CameraWidget[Camera Widget]\n    CameraModal[Camera Control Modal]\n    AdminDevices[Admin Device Management — modified]\n  end\n\n  subgraph Backend [packages/backend]\n    PreviewManager[PreviewStreamManager]\n    CameraService[CameraService]\n    CameraModule[CameraSocketModule]\n    NdiDriver[NdiCameraDriver]\n    ViscaDriver[ViscaCameraDriver]\n    ObsService[ObsService — existing]\n    EventBus[EventBus]\n  end\n\n  subgraph External\n    OBS[OBS Studio]\n    RTMPRelay[RTMP Relay — existing]\n    NDICamera[NDI Camera on LAN]\n  end\n\n  subgraph FFmpeg [FFmpeg Processes]\n    ObsFFmpeg[FFmpeg: RTMP → fMP4]\n    CamFFmpeg[FFmpeg: NDI → fMP4]\n  end\n\n  OBS -->|RTMP| RTMPRelay\n  RTMPRelay -->|RTMP read| ObsFFmpeg\n  NDICamera -->|NDI video| CamFFmpeg\n  NDICamera -->|NDI PTZ| NdiDriver\n  NDICamera -->|VISCA/IP| ViscaDriver\n\n  ObsFFmpeg -->|fMP4 chunks| PreviewManager\n  CamFFmpeg -->|fMP4 chunks| PreviewManager\n\n  PreviewManager -->|WebSocket /preview/obs| ObsPreviewWidget\n  PreviewManager -->|WebSocket /preview/camera/:id| CameraWidget\n  PreviewManager -->|WebSocket /preview/camera/:id| CameraModal\n\n  CameraWidget -->|Socket.io| CameraModule\n  CameraModal -->|Socket.io| CameraModule\n  CameraModule --> CameraService\n  CameraService --> NdiDriver\n  CameraService --> ViscaDriver\n  CameraService -->|stc:camera:state| CameraWidget\n\n  ObsService -->|streaming/recording state| PreviewManager\n  EventBus -->|bus:obs:state:changed| PreviewManager\n```\n\n### Key Architectural Decisions\n\n**Dedicated WebSocket for video (not Socket.io)**: Binary video data at 2-5 Mbps would saturate the Socket.io command channel and make debugging impossible. Separate WebSocket endpoints allow independent lifecycle, authentication, and monitoring. Socket.io remains for structured command/event exchange.\n\n**fMP4 + MSE over WebRTC**: WebRTC adds ICE/STUN complexity for a LAN-only system where NAT traversal is unnecessary. fMP4 over WebSocket achieves equivalent latency (<500ms) with simpler implementation, no STUN server, and easier debugging (binary frames over a single TCP connection).\n\n**Single FFmpeg per source with fan-out**: Avoids redundant transcoding when multiple clients view the same preview. The `PreviewStreamManager` buffers the latest keyframe + subsequent frames so new subscribers get immediate playback without waiting for the next keyframe.\n\n**NDI SDK as optional dynamic dependency**: The NDI SDK requires native bindings (`grandiose`) that need C++ build tools. Making it a dynamic import (`import()` with try/catch) means `npm install` succeeds on any machine, and the system degrades gracefully to VISCA-only control without video preview.\n\n**Virtual joystick over D-pad**: Touch devices benefit from proportional analog input. The joystick provides natural diagonal movement, proportional speed control (distance from center), and better ergonomics for sustained operation during a service.\n\n**Adaptive speed tied to zoom**: Prevents PTZ overshoot at telephoto without requiring the operator to manually adjust speed. The formula `speed * (1 - zoom * 0.7)` gives 100% at wide angle, 30% at full telephoto.\n\n**Hybrid preset storage**: Database-first with optional camera onboard mirroring. Database presets are camera-agnostic (survive camera replacement), store metadata cameras can't (toggle states), and have well-defined content. Onboard presets provide MotionSync smooth recall on cameras that support it.\n\n---\n\n## Database Schema\n\n### Modified: `device_connections`\n\n```sql\n-- Existing columns remain unchanged. New columns for camera devices:\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN controlProtocol TEXT; -- 'ndi' | 'visca'\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN viscaHost TEXT;\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN viscaPort INTEGER DEFAULT 5500;\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN ndiSourceName TEXT;\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN fovWideAngle REAL DEFAULT 60.0;\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN features TEXT; -- JSON string: [\"pan\",\"tilt\",\"zoom\",\"focus\",\"ai-tracking\",\"ai-tracking-tilt-disable\",\"ai-tracking-zoom-disable\"]\n```\n\n`deviceType` CHECK constraint updated: `CHECK(deviceType IN ('obs', 'camera'))`\n\n### New: `camera_presets`\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE camera_presets (\n  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  cameraId TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES device_connections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  sortOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  storedOnCamera INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  cameraPresetSlot INTEGER,\n  pan REAL,\n  tilt REAL,\n  zoom REAL,\n  focus REAL,\n  autoFocus INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, -- boolean\n  aiTracking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  disableTilt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  disableZoom INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  createdAt TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_camera_presets_camera ON camera_presets(cameraId);\n```\n"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },

        "content": [
          {
