    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "Prompt",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "c0ccccde-f9c9-4888-a415-967ee1c4dbe6",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "You mentioned a present vs tracking mode. What do those do?"
          }
        ],
        "meta": {
          "timestamp": 1780705096
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "AssistantMessage",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "9582082a-c2cb-4513-a6c5-5b7775d42a92",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Based on the Tongveo/Tenveo product listings and similar cameras:\n\n**Presenter Tracking** — The camera uses AI (face + body recognition) to follow a single person as they move around the stage. The camera pans, tilts, and zooms to keep that person centered in frame. If the person leaves the field of view entirely, the camera returns to a \"home\" position and waits for them to reappear.\n\n**Auto-Framing** — Instead of physically panning/tilting the camera, it uses the full sensor (often at a wider angle) and digitally crops/zooms to frame the subject. The camera body stays still — only the digital crop window moves. This is smoother but you lose optical resolution since you're cropping a portion of the sensor.\n\nSome cameras in this tier (like the Newegg listing for the Tongveo NDI) also mention a third mode:\n\n**Zone Tracking** — You define preset zones (areas of the stage). When the subject moves from one zone to another, the camera transitions to the corresponding preset position. This is less \"following\" and more \"switching between predetermined shots based on where the person is.\"\n\nFor our spec purposes: the Tongveo appears to expose **Presenter Tracking on/off** and **Auto-Framing on/off** as the two modes — selectable via the camera's web interface. What we're calling \"AI Tracking\" in our spec would map to enabling Presenter Tracking. The \"Disable Zoom\" concept would mean switching from Presenter Tracking (which zooms to follow) to something more constrained — but the camera doesn't expose that as a separate toggle; it's baked into the mode selection.\n\nDoes this change how you want to model the AI tracking toggles, or are you comfortable with the current approach (keep them in the feature set, disable the ones this camera can't do)?"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "Prompt",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "2d37f6f6-445a-4a6a-8ad2-3474c6bb6415",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Okay, we're going to need to make the camera setup a bit more complex. From the customer perspective, the buggest change is that AI Tracking is now a PowerUser/Admin feature. AvVolunteer should not have the ability to configure this directly (presets still can).\n\nFrom a architectural standpoint, and admin setup standpoint, we're going to need to know if we support a specific model of camera for these controls. For the Tongveo model mentioned, we will need to use HTTP commands sent to the camera. Only if we know the camera (i.e. the user sets a given camera setup as a non-generic one), then will we support AI modes. Otherwise, no AI options should be present.\n\nWe'll need a cookie sent with the HTTP requests. This should be a new .env file configuration, which will also need updated in the setup docs. The way to get this is to visit the camera's web interface, and take the cooke from a PTZ or AI request sent to the camera. A word of caution should be put that the admin will need to check if the cookie is stable. If it's not, the features aren't supported.\n\nFor our Tongveo camera, AI controls are set via two APIs\nEnabling AI\nPath: http://192.168.50.43/api/aiControl\nBody:\n```\n{\n \"ai_on\": \"1\",\n \"ai_enable\": \"1\",\n \"ai_mode\": \"1\",\n \"ai_auto_zoom\": \"0\",\n \"ai_auto_tilt\": \"0\"\n}\n```\nai_on and a_enable should be `\"0\"` when we want AI off, and `\"1\"` when we want AI on.\nai_mode will always be 1\nai_auto_zoom and ai_auto_tilt should be `\"0\"` or `\"1\"` depending if we have those features on or off\n\nOn top of that, once that command is set the camera will need to choose which subject to track. We won't support switching targets, which means we're going to blindly set the first one the camera sees. So the software will turn on AI, and then immediately send this next command\nPath: http://192.168.50.43/api/setPTZCmd\nBody:\n```\n{\n \"Channel\": 0,\n \"PtzCmd\": 15,\n \"param1\": 7,\n \"param2\": 0,\n \"ID\": \"YWRtaW46YWRtaW4=\"\n}\n```\n\nThe ID is another env file addition, which the admin can pull from the web dev tools just like the cookie.\n\nAny questions?"
          }
        ],
        "meta": {
          "timestamp": 1780792131
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "AssistantMessage",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "ea0b3377-7318-4d58-9718-01e2f1e1b17b",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "A few questions:\n\n1. **AI toggle role restriction** — You said AI Tracking is now PowerUser/Admin only. Does that mean the toggle is *hidden* from volunteers entirely, or *visible but disabled* (greyed out, showing current state)? Volunteers can still activate presets that change AI state — they just can't toggle it directly?\n\n2. **Camera model selection** — When you say \"the user sets a given camera setup as a non-generic one\" — are you envisioning a dropdown in the admin device panel like \"Camera Model: Generic / Tongveo NVS20A\" ? And only when a known model is selected do the AI controls appear in the widget? Or is it more of a \"AI Control Protocol: None / Tongveo HTTP\" selection?\n\n3. **The cookie and ID env vars** — Should these be per-camera (since you might have multiple cameras with different cookies), or global? If per-camera, they'd go in the device config (stored encrypted like OAuth tokens) rather than `.env`. If you only ever have one camera model, `.env` is simpler but less flexible.\n\n4. **Disabling AI** — When turning AI off, do we need to send the `setPTZCmd` command too, or just the `aiControl` with `ai_on: \"0\"` / `ai_enable: \"0\"`?\n\n5. **ai_auto_zoom and ai_auto_tilt** — These map directly to our existing `ai-tracking-zoom-disable` and `ai-tracking-tilt-disable` features. So the Tongveo *does* support them after all — just via its HTTP API, not VISCA/NDI. Should we keep our feature names as-is (`ai-tracking-zoom-disable`, `ai-tracking-tilt-disable`) and the Tongveo driver translates them to `ai_auto_zoom: \"0\"` / `ai_auto_tilt: \"0\"`? (Noting the inversion: our \"disable zoom\" = their `ai_auto_zoom: \"0\"`)\n\n6. **The `setPTZCmd` \"pick first target\"** — Does this need to be sent every time AI is enabled, or only the first time? If the camera remembers its last tracking target across AI toggles, we might not need to resend. If it always starts in \"searching\" mode with no target, we always send it.\n\n7. **Latency concern** — After sending `aiControl` to enable tracking, how quickly do we need to send `setPTZCmd`? Is there a minimum delay needed for the camera to initialize tracking before it can accept a target selection? Or can we fire them back-to-back?"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "Prompt",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "14e0e0c5-6e3b-4edf-9079-56688661a77f",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "1. Hidden entirely\n2. Yes, exactly. A dropdown that is Camera Model.\n3. Let's go with per camera, and store it in the device config.\n4. When disabling, we only seend to run the aiControl command. DO NOT run the setPTZCmd, or we'll make the camera do things we don't want (explictly document that we do not call that second API when disabling)\n5. Eh, let's make then not be inverted. So `ai-tracking-zoom-enable` or really, `ai-tracking-zoom` is really sufficient, since we can enable or disable, and that word doesn't add anything.\n6. Since we won't know the state, always send it\n7. As far as I know, there's no delay needed. I assume that's an easy add later if we find we do need a short wait?"
          }
        ],
        "meta": {
          "timestamp": 1780792373
        }
      }
    },

    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "AssistantMessage",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "f50731cf-3533-45e4-99c2-ac0876c60af9",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Now the big one — update Req 7.1 to add camera model dropdown and HTTP API configuration:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "tooluse_flQTAWkfuHKeNibYm7Yluh",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Update Req 7.1 - Add camera model dropdown and HTTP API config",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "1. THE admin Device Management page (`/admin/devices`) SHALL support a new device type `\"camera-ptz\"`. WHEN adding a camera, the admin SHALL provide: label, Camera Model (dropdown: \"Generic\" or a known supported model, e.g., \"Tongveo NVS20A-4KN\"), NDI source name (required — for video feed and PTZ control; the NDI SDK discovers cameras by name on the LAN via mDNS-like broadcast), optionally VISCA IP address and port (for enhanced position polling accuracy, default port 5500), and wide-angle field of view in degrees (`fovWideAngle`, used for tap-to-center calculations, defaulting to 60°). WHEN a non-Generic camera model is selected, THE admin form SHALL display an additional \"AI Tracking Configuration\" section containing: (a) an HTTP Cookie field (stored encrypted in device config — the admin obtains this from browser dev tools while interacting with the camera's web interface), (b) an API Credential ID field (stored encrypted — the admin obtains this from the request payload in browser dev tools). THE admin form SHALL display a cautionary note: \"The cookie and credential may expire if the camera is rebooted or its session times out. Verify these values remain stable. If they change, AI tracking features will stop working until updated.\" `docs/setup.md` SHALL document how to obtain the cookie and credential ID from the camera's web interface using browser developer tools. WHEN Camera Model is \"Generic\", AI tracking features (`ai-tracking`, `ai-tracking-zoom`, `ai-tracking-tilt`) SHALL NOT appear in the features section and SHALL be unavailable in the widget. Camera device CRUD uses the existing `/api/admin/devices` endpoints with conditional validation: when `deviceType === \"camera-ptz\"`, the backend validates `ndiSourceName` is present (required) and accepts optional `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, `fovWideAngle`, `cameraFeatures`, `cameraModel`, `aiHttpCookie` (encrypted), and `aiCredentialId` (encrypted) fields. The existing `host`/`port` fields are auto-populated with `\"127.0.0.1\"`/`0` for cameras (not shown in the admin form). The admin form SHALL show VISCA fields as an optional \"Position Polling (Recommended)\" section with a toggle to enable/disable. For camera devices, the existing `host` and `port` columns in `device_connections` SHALL be stored as `\"127.0.0.1\"` and `0` respectively — these columns are NOT NULL and used by OBS devices, but irrelevant for cameras (camera-specific connection details use `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, and `ndiSourceName` columns). IF the NDI SDK is not available (Req 1.13), THE admin page SHALL display a warning: \"NDI SDK not installed — camera features are unavailable. Install the NDI SDK to enable cameras.\" `docs/setup.md` SHALL document NDI SDK installation as a prerequisite for camera features. THE Backend SHALL receive NDI video frames via the `grandiose` native module's receiver API and pipe them to FFmpeg (via stdin) for transcoding to fMP4 — this avoids requiring the separate FFmpeg NDI plugin to be compiled.",
                "oldStr": "1. THE admin Device Management page (`/admin/devices`) SHALL support a new device type `\"camera-ptz\"`. WHEN adding a camera, the admin SHALL provide: label, NDI source name (required — for video feed and PTZ control; the NDI SDK discovers cameras by name on the LAN via mDNS-like broadcast), optionally VISCA IP address and port (for enhanced position polling accuracy, default port 5500), and wide-angle field of view in degrees (`fovWideAngle`, used for tap-to-center calculations, defaulting to 60°). Camera device CRUD uses the existing `/api/admin/devices` endpoints with conditional validation: when `deviceType === \"camera-ptz\"`, the backend validates `ndiSourceName` is present (required) and accepts optional `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, `fovWideAngle`, and `cameraFeatures` fields. The existing `host`/`port` fields are auto-populated with `\"127.0.0.1\"`/`0` for cameras (not shown in the admin form). The admin form SHALL show VISCA fields as an optional \"Position Polling (Recommended)\" section with a toggle to enable/disable. For camera devices, the existing `host` and `port` columns in `device_connections` SHALL be stored as `\"127.0.0.1\"` and `0` respectively — these columns are NOT NULL and used by OBS devices, but irrelevant for cameras (camera-specific connection details use `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, and `ndiSourceName` columns). IF the NDI SDK is not available (Req 1.13), THE admin page SHALL display a warning: \"NDI SDK not installed — camera features are unavailable. Install the NDI SDK to enable cameras.\" `docs/setup.md` SHALL document NDI SDK installation as a prerequisite for camera features. THE Backend SHALL receive NDI video frames via the `grandiose` native module's receiver API and pipe them to FFmpeg (via stdin) for transcoding to fMP4 — this avoids requiring the separate FFmpeg NDI plugin to be compiled.",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/requirements.md"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },

                    "newStr": "1. THE admin Device Management page (`/admin/devices`) SHALL support a new device type `\"camera-ptz\"`. WHEN a non-Generic camera model is selected, THE admin form SHALL display an additional \"AI Tracking Configuration\" section containing: (a) an HTTP Cookie field (stored encrypted in device config — the admin obtains this from browser dev tools while interacting with the camera's web interface), (b) an API Credential ID field (stored encrypted — the admin obtains this from the request payload in browser dev tools).               "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "11. THE Backend SHALL implement a dead-man's switch for continuous PTZ movement. WHEN a `cts:camera:ptz:move:start` command is received, THE Backend SHALL begin continuous movement and expect `cts:camera:ptz:move:keepalive` events every 200ms from the client. IF no keepalive arrives within `DEADMAN_TIMEOUT_MS` (code constant, default: 750), THE Backend SHALL issue a stop command to the camera. The 750ms default (vs. the 200ms send interval) provides a 3.5× safety margin to absorb WiFi micro-dropouts and tablet JS thread jank without false-triggering on a healthy connection. This value is a tunable constant — if WiFi environments prove unreliable at 750ms, it can be increased without architectural changes. THE Frontend SHALL send `cts:camera:ptz:move:stop` on touch release. This protects against network drops causing runaway camera movement.\n12. THE Backend SHALL expose camera state via Socket.io using the established SocketModule pattern. Events: `stc:camera:state` (full state broadcast), `stc:camera:state:update` (single camera delta), `cts:camera:ptz:move:start`, `cts:camera:ptz:move:keepalive`, `cts:camera:ptz:move:stop`, `cts:camera:zoom:set`, `cts:camera:focus:auto`, `cts:camera:focus:set`, `cts:camera:preset:activate`, `cts:camera:ptz:tap-to-center`, `cts:camera:ai-tracking:set`, `cts:camera:disable-tilt:set`, `cts:camera:disable-zoom:set`. All event name constants SHALL be defined in `packages/shared/src/constants/socketEvents.ts`. THE `stc:camera:state` payload SHALL include per camera: `{ cameraId, connected, position: { pan, tilt, zoom, focus } | null, autoFocus, aiTracking, disableTilt, disableZoom, activePresetId: string | null, features: string[], presets: CameraPreset[] }`. THE `emitInitialState` handler SHALL send the state for all configured cameras. THE Backend SHALL also include `ndiAvailable: boolean` at the top level so the frontend knows whether NDI features are operational. THE `CameraService` SHALL emit `bus:camera:state:changed` on the EventBus whenever camera state changes (position, connection, toggles, active preset). THE `CameraSocketModule` subscribes to this event to broadcast updates — consistent with the EventBus subscription pattern used by all other socket modules.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 4: NDI Camera Video Preview\n\n**User Story:** As a volunteer, I want to see a real-time preview of what the camera sees directly on my dashboard, so that I can frame shots accurately without needing a separate monitor."
                }
              ],
              "status": "success"
            }
          }

THE Backend SHALL implement AI tracking control via model-specific HTTP APIs. WHEN a camera's model is set to a known supported model (not \"Generic\"), THE `CameraService` SHALL use the model-specific driver to send AI tracking commands. FOR the Tongveo NVS20A-4KN model, THE Backend SHALL send HTTP POST requests to the camera's web interface at `http://{viscaHost}/api/aiControl` with JSON body: `{ \"ai_on\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_enable\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_mode\": \"1\", \"ai_auto_zoom\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_auto_tilt\": \"1\"|\"0\" }`. The `ai_on` and `ai_enable` fields map to the `ai-tracking` toggle (both \"1\" when enabled, both \"0\" when disabled). The `ai_auto_zoom` field maps to the `ai-tracking-zoom` toggle. The `ai_auto_tilt` field maps to the `ai-tracking-tilt` toggle. HTTP requests SHALL include the configured cookie in the `Cookie` header. WHEN enabling AI tracking, THE Backend SHALL immediately follow the `aiControl` request with a target selection command: HTTP POST to `http://{viscaHost}/api/setPTZCmd` with JSON body `{ \"Channel\": 0, \"PtzCmd\": 15, \"param1\": 7, \"param2\": 0, \"ID\": \"{configured credential ID}\" }`. This tells the camera to track the first detected subject. THE Backend SHALL NOT send the `setPTZCmd` command when disabling AI tracking — only the `aiControl` command is sent when turning AI off. If a configurable delay is needed between the two requests in the future, THE Backend SHALL support a `AI_ENABLE_DELAY_MS` code constant (default: 0) inserted between the `aiControl` and `setPTZCmd` calls. THE `CameraSocketModule` subscribes to this event to broadcast updates — consistent with the EventBus subscription pattern used by all other socket modules.\n\n13. THE Backend SHALL implement AI tracking control via model-specific HTTP APIs. WHEN a camera's model is set to a known supported model (not \"Generic\"), THE `CameraService` SHALL use the model-specific driver to send AI tracking commands. FOR the Tongveo NVS20A-4KN model, THE Backend SHALL send HTTP POST requests to the camera's web interface at `http://{viscaHost}/api/aiControl` with JSON body: `{ \"ai_on\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_enable\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_mode\": \"1\", \"ai_auto_zoom\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_auto_tilt\": \"1\"|\"0\" }`. The `ai_on` and `ai_enable` fields map to the `ai-tracking` toggle (both \"1\" when enabled, both \"0\" when disabled). The `ai_auto_zoom` field maps to the `ai-tracking-zoom` toggle. The `ai_auto_tilt` field maps to the `ai-tracking-tilt` toggle. HTTP requests SHALL include the configured cookie in the `Cookie` header. WHEN enabling AI tracking, THE Backend SHALL immediately follow the `aiControl` request with a target selection command: HTTP POST to `http://{viscaHost}/api/setPTZCmd` with JSON body `{ \"Channel\": 0, \"PtzCmd\": 15, \"param1\": 7, \"param2\": 0, \"ID\": \"{configured credential ID}\" }`. This tells the camera to track the first detected subject. THE Backend SHALL NOT send the `setPTZCmd` command when disabling AI tracking — only the `aiControl` command is sent when turning AI off. If a configurable delay is needed between the two requests in the future, THE Backend SHALL support a `AI_ENABLE_DELAY_MS` code constant (default: 0) inserted between the `aiControl` and `setPTZCmd` calls. IF the HTTP request fails (timeout, non-2xx response, network error), THE Backend SHALL emit a Toast-level notification: \"AI tracking command failed — check camera connection and credentials.\" and log the error at WARN level.",
                    "replaceAll": false
                  }
                }
              }
            },

        "message_id": "cf7ac7e6-c0b9-4e52-97e7-624c78798a20",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "All clean. Here's a summary of what was changed:\n\n**Changes applied:**\n\n1. **Feature rename:** `ai-tracking-zoom-disable` → `ai-tracking-zoom`, `ai-tracking-tilt-disable` → `ai-tracking-tilt` (positive semantics — enabled means AI *uses* that axis)\n2. **AI toggles restricted to ADMIN/AvPowerUser** — completely hidden from AvVolunteer (Req 3.6, 5.5, 5.6, 5.14)\n3. **Camera Model dropdown** added to admin (Req 7.1) — \"Generic\" or known models like \"Tongveo NVS20A-4KN\". AI features only available for non-Generic models.\n4. **Per-camera HTTP cookie + credential ID** stored encrypted in device config (Req 7.1) — admin obtains from browser dev tools, with stability warning\n5. **New Req 3.13** — Full AI tracking HTTP API protocol spec for Tongveo: `aiControl` endpoint for enable/disable with `ai_auto_zoom`/`ai_auto_tilt` fields, followed by `setPTZCmd` target selection (only on enable, never on disable), error handling, and future-proofed delay constant\n6. **Preset AI state applies regardless of role** — volunteer activating a preset that changes AI state works correctly (Req 6.4 clarification)\n7. **State payload updated** — `disableTilt`/`disableZoom` → `aiTilt`/`aiZoom`, added `capabilities` object (Req 3.12)\n8. **DB schema** — preset table uses `aiTilt`/`aiZoom` instead of `disableTilt`/`disableZoom` (Req 6.9)\n\n7 is easy to add later — just bump the `AI_ENABLE_DELAY_MS` constant if testing reveals the camera needs time between requests."
          }
        ]
      }
    },

              "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "# Design Document — Video Control and Preview\n\n## Overview\n\nThis document extends the existing system design with real-time video preview and NDI/VISCA camera control capabilities. It covers the preview streaming infrastructure, OBS preview widget, Camera HAL abstraction, camera control widget with virtual joystick, preset management, and admin configuration.\n\nThis is an extension document — it references and builds on the designs at `.kiro/specs/livestream-control-system/design.md` and `.kiro/specs/multi-platform-streaming/design.md`. Patterns, conventions, and components defined there remain authoritative unless explicitly superseded here.\n\n### What This Release Adds\n\n- Preview WebSocket infrastructure (fMP4 over dedicated WebSocket, MSE playback, fan-out)\n- FFmpeg hardware encoder auto-detection (VA-API, QSV, NVENC) with software fallback\n- OBS Preview widget (`obs-preview`) — 2×2, live stream/recording preview with audio toggle\n- `CameraControlInterface` — protocol-agnostic PTZ abstraction (NDI + VISCA implementations)\n- `CameraService` — manages camera connections, state polling, dead-man's switch\n- Camera widget (`camera`) — 6×4, live preview with virtual joystick PTZ controls\n- Camera preset system — database-stored with optional onboard camera mirroring\n- Admin camera device type with feature toggles, preset configuration modal\n- `CameraSocketModule` — Socket.io gateway for PTZ commands and state broadcast\n- NDI SDK dynamic loading with graceful degradation\n\n### Breaking Changes\n\n- **`device_connections` table**: `deviceType` CHECK constraint expanded to include `\"camera-ptz\"`. New nullable columns for camera-specific config: `ndiSourceName`, `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, `fovWideAngle`, `cameraFeatures`. Camera devices store `\"127.0.0.1\"` / `0` in the existing `host` / `port` NOT NULL columns (unused by cameras — camera-specific connections use the new columns). OBS devices gain a new nullable `ndiSourceName` column for NDI preview output.\n- **New table**: `camera_presets` for preset storage.\n- **`seed-dashboard.ts`**: Two new widget entries (OBS Preview at 2×2, Camera at 6×4); existing widget positions adjusted to avoid overlap.\n- **Caddy routing**: Both `Caddyfile` and `Caddyfile.dev` must add `/preview/*` to the backend route matcher (alongside `/api/*` and `/socket.io/*`). Without this, preview WebSocket upgrade requests are routed to the frontend and fail silently.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Extended Topology\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n  subgraph Frontend [packages/frontend]\n    ObsPreviewWidget[OBS Preview Widget]\n    CameraWidget[Camera Widget]\n    CameraModal[Camera Control Modal]\n    AdminDevices[Admin Device Management — modified]\n  end\n\n  subgraph Backend [packages/backend]\n    PreviewManager[PreviewStreamManager]\n    CameraService[CameraService]\n    CameraModule[CameraSocketModule]\n    NdiDriver[NdiCameraDriver]\n    ViscaDriver[ViscaCameraDriver]\n    ObsService[ObsService — existing]"
                }
              ],
              "status": "success"
            }
          }
        ],

                  {
                    "Text": "# Design Document — Video Control and Preview\n\n## Overview\n\nThis document extends the existing system design with real-time video preview and NDI/VISCA camera control capabilities. It covers the preview streaming infrastructure, OBS preview widget, Camera HAL abstraction, camera control widget with virtual joystick, preset management, and admin configuration.\n\nThis is an extension document — it references and builds on the designs at `.kiro/specs/livestream-control-system/design.md` and `.kiro/specs/multi-platform-streaming/design.md`. Patterns, conventions, and components defined there remain authoritative unless explicitly superseded here.\n\n### What This Release Adds\n\n- Preview WebSocket infrastructure (fMP4 over dedicated WebSocket, MSE playback, fan-out)\n- FFmpeg hardware encoder auto-detection (VA-API, QSV, NVENC) with software fallback\n- OBS Preview widget (`obs-preview`) — 2×2, live stream/recording preview with audio toggle\n- `CameraControlInterface` — protocol-agnostic PTZ abstraction (NDI + VISCA implementations)\n- `CameraService` — manages camera connections, state polling, dead-man's switch\n- Camera widget (`camera`) — 6×4, live preview with virtual joystick PTZ controls\n- Camera preset system — database-stored with optional onboard camera mirroring\n- Admin camera device type with feature toggles, preset configuration modal\n- `CameraSocketModule` — Socket.io gateway for PTZ commands and state broadcast\n- NDI SDK dynamic loading with graceful degradation\n\n### Breaking Changes\n\n- **`device_connections` table**: `deviceType` CHECK constraint expanded to include `\"camera-ptz\"`. New nullable columns for camera-specific config: `ndiSourceName`, `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, `fovWideAngle`, `cameraFeatures`. Camera devices store `\"127.0.0.1\"` / `0` in the existing `host` / `port` NOT NULL columns (unused by cameras — camera-specific connections use the new columns). OBS devices gain a new nullable `ndiSourceName` column for NDI preview output.\n- **New table**: `camera_presets` for preset storage.\n- **`seed-dashboard.ts`**: Two new widget entries (OBS Preview at 2×2, Camera at 6×4); existing widget positions adjusted to avoid overlap.\n- **Caddy routing**: Both `Caddyfile` and `Caddyfile.dev` must add `/preview/*` to the backend route matcher (alongside `/api/*` and `/socket.io/*`). Without this, preview WebSocket upgrade requests are routed to the frontend and fail silently.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Extended Topology\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n  subgraph Frontend [packages/frontend]\n    ObsPreviewWidget[OBS Preview Widget]\n    CameraWidget[Camera Widget]\n    CameraModal[Camera Control Modal]\n    AdminDevices[Admin Device Management — modified]\n  end\n\n  subgraph Backend [packages/backend]\n    PreviewManager[PreviewStreamManager]\n    CameraService[CameraService]\n    CameraModule[CameraSocketModule]\n    NdiDriver[NdiCameraDriver]\n    ViscaDriver[ViscaCameraDriver]\n    ObsService[ObsService — existing]"
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    },

                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "\n**Adaptive speed tied to zoom**: Prevents PTZ overshoot at telephoto without requiring the operator to manually adjust speed. The formula `speed * (1 - zoom * 0.7)` gives 100% at wide angle, 30% at full telephoto.\n\n**Hybrid preset storage**: Database-first with optional camera onboard mirroring. Database presets are camera-agnostic (survive camera replacement), store metadata cameras can't (toggle states), and have well-defined content. Onboard presets provide MotionSync smooth recall on cameras that support it.\n\n**NDI video via grandiose receiver → FFmpeg stdin pipe**: Rather than requiring the FFmpeg NDI input plugin (which requires separate compilation against the NDI SDK), video frames are received by `grandiose`'s receiver API in Node.js and piped to FFmpeg's stdin as raw frames. This keeps the FFmpeg dependency simple (standard package-manager install) and centralizes all NDI SDK interaction in one native module. The tradeoff is slightly higher CPU usage from the JS → pipe → FFmpeg path, but this is negligible compared to the transcoding work FFmpeg performs.\n\n**Cookie-based WebSocket authentication**: Preview WebSocket endpoints authenticate via the same HttpOnly JWT cookie used by Socket.io and REST. The browser sends cookies automatically on same-origin WebSocket upgrade requests routed through Caddy. This requires no frontend token handling and maintains consistency with the existing auth model — no token appears in URLs or logs.\n\n**Caddy routing requirement**: The reverse proxy must route `/preview/*` to the backend alongside `/api/*` and `/socket.io/*`. This is a deployment prerequisite documented in the breaking changes section.\n\n### EventBus Events\n\n```typescript\n// Camera — Internal Bus Events\nexport const BUS_CAMERA_STATE_CHANGED = \"bus:camera:state:changed\";\n\ninterface CameraEventMap {\n  [BUS_CAMERA_STATE_CHANGED]: { cameraId: string; state: CameraState };\n}\n```\n\n`CameraSocketModule.register(io)` subscribes to `BUS_CAMERA_STATE_CHANGED` and broadcasts `stc:camera:state:update` to all connected clients. This follows the same pattern as `ObsModule` subscribing to `BUS_OBS_STATE_CHANGED`.\n\n---\n\n## Database Schema\n\n### Modified: `device_connections`\n\n```sql\n-- Existing columns remain unchanged. New columns:\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN ndiSourceName TEXT; -- cameras: NDI source for video+PTZ; OBS: NDI output for preview\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN viscaHost TEXT; -- cameras only: optional VISCA IP for position polling\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN viscaPort INTEGER DEFAULT 5500; -- cameras only: optional VISCA port\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN fovWideAngle REAL DEFAULT 60.0; -- cameras only\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN cameraFeatures TEXT; -- cameras only: JSON array of enabled features\n```\n\nCamera devices store `\"127.0.0.1\"` / `0` in the existing `host` / `port` NOT NULL columns (these are used by OBS devices but irrelevant for cameras).\n\nSchema migration uses the existing ad-hoc column-check pattern: at startup, check for missing columns via `PRAGMA table_info(device_connections)` and add them if absent (same pattern as `migrateMetadataTemplates`). Validation of `deviceType` values is enforced at the route/TypeScript level, not via SQL CHECK constraint (SQLite doesn't support altering CHECK constraints on existing tables).\n\n### New: `camera_presets`\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE camera_presets (\n  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  cameraId TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES device_connections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  sortOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  storedOnCamera INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  cameraPresetSlot INTEGER,\n  pan REAL,\n  tilt REAL,\n  zoom REAL,\n  focus REAL,\n  autoFocus INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, -- boolean\n  aiTracking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  disableTilt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  disableZoom INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  createdAt TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_camera_presets_camera ON camera_presets(cameraId);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Backend Services\n\n### PreviewStreamManager (New)\n\nManages FFmpeg lifecycle, WebSocket fan-out, and hardware encoder selection.\n\n```typescript\ninterface PreviewStreamManager {\n  // Called at startup — probes FFmpeg encoders, caches result\n  initialize(): Promise<void>;\n\n  // WebSocket endpoint registration (called during Express setup)\n  registerEndpoints(server: HttpServer): void;\n\n  // Source availability (called by ObsService/CameraService)\n  setSourceAvailable(sourceId: string, available: boolean, inputUrl: string): void;\n\n  // Metrics\n  getActiveStreams(): number;\n  getSubscriberCount(sourceId: string): number;\n\n  destroy(): void;\n}\n\n// Internal types\ninterface PreviewSource {\n  sourceId: string;          // e.g., \"obs\", \"camera-{id}\"\n  inputUrl: string;          // e.g., \"rtmp://localhost:1935/live/stream\" or NDI pipe path\n  ffmpegProcess: ChildProcess | null;\n  subscribers: Set<WebSocket>;\n  initSegment: Buffer | null; // fMP4 init segment (moov atom) — sent to new subscribers"
                }
              ],
              "status": "success"
            }
          }

                  "data": "```\n\n---\n\n## Frontend — OBS Preview Widget\n\n### Zustand Slice\n\n```typescript\ninterface ObsPreviewSlice {\n  obsPreviewStatus: \"inactive\" | \"connecting\" | \"streaming\" | \"error\";\n  setObsPreviewStatus: (status: ObsPreviewSlice[\"obsPreviewStatus\"]) => void;\n}\n```\n\n### Widget: `ObsPreviewWidget`\n\n```\nWidgetContainer (title: \"OBS Preview\", connections: [{ label: \"Feed\", status }])\n├── VideoContainer (position: relative, 100% of content area)\n│   ├── <video> (object-fit: contain, centered)\n│   ├── MuteButton (bottom-right, 48×48, semi-transparent)\n│   └── InactiveOverlay (\"No Active Stream or Recording\" | \"Reconnecting...\")\n└── [Modal: StreamPreviewModal]\n    ├── <video> (same stream, larger, object-fit: contain)\n    ├── MuteButton (bottom-right, 48×48)\n    └── DismissButton\n```\n\n### Connection Status Derivation\n\n```typescript\nfunction deriveObsFeedStatus(wsState: WebSocketState, framesRecent: boolean, ndiSourceConfigured: boolean): ConnectionStatus[\"status\"] {\n  if (!ndiSourceConfigured) return \"inactive\";\n  if (wsState === \"connected\" && framesRecent) return \"healthy\";\n  return \"unhealthy\";\n}\n```\n\n### MSE Playback Hook: `usePreviewStream`\n\n```typescript\nfunction usePreviewStream(endpoint: string, enabled: boolean) {\n  // Returns: { videoRef, status, error }\n  // Manages: WebSocket lifecycle, MediaSource creation, SourceBuffer appending\n  // Buffer trim: removes segments > 2s old on each append\n  // Seek-to-live: if buffered.end - currentTime > 3s, seek to live edge\n  // Reconnect: exponential backoff 1s→2s→4s→10s max\n  // Auth: browser sends HttpOnly JWT cookie automatically on same-origin WS upgrade\n}\n```\n\nShared between OBS Preview and Camera Preview widgets.\n\n### Video Centering CSS\n\n```css\n.preview-video-container {\n  position: relative;\n  width: 100%;\n  height: 100%;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: center;\n  background: var(--color-surface);\n}\n.preview-video {\n  max-width: 100%;\n  max-height: 100%;\n  object-fit: contain;\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Backend Services — Camera\n\n### CameraControlInterface\n\n```typescript\ninterface CameraControlInterface {\n  panTiltSpeed(panSpeed: number, tiltSpeed: number): Promise<void>;\n  panTiltAbsolute(pan: number, tilt: number): Promise<void>;\n  zoomAbsolute(zoom: number): Promise<void>;\n  focusAuto(): Promise<void>;\n  focusManual(position: number): Promise<void>;\n  stop(): Promise<void>;\n  inquirePosition(): Promise<PositionInquiry>;\n  connect(): Promise<boolean>;\n  disconnect(): void;\n  isConnected(): boolean;\n}\n\ninterface PositionInquiry {\n  pan: number | null;\n  tilt: number | null;\n  zoom: number | null;\n  focus: number | null;\n  autoFocus: boolean | null;\n}\n```\n\n### NdiCameraDriver\n\n```typescript\nclass NdiCameraDriver implements CameraControlInterface {\n  // Uses grandiose (dynamic import) for NDI SDK access\n  // PTZ commands: NDIlib_recv_ptz_pan_tilt_speed, NDIlib_recv_ptz_pan_tilt, etc.\n  // inquirePosition(): returns last-commanded values (NDI has no position query)\n  // connect(): NDI find + receive + ptz_is_supported check\n  // Video: provides raw frame data via a readable stream that PreviewStreamManager\n  //   pipes to FFmpeg's stdin (format: raw UYVY/BGRA frames, resolution from NDI source)\n  //   This avoids requiring the FFmpeg NDI input plugin to be compiled separately.\n  private lastCommanded: PositionInquiry;\n  private receiver: NdiReceiver | null;\n}\n```\n\n### ViscaCameraDriver\n\n```typescript\nclass ViscaCameraDriver {\n  // Used ONLY for position inquiry — PTZ commands always go via NDI\n  // Raw TCP socket to camera (viscaHost:viscaPort)\n  // inquirePosition(): CAM_PanTiltPosInq + CAM_ZoomPosInq + CAM_FocusPosInq + CAM_FocusAFModeInq\n  // Handles VISCA ACK/Completion/Error responses\n  // Probe: CAM_PowerInq to verify connectivity\n  private socket: net.Socket;\n  private host: string;\n  private port: number;\n}\n```\n\n**VISCA value normalization** (16-bit raw ↔ normalized float):\n\n```typescript\n// Pan: raw range camera-specific (e.g., 0x0000–0xFFFF maps to -1.0–1.0)\n// Zoom: raw 0x0000 (wide) – 0x4000 (tele) maps to 0.0–1.0\n// Focus: raw 0x0000 (near) – 0x4000 (far) maps to 0.0–1.0\nfunction normalizeViscaPan(raw: number, maxRaw: number): number {\n  return (raw / maxRaw) * 2 - 1; // center = 0\n}\nfunction denormalizeViscaPan(normalized: number, maxRaw: number): number {\n  return Math.round((normalized + 1) / 2 * maxRaw);\n}\n```\n\n### CameraService\n\n```typescript"

number) {\n  const session: MoveSession = {\n    cameraId,\n    lastKeepalive: Date.now(),\n    timeout: setTimeout(() => deadManStop(cameraId), KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS),\n    currentPan: pan,\n    currentTilt: tilt,\n  };\n  activeSessions.set(cameraId, session);\n  issueMove(cameraId, pan, tilt);\n}\n\nfunction onKeepalive(cameraId: string, pan: number, tilt: number) {\n  const session =                   "kind": "text",
                  "data": "\n```typescript\n// Thresholds defined in rem, converted at runtime using computed root font size\nconst MIN_EXPANDED_WIDTH_REM = 30;  // 30rem — enough for video + controls side-by-side\nconst MIN_EXPANDED_HEIGHT_REM = 20; // 20rem — enough for joystick + presets stacked\nconst BASE_FONT_SIZE = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize);\n\nfunction useWidgetMode(containerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>) {\n  const [mode, setMode] = useState<\"compact\" | \"expanded\">(\"compact\");\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const observer = new ResizeObserver(([entry]) => {\n      const { width, height } = entry.contentRect;\n      const fontSize = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize);\n      setMode(\n        width >= MIN_EXPANDED_WIDTH_REM * fontSize &&\n        height >= MIN_EXPANDED_HEIGHT_REM * fontSize\n          ? \"expanded\" : \"compact\"\n      );\n    });\n    if (containerRef.current) observer.observe(containerRef.current);\n    return () => observer.disconnect();\n  }, []);\n  return mode;\n}\n```\n\n### Virtual Joystick: `PtzJoystick`\n\n```typescript\ninterface PtzJoystickProps {\n  onMoveStart: (panSpeed: number, tiltSpeed: number) => void;\n  onMove: (panSpeed: number, tiltSpeed: number) => void;\n  onMoveEnd: () => void;\n  disabled?: boolean;\n  panEnabled?: boolean;\n  tiltEnabled?: boolean;\n}\n```\n\nImplementation:\n- Circular container, `min-width: 7.5rem; min-height: 7.5rem`\n- Track touch/mouse position relative to center\n- Compute angle (`atan2`) and distance (clamped to radius)\n- Dead-zone: 15% of radius → treat as (0, 0)\n- Convert to pan/tilt speeds: `panSpeed = cos(angle) * distance`, `tiltSpeed = -sin(angle) * distance`\n- Quantize to 0.05 increments before emitting\n- Only emit if quantized value differs from last emission\n- Visual: indicator dot tracks finger position, snaps back to center on release\n\n```typescript\nconst DEAD_ZONE = 0.15;\nconst QUANTIZE_STEP = 0.05;\n\nfunction computeJoystickOutput(dx: number, dy: number, radius: number) {\n  const distance = Math.min(Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) / radius, 1.0);\n  if (distance < DEAD_ZONE) return { pan: 0, tilt: 0 };\n  const angle = Math.atan2(-dy, dx); // Y inverted for screen coords\n  const speed = (distance - DEAD_ZONE) / (1 - DEAD_ZONE); // remap post-deadzone to 0–1\n  const pan = Math.cos(angle) * speed;\n  const tilt = Math.sin(angle) * speed;\n  return {\n    pan: quantize(pan, QUANTIZE_STEP),\n    tilt: quantize(tilt, QUANTIZE_STEP),\n  };\n}\n\nfunction quantize(value: number, step: number): number {\n  return Math.round(value / step) * step;\n}\n```\n\n### Keepalive Timer Hook: `usePtzMove`\n\n```typescript\nfunction usePtzMove(cameraId: string) {\n  const intervalRef = useRef<number>();\n  const lastSent = useRef({ pan: 0, tilt: 0 });\n\n  function startMove(pan: number, tilt: number) {\n    socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_MOVE_START, { cameraId, pan, tilt });\n    lastSent.current = { pan, tilt };\n    intervalRef.current = setInterval(() => {\n      socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_MOVE_KEEPALIVE, { cameraId, ...lastSent.current });\n    }, 200);\n  }\n\n  function updateMove(pan: number, tilt: number) {\n    lastSent.current = { pan, tilt };\n    // Next keepalive will carry updated values\n  }\n\n  function endMove() {\n    clearInterval(intervalRef.current);\n    socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_MOVE_STOP, { cameraId });\n  }\n\n  return { startMove, updateMove, endMove };\n}\n```\n\n### Zoom Slider\n\nVertical `<input type=\"range\">` rotated 90° via CSS transform. Value 0 (bottom, wide) to 1 (top, telephoto). On change, emits `CTS_CAMERA_ZOOM_SET`. Reflects server state from `cameraStates[id].position.zoom`.\n\n```css\n.zoom-slider {\n  writing-mode: vertical-lr;\n  direction: rtl; /* 1.0 at top */\n  min-height: 10rem;\n  width: 2.75rem;\n}\n```\n\n### Double-Tap-to-Center Handler\n\n```typescript\nconst DOUBLE_TAP_THRESHOLD_MS = 400;\n\nfunction useDoubleTapToCenter(cameraId: string, cameraState: CameraState) {\n  const lastTapTime = useRef(0);\n\n  function handleTap(e: React.MouseEvent | React.TouchEvent) {\n    const now = Date.now();\n    if (now - lastTapTime.current > DOUBLE_TAP_THRESHOLD_MS) {\n      // First tap — just record time\n      lastTapTime.current = now;\n      return;\n    }\n    // Second tap within threshold — use this tap's location\n    lastTapTime.current = 0; // reset\n\n    if (cameraState.aiTracking) {\n      showToast(\"Tap-to-center is disabled when AI Tracking is active.\");\n      return;\n    }\n    const rect = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect();\n    const clientX = \"touches\" in e ? e.changedTouches[0].clientX : e.clientX;\n    const clientY = \"touches\" in e ? e.changedTouches[0].clientY : e.clientY;\n    const offsetX = ((clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 2 - 1; // -1 to 1\n    const offsetY = ((clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 2 - 1;\n    const adjustedY = cameraState.disableTilt ? 0 : offsetY;\n    socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_TAP_TO_CENTER, { cameraId, offsetX, offsetY: adjustedY });\n  }\n\n  return handleTap;\n}\n```\n\nThe video container must set `touch-action: manipulation` to suppress browser double-tap-to-zoom.\n\n---\n\n## Frontend — Camera Presets\n\n### Preset List Component\n\n```\nPresetList (max-height: 3 × 2.75rem, overflow-y: auto)\n├── PresetRow\n│   ├── PresetName (text, truncate with ellipsis)\n│   └── ActivateButton (min-height: 2.75rem)\n│       States: default | highlighted (color-primary, active preset)\n├── PresetRow ...\n└── PresetRow ...\n```\n\n### Preset Activation Flow\n\n```typescript\nfunction handleActivatePreset(cameraId: string, presetId: string, presetName: string) {\n  socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PRESET_ACTIVATE, { cameraId, presetId });\n  showToast(`Moving to ${presetName}`);\n  // Backend broadcasts activePresetId immediately — button highlights on state update\n  // Volunteer relies on preview to verify camera arrived\n  // New preset tap or manual movement clears the active indicator\n}\n```\n\nActive preset clears when `CameraService` detects any manual command (move, zoom, focus, double-tap-to-center, toggle change) on that camera. No timeout, no disabled state — matches a physical remote control mental model.\n\n---\n\n## Frontend — Admin Camera Configuration\n\n### Device Detail Panel (Camera Type)\n\n```\nCameraDeviceDetail\n├── ConnectionSection\n│   ├── LabelInput\n│   ├── NdiSourceNameInput (required)\n│   ├── ViscaSection (collapsible, \"Position Polling (Recommended)\")\n│   │   ├── ViscaEnabledToggle\n│   │   ├── ViscaHostInput (visible when enabled)\n│   │   └── ViscaPortInput (visible when enabled, default 5500)\n│   ├── FovWideAngleInput (number, default 60, suffix \"°\")\n│   ├── NdiOnlyNote (visible when VISCA disabled)\n│   └── ProbeResult (green checkmark | red X + reason)\n├── FeaturesSection\n│   ├── FeatureToggle (\"pan\")"

// 20rem — enough for joystick + presets stacked\nconst BASE_FONT_SIZE = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize);\n\nfunction useWidgetMode(containerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>) {\n  const [mode, setMode] = useState<\"compact\" | \"expanded\">(\"compact\");\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const observer = new ResizeObserver(([entry]) => {\n      const { width, height } = entry.contentRect;\n      const fontSize = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize);\n      setMode(\n        width >= MIN_EXPANDED_WIDTH_REM * fontSize &&\n        height >= MIN_EXPANDED_HEIGHT_REM * fontSize\n          ? \"expanded\" : \"compact\"\n      );\n    });\n    if (containerRef.current) observer.observe(containerRef.current);\n    return () => observer.disconnect();\n  }, []);\n  return mode;\n}\n```\n\n### Virtual Joystick: `PtzJoystick`\n\n```typescript\ninterface PtzJoystickProps {\n  onMoveStart: (panSpeed: number, tiltSpeed: number) => void;\n  onMove: (panSpeed: number, tiltSpeed: number) => void;\n  onMoveEnd: () => void;\n  disabled?: boolean;\n  panEnabled?: boolean;\n  tiltEnabled?: boolean;\n}\n```\n\nImplementation:\n- Circular container, `min-width: 7.5rem; min-height: 7.5rem`\n- Track touch/mouse position relative to center\n- Compute angle (`atan2`) and distance (clamped to radius)\n- Dead-zone: 15% of radius → treat as (0, 0)\n- Convert to pan/tilt speeds: `panSpeed = cos(angle) * distance`, `tiltSpeed = -sin(angle) * distance`\n- Quantize to 0.05 increments before emitting\n- Only emit if quantized value differs from last emission\n- Visual: indicator dot tracks finger position, snaps back to center on release\n\n```typescript\nconst DEAD_ZONE = 0.15;\nconst QUANTIZE_STEP = 0.05;\n\nfunction computeJoystickOutput(dx: number, dy: number, radius: number) {\n  const distance = Math.min(Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) / radius, 1.0);\n  if (distance < DEAD_ZONE) return { pan: 0, tilt: 0 };\n  const angle = Math.atan2(-dy, dx); // Y inverted for screen coords\n  const speed = (distance - DEAD_ZONE) / (1 - DEAD_ZONE); // remap post-deadzone to 0–1\n  const pan = Math.cos(angle) * speed;\n  const tilt = Math.sin(angle) * speed;\n  return {\n    pan: quantize(pan, QUANTIZE_STEP),\n    tilt: quantize(tilt, QUANTIZE_STEP),\n  };\n}\n\nfunction quantize(value: number, step: number): number {\n  return Math.round(value / step) * step;\n}\n```\n\n### Keepalive Timer Hook: `usePtzMove`\n\n```typescript\nfunction usePtzMove(cameraId: string) {\n  const intervalRef = useRef<number>();\n  const lastSent = useRef({ pan: 0, tilt: 0 });\n\n  function startMove(pan: number, tilt: number) {\n    socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_MOVE_START, { cameraId, pan, tilt });\n    lastSent.current = { pan, tilt };\n    intervalRef.current = setInterval(() => {\n      socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_MOVE_KEEPALIVE, { cameraId, ...lastSent.current });\n    }, 200);\n  }\n\n  function updateMove(pan: number, tilt: number) {\n    lastSent.current = { pan, tilt };\n    // Next keepalive will carry updated values\n  }\n\n  function endMove() {\n    clearInterval(intervalRef.current);\n    socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_MOVE_STOP, { cameraId });\n  }\n\n  return { startMove, updateMove, endMove };\n}\n```\n\n### Zoom Slider\n\nVertical `<input type=\"range\">` rotated 90° via CSS transform. Value 0 (bottom, wide) to 1 (top, telephoto). On change, emits `CTS_CAMERA_ZOOM_SET`. Reflects server state from `cameraStates[id].position.zoom`.\n\n```css\n.zoom-slider {\n  writing-mode: vertical-lr;\n  direction: rtl; /* 1.0 at top */\n  min-height: 10rem;\n  width: 2.75rem;\n}\n```\n\n### Double-Tap-to-Center Handler\n\n```typescript\nconst DOUBLE_TAP_THRESHOLD_MS = 400;\n\nfunction useDoubleTapToCenter(cameraId: string, cameraState: CameraState) {\n  const lastTapTime = useRef(0);\n\n  function handleTap(e: React.MouseEvent | React.TouchEvent) {\n    const now = Date.now();\n    if (now - lastTapTime.current > DOUBLE_TAP_THRESHOLD_MS) {\n      // First tap — just record time\n      lastTapTime.current = now;\n      return;\n    }\n    // Second tap within threshold — use this tap's location\n    lastTapTime.current = 0; // reset\n\n    if (cameraState.aiTracking) {\n      showToast(\"Tap-to-center is disabled when AI Tracking is active.\");\n      return;\n    }\n    const rect = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect();\n    const clientX = \"touches\" in e ? e.changedTouches[0].clientX : e.clientX;\n    const clientY = \"touches\" in e ? e.changedTouches[0].clientY : e.clientY;\n    const offsetX = ((clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 2 - 1; // -1 to 1\n    const offsetY = ((clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 2 - 1;\n    const adjustedY = cameraState.disableTilt ? 0 : offsetY;\n    socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_TAP_TO_CENTER, { cameraId, offsetX, offsetY: adjustedY });\n  }\n\n  return handleTap;\n}\n```\n\nThe video container must set `touch-action: manipulation` to suppress browser double-tap-to-zoom.\n\n---\n\n## Frontend — Camera Presets\n\n### Preset List Component\n\n```\nPresetList (max-height: 3 × 2.75rem, overflow-y: auto)\n├── PresetRow\n│   ├── PresetName (text, truncate with ellipsis)\n│   └── ActivateButton (min-height: 2.75rem)\n│       States: default | highlighted (color-primary, active preset)\n├── PresetRow ...\n└── PresetRow ...\n```\n\n### Preset Activation Flow\n\n```typescript\nfunction handleActivatePreset(cameraId: string, presetId: string, presetName: string) {\n  socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PRESET_ACTIVATE, { cameraId, presetId });\n  showToast(`Moving to ${presetName}`);\n  // Backend broadcasts activePresetId immediately — button highlights on state update\n  // Volunteer relies on preview to verify camera arrived\n  // New preset tap or manual movement clears the active indicator\n}\n```\n\nActive preset clears when `CameraService` detects any manual command (move, zoom, focus, double-tap-to-center, toggle change) on that camera. No timeout, no disabled state — matches a physical remote control mental model.\n\n---\n\n## Frontend — Admin Camera Configuration\n\n### Device Detail Panel (Camera Type)\n\n```\nCameraDeviceDetail\n├── ConnectionSection\n│   ├── LabelInput\n│   ├── NdiSourceNameInput (required)\n│   ├── ViscaSection (collapsible, \"Position Polling (Recommended)\")\n│   │   ├── ViscaEnabledToggle\n│   │   ├── ViscaHostInput (visible when enabled)\n│   │   └── ViscaPortInput (visible when enabled, default 5500)\n│   ├── FovWideAngleInput (number, default 60, suffix \"°\")\n│   ├── NdiOnlyNote (visible when VISCA disabled)\n│   └── ProbeResult (green checkmark | red X + reason)\n├── FeaturesSection\n│   ├── FeatureToggle (\"pan\")"
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }

Note that `ndiSourceName` on OBS device_connections enables OBS preview via NDI (decoupled from RTMP relay).\n- **§7 (Event Naming)**: Add exception note that `/preview/*` WebSocket endpoints are raw binary transport — no event naming convention applies.\n\n---\n\n## FFmpeg NDI Input Arguments\n\nWhen receiving NDI frames via grandiose and piping to FFmpeg stdin, the input arguments must be derived at runtime from the NDI source's actual format:\n\n```typescript\nfunction buildNdiInputArgs(ndiFormat: NdiFrameFormat): string[] {\n  // ndiFormat is queried from the first received frame's metadata\n  return [\n    \"-f\", \"rawvideo\",\n    \"-pix_fmt\", ndiFormat.fourCC === \"UYVY\" ? \"uyvy422\" : \"bgra\",\n    \"-s\", `${ndiFormat.width}x${ndiFormat.height}`,\n    \"-r\", String(ndiFormat.frameRateN / ndiFormat.frameRateD),\n    \"-i\", \"pipe:0\",  // read raw frames from stdin\n  ];\n}\n```\n\nBackpressure handling: if FFmpeg's stdin pipe returns `false` on write (pipe full), the frame is dropped. This prevents the grandiose receiver's internal buffer from growing unbounded when FFmpeg can't keep up (e.g., during hardware encoder initialization).\n\n---\n\n## Seed Script Updates\n\n### `seed-dashboard.ts` Changes\n\n```typescript\nconst OBS_PREVIEW_WIDGET_ID = \"obs-preview\";\nconst CAMERA_WIDGET_ID = \"camera\";\n\n// Existing widgets repositioned:\n// OBS controls: col=0, row=0, 3×2 (unchanged position)\n// Lower Thirds: col=3, row=0, 3×2 (unchanged position)\n\n// New widgets:\n// OBS Preview: col=6, row=0, 2×2\n// Camera: col=0, row=2, 6×4\n\nconst newWidgets = [\n  {\n    id: `${DASHBOARD_ID}-${OBS_PREVIEW_WIDGET_ID}`,\n    dashboardId: DASHBOARD_ID,\n    widgetId: OBS_PREVIEW_WIDGET_ID,\n    title: \"OBS Preview\","
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }

CameraFeature type: rename values\n4. CameraState/CameraPreset: rename fields, add `capabilities`\n5. Socket events: rename `disable-tilt`/`disable-zoom` → `ai-tilt`/`ai-zoom`\n6. Admin panel: add Camera Model dropdown, AI config section, drag-to-reorder presets\n7. Add AI tracking HTTP driver section\n8. Widget component tree: rename toggles\n9. Double-tap handler: fix `disableTilt` → `aiTilt` (inverted logic)"

                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "    if (!cameraState.capabilities.tapToCenter) {\n      showToast(\"Tap-to-center requires VISCA position tracking. Use the joystick or activate a preset.\");\n      return;\n    }\n    if (cameraState.aiTracking) {\n      showToast(\"Tap-to-center is disabled when AI Tracking is active.\");\n      return;\n    }\n    const rect = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect();\n    const clientX = \"touches\" in e ? e.changedTouches[0].clientX : e.clientX;\n    const clientY = \"touches\" in e ? e.changedTouches[0].clientY : e.clientY;\n    const offsetX = ((clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 2 - 1; // -1 to 1\n    const offsetY = ((clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 2 - 1;\n    const adjustedY = !cameraState.aiTilt ? 0 : offsetY; // if AI doesn't control tilt, neither does tap\n    socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_TAP_TO_CENTER, { cameraId, offsetX, offsetY: adjustedY });",
                "oldStr": "    if (cameraState.aiTracking) {\n      showToast(\"Tap-to-center is disabled when AI Tracking is active.\");\n      return;\n    }\n    const rect = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect();\n    const clientX = \"touches\" in e ? e.changedTouches[0].clientX : e.clientX;\n    const clientY = \"touches\" in e ? e.changedTouches[0].clientY : e.clientY;\n    const offsetX = ((clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 2 - 1; // -1 to 1\n    const offsetY = ((clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 2 - 1;\n    const adjustedY = cameraState.disableTilt ? 0 : offsetY;\n    socket.emit(CTS_CAMERA_PTZ_TAP_TO_CENTER, { cameraId, offsetX, offsetY: adjustedY });",

                "newStr": "### Device Detail Panel (Camera Type)\n\n```\nCameraDeviceDetail\n├── ConnectionSection\n│   ├── LabelInput\n│   ├── CameraModelSelect (\"Generic\" | \"Tongveo NVS20A-4KN\")\n│   ├── NdiSourceNameInput (required)\n│   ├── ViscaSection (collapsible, \"Position Polling (Recommended)\")\n│   │   ├── ViscaEnabledToggle\n│   │   ├── ViscaHostInput (visible when enabled)\n│   │   └── ViscaPortInput (visible when enabled, default 5500)\n│   ├── FovWideAngleInput (number, default 60, suffix \"°\")\n│   ├── NdiOnlyNote (visible when VISCA disabled)\n│   ├── AiTrackingConfigSection (visible when model ≠ \"Generic\")\n│   │   ├── AiHttpCookieInput (password-masked, stored encrypted)\n│   │   ├── AiCredentialIdInput (password-masked, stored encrypted)\n│   │   └── CautionNote (\"Cookie may expire if camera reboots...\")\n│   └── ProbeResult (green checkmark | red X + reason)\n├── FeaturesSection\n│   ├── FeatureToggle (\"pan\")\n│   ├── FeatureToggle (\"tilt\")\n│   ├── FeatureToggle (\"zoom\")\n│   ├── FeatureToggle (\"focus\")\n│   ├── FeatureToggle (\"ai-tracking\") — only visible when model ≠ \"Generic\"\n│   ├── FeatureToggle (\"ai-tracking-tilt\") — only visible when model ≠ \"Generic\"\n│   └── FeatureToggle (\"ai-tracking-zoom\") — only visible when model ≠ \"Generic\"\n└── PresetsSection\n    ├── PresetRow (draggable, name, badge: \"On Camera\" | \"Software Only\", Edit/Delete)\n    ├── PresetRow ...\n    └── AddPresetButton\n```\n\nDrag-to-reorder: preset rows support drag handles. On drop, the frontend sends the new order to the backend which assigns `sortOrder` values (0, 1, 2...) based on position.\n\n### Preset Configuration Modal\n\n```\nPresetConfigModal (title: \"Configure Preset\" | \"Edit Preset: {name}\")\n├── NameInput\n├── StoreOnCameraToggle\n│   └── SlotNumberInput (visible when toggled on)\n├── LiveVideoPreview (same camera preview stream)\n├── PTZ Controls (same VirtualJoystick, ZoomSlider, toggles as widget)\n├── CapturePositionButton\n│   └── CapturedSummary (\"Pan: -0.32, Tilt: 0.15, Zoom: 0.45, Focus: N/A\")\n├── CancelButton\n└── SaveButton\n```",

        "message_id": "451646d5-c0b7-4ea1-9c8a-1cb3ef5ea1e6",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Now add the AI Tracking HTTP driver section after the ViscaCameraDriver:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "tooluse_eTYBfu7hbzPcLrMy5JH02H",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Add AI Tracking HTTP driver section after ViscaCameraDriver",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "**VISCA value normalization** (16-bit raw ↔ normalized float):\n\n```typescript\n// Pan: raw range camera-specific (e.g., 0x0000–0xFFFF maps to -1.0–1.0)\n// Zoom: raw 0x0000 (wide) – 0x4000 (tele) maps to 0.0–1.0\n// Focus: raw 0x0000 (near) – 0x4000 (far) maps to 0.0–1.0\nfunction normalizeViscaPan(raw: number, maxRaw: number): number {\n  return (raw / maxRaw) * 2 - 1; // center = 0\n}\nfunction denormalizeViscaPan(normalized: number, maxRaw: number): number {\n  return Math.round((normalized + 1) / 2 * maxRaw);\n}\n```\n\n### AiTrackingDriver (Model-Specific)\n\nHandles AI tracking control via HTTP for known camera models. Only instantiated when `cameraModel !== \"generic\"`.\n\n```typescript\ninterface AiTrackingDriver {\n  setAiState(enabled: boolean, aiTilt: boolean, aiZoom: boolean): Promise<void>;\n}\n\nclass TongveoAiDriver implements AiTrackingDriver {\n  private baseUrl: string;   // http://{viscaHost}\n  private cookie: string;    // from device config (decrypted)\n  private credentialId: string; // from device config (decrypted)\n\n  async setAiState(enabled: boolean, aiTilt: boolean, aiZoom: boolean): Promise<void> {\n    // Step 1: Set AI control state\n    await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}/api/aiControl`, {\n      method: \"POST\",\n      headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\", \"Cookie\": this.cookie },\n      body: JSON.stringify({\n        ai_on: enabled ? \"1\" : \"0\",\n        ai_enable: enabled ? \"1\" : \"0\",\n        ai_mode: \"1\",\n        ai_auto_zoom: aiZoom ? \"1\" : \"0\",\n        ai_auto_tilt: aiTilt ? \"1\" : \"0\",\n      }),\n    });\n\n    // Step 2: ONLY when enabling — select first tracking target\n    // DO NOT call setPTZCmd when disabling AI\n    if (enabled) {\n      await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}/api/setPTZCmd`, {\n        method: \"POST\",\n        headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\", \"Cookie\": this.cookie },\n        body: JSON.stringify({\n          Channel: 0,\n          PtzCmd: 15,\n          param1: 7,\n          param2: 0,\n          ID: this.credentialId,\n        }),\n      });\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nconst AI_ENABLE_DELAY_MS = 0; // Increase if camera needs time between aiControl and setPTZCmd\n```\n\nThe `CameraService` calls `aiDriver.setAiState()` when processing `cts:camera:ai-tracking:set`, `cts:camera:ai-tilt:set`, or `cts:camera:ai-zoom:set` events. For tilt/zoom toggle changes while AI is already enabled, the full `setAiState()` is called with the updated values (camera applies all fields atomically).",
                "oldStr": "**VISCA value normalization** (16-bit raw ↔ normalized float):\n\n```typescript\n// Pan: raw range camera-specific (e.g., 0x0000–0xFFFF maps to -1.0–1.0)\n// Zoom: raw 0x0000 (wide) – 0x4000 (tele) maps to 0.0–1.0\n// Focus: raw 0x0000 (near) – 0x4000 (far) maps to 0.0–1.0\nfunction normalizeViscaPan(raw: number, maxRaw: number): number {\n  return (raw / maxRaw) * 2 - 1; // center = 0\n}\nfunction denormalizeViscaPan(normalized: number, maxRaw: number): number {\n  return Math.round((normalized + 1) / 2 * maxRaw);\n}\n```",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/design.md"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }

            "data": "Design doc is updated. All changes are consistent between requirements and design:\n\n**Design doc updates applied:**\n1. DB schema: `disableTilt`/`disableZoom` → `aiTilt`/`aiZoom`; added `cameraModel`, `aiHttpCookie`, `aiCredentialId` columns\n2. `CameraService` interface: `setDisableTilt`/`setDisableZoom` → `setAiTilt`/`setAiZoom`\n3. `CameraState`: renamed fields, added `capabilities: { tapToCenter }`, added `CameraModel` type\n4. `CameraFeature` type: updated enum values\n5. `CameraPreset`: renamed fields\n6. New `AiTrackingDriver` section with `TongveoAiDriver` HTTP implementation (aiControl + setPTZCmd, with explicit \"DO NOT call setPTZCmd when disabling\" comment)\n7. Widget component tree: renamed toggles, added role annotations\n8. Admin panel: added Camera Model dropdown, AI config section with cookie/credential inputs, drag-to-reorder presets (removed SortOrderInput)\n9. Socket events: renamed constants\n10. REST API: updated `PresetBody`, added reorder endpoint\n11. Double-tap handler: added `tapToCenter` capability check, fixed `aiTilt` logic (inverted from old `disableTilt`)\n12. Breaking changes and \"What This Release Adds\" sections updated"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "Prompt",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "4a4f960c-ee02-4aa5-8abf-a61f91c64e31",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "1. The design say that we're going to add new nullable columns for the camera-ptz instead of using the metadata field like I believe it was designed for. We should just put all those fields into the metadata JSON blob.\n2. Should we use the metadata for the presets as well? We could in the metadata have `presets: [ {...}, {...}]` where the objects match what is described in the current camera_presets table.\n3. The design says we should alter the connections table to add a viscaHost and viscaPort column. We should just reuse the host and port columns that already exist.\n4. Why do we have ndiAvailable in our Camera Widget Zustand slice? NDI is required, so what would use this information?\n5. In the CameraWidget, we should not hide the dropdown if there's only one value. We should just have it disabled.\n6. In the CameraWidget expanded mode, why don't we have the ConnectingOverlay across the controls as well? Right now it's only over the video preview.\n7. We shouldn't be using input type=\"range\" for the zoom slider, we should be using ion-range. Double check we don't have any other base elements that should be ion elements\n8. Remove the caution note for the AiTrackingConfigSection. The warnings just need to be in the setup docs.\n9. Does it make sense to add as many cts:camera commands as we have, or should we make them act more like a state, where anything undefined is treated as not being changed. What's a more common pattern here? Do more commands add higher complexity, lower complexity, or no change for our overall code?"
          }
        ],
        "meta": {
          "timestamp": 1780800191
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "AssistantMessage",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "cc129988-9961-44ad-974e-556c8aabf0db",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "\nGood questions. Let me address each:\n\n**1. Metadata JSON blob instead of new columns:**\n\nYou're right. Looking at the existing schema, `device_connections` already has a `metadata` JSON column designed for device-type-specific fields. Camera config (ndiSourceName, fovWideAngle, cameraModel, cameraFeatures, aiHttpCookie, aiCredentialId) should go there rather than adding 7+ nullable columns that only cameras use. I'll fix this.\n\n**2. Presets in metadata vs. separate table:**\n\nI'd recommend keeping presets in a separate table for these reasons:\n- Presets have their own CRUD lifecycle (create/edit/delete/reorder independently of the device config)\n- A separate table gives us indexing, cascade delete, and cleaner queries\n- The metadata blob would become very large with multiple presets each containing 12+ fields\n- Preset reorder is a `PUT /presets/order` — surgically updating a nested array in a JSON blob requires read-modify-write (race condition prone in SQLite without row locks)\n\nThe metadata JSON blob works well for config that changes rarely and is always read/written as a unit. Presets are more like child entities with their own lifecycles.\n\n**3. Reuse host/port for VISCA:**\n\nGood catch. Since cameras use NDI as the primary protocol and VISCA is just for position polling (same IP, different port), we can store the camera's IP in `host` and the VISCA port in `port`. The `ndiSourceName` goes in metadata. This eliminates the \"store 127.0.0.1/0\" hack entirely. When VISCA is not configured, `host` and `port` would be... hmm, but those columns are NOT NULL. We'd need a sentinel value still for cameras without VISCA. OR we make VISCA optional by checking if `host` is empty string vs. an actual IP. What's cleaner: empty string sentinel, or just always requiring a host (even if VISCA isn't used, the camera has an IP)?\n\nActually — the camera always has an IP (it's on the network for NDI), and the AI HTTP API also uses that same IP. So `host` = camera's IP (always populated), `port` = VISCA port (5500 default, used if VISCA is enabled). Whether VISCA polling is enabled can be a boolean in metadata (`viscaEnabled: true/false`). This is clean.\n\n**4. ndiAvailable in Zustand:**\n\nYou're right — since NDI is now required for all cameras (Req 3.4 says cameras without NDI are not supported), and if NDI isn't available no cameras will even appear, this flag is redundant for the camera widget. It was there from the earlier design where NDI was optional. It should be removed from the camera slice. The only place `ndiAvailable` matters is the admin page (to show \"NDI SDK not installed\" warning) — and that can come from the initial state payload without being in the camera zustand slice.\n\n**5. Disabled dropdown vs hidden:**\n\nMakes sense — disabled with one value is more consistent and tells the volunteer \"this is a camera selector, there's just one.\" I'll update.\n\n**6. ConnectingOverlay across controls in expanded mode:**\n\nGood point. If the camera is offline/connecting, the controls are non-functional anyway. Showing the overlay across the entire widget (video + controls) rather than just the video section makes it clear that nothing works until the connection is established. I'll update.\n\n**7. ion-range instead of input type=\"range\":**\n\nYou're right. For consistency with the Ionic component library used throughout. Let me check for other base elements that should be Ionic:\n- Zoom slider: `<input type=\"range\">` → `<ion-range>`\n- Focus slider: same fix\n- Camera model dropdown in admin: should be `<IonSelect>` (already described as IonSelect for the camera switcher)\n- Preset name input: should be `<IonInput>`\n- FOV input: `<IonInput type=\"number\">`\n- Toggle buttons are already specified as Ionic toggles ✓\n- Joystick: custom component (no Ionic equivalent) ✓\n\n**8. Remove caution note from admin UI:**\n\nWill do — keep it in setup docs only.\n\n**9. Many CTS commands vs. single state-update command:**\n\nCurrent approach: `cts:camera:zoom:set`, `cts:camera:focus:auto`, `cts:camera:focus:set`, `cts:camera:ai-tracking:set`, `cts:camera:ai-tilt:set`, `cts:camera:ai-zoom:set` — 6 separate events for what are all \"set a value on the camera.\"\n\n**Alternative: Single `cts:camera:set` with partial state:**\n```typescript\nsocket.emit(\"cts:camera:set\", { cameraId, zoom: 0.5 });\nsocket.emit(\"cts:camera:set\", { cameraId, aiTracking: true });\nsocket.emit(\"cts:camera:set\", { cameraId, focus: 0.3 });\n```\n\nAnything undefined = not changed. This is the pattern used by React's `setState` and most REST PATCH endpoints.\n\n**My recommendation: Consolidate.** Reasons:\n- Fewer event constants to maintain\n- The handler logic is the same either way (switch on which fields are present)\n- Presets already set multiple values atomically — the single-event pattern is more natural for that\n- Less surface area for typos in event names\n- The PTZ move events (`start`/`keepalive`/`stop`) should stay separate because they have fundamentally different semantics (continuous vs. fire-once)\n\nSo the final event set would be:\n- `cts:camera:ptz:move:start` / `keepalive` / `stop` — continuous movement (stays as-is)\n- `cts:camera:set` — fire-once state changes: `{ cameraId, zoom?, focus?, autoFocus?, aiTracking?, aiTilt?, aiZoom? }`\n- `cts:camera:preset:activate` — stays separate (has its own response flow with Toast)\n- `cts:camera:ptz:tap-to-center` — stays separate (takes offset coordinates, not a state value)\n\nThis reduces 6 events → 1 for the \"set a value\" category, while keeping the semantically distinct ones separate. Complexity-wise it's lower: one handler with a simple `if (payload.zoom !== undefined) setZoom(...)` pattern vs. 6 separate handler registrations.\n\n---\n\nWant me to apply all 9 changes to the design doc now?"
          }
        ]
      }
    },

              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Fix #1 and #3: Replace DB schema to use metadata blob and reuse host/port",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "## Database Schema\n\n### Modified: `device_connections`\n\nCamera-specific configuration is stored in the existing `metadata` JSON column, consistent with how OBS stores its device-specific settings. No new columns are added to `device_connections`.\n\nThe existing `host` and `port` columns are reused for VISCA connectivity:\n- When VISCA is enabled: `host` = camera's IP address, `port` = VISCA port (default 5500)\n- When VISCA is not enabled: `host` = `\"127.0.0.1\"` (placeholder), `port` = `5500` (default). The user never sees these values unless they enable VISCA in the admin form.\n\n**Camera metadata schema** (stored as JSON in `metadata` column):\n\n```typescript\ninterface CameraMetadata {\n  ndiSourceName: string;           // required — NDI source name for video + PTZ\n  fovWideAngle: number;            // default 60 — for tap-to-center math\n  cameraModel: CameraModel;        // \"generic\" | \"tongveo-nvs20a-4kn\"\n  cameraFeatures: CameraFeature[]; // enabled features array\n  viscaEnabled: boolean;            // whether to use host/port for VISCA polling\n  aiHttpCookie?: string;            // encrypted — for AI HTTP API (non-generic models only)\n  aiCredentialId?: string;          // encrypted — for AI HTTP API (non-generic models only)\n}\n```\n\nValidation of `deviceType` values is enforced at the route/TypeScript level, not via SQL CHECK constraint (SQLite doesn't support altering CHECK constraints on existing tables).\n\nSchema migration: no migration needed — the `metadata` column already exists as a TEXT field. Camera devices simply store a different JSON shape than OBS devices.\n\n### New: `camera_presets`\n\nPresets remain in a separate table (not in metadata) because they have independent CRUD lifecycle, benefit from indexing and cascade delete, and avoid read-modify-write race conditions on reorder operations.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE camera_presets (\n  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  cameraId TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES device_connections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  sortOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  storedOnCamera INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  cameraPresetSlot INTEGER,\n  pan REAL,\n  tilt REAL,\n  zoom REAL,\n  focus REAL,\n  autoFocus INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, -- boolean\n  aiTracking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  aiTilt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean (AI controls tilt axis)\n  aiZoom INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean (AI controls zoom axis)\n  createdAt TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_camera_presets_camera ON camera_presets(cameraId);\n```",
                "oldStr": "## Database Schema\n\n### Modified: `device_connections`\n\n```sql\n-- Existing columns remain unchanged. New columns:\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN ndiSourceName TEXT; -- cameras: NDI source for video+PTZ; OBS: NDI output for preview\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN viscaHost TEXT; -- cameras only: optional VISCA IP for position polling\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN viscaPort INTEGER DEFAULT 5500; -- cameras only: optional VISCA port\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN fovWideAngle REAL DEFAULT 60.0; -- cameras only\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN cameraFeatures TEXT; -- cameras only: JSON array of enabled features\n```\n\nCamera devices store `\"127.0.0.1\"` / `0` in the existing `host` / `port` NOT NULL columns (these are used by OBS devices but irrelevant for cameras).\n\nSchema migration uses the existing ad-hoc column-check pattern: at startup, check for missing columns via `PRAGMA table_info(device_connections)` and add them if absent (same pattern as `migrateMetadataTemplates`). Validation of `deviceType` values is enforced at the route/TypeScript level, not via SQL CHECK constraint (SQLite doesn't support altering CHECK constraints on existing tables).\n\n### New: `camera_presets`\n\nPresets remain in a separate table (not in metadata) because they have independent CRUD lifecycle, benefit from indexing and cascade delete, and avoid read-modify-write race conditions on reorder operations.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE camera_presets (\n  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  cameraId TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES device_connections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  sortOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  storedOnCamera INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  cameraPresetSlot INTEGER,\n  pan REAL,\n  tilt REAL,\n  zoom REAL,\n  focus REAL,\n  autoFocus INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, -- boolean\n  aiTracking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  aiTilt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean (AI controls tilt axis)\n  aiZoom INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean (AI controls zoom axis)\n  createdAt TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_camera_presets_camera ON camera_presets(cameraId);\n```\n\n### New columns on `device_connections` for camera model and AI config\n\n```sql\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN cameraModel TEXT DEFAULT 'generic'; -- 'generic' | 'tongveo-nvs20a-4kn'\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN aiHttpCookie TEXT; -- encrypted, for AI tracking HTTP requests\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN aiCredentialId TEXT; -- encrypted, for AI tracking API auth\n```",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/design.md"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
