                "newStr": "## Database Schema\n\n### `device_connections` — Camera Usage\n\nCamera-specific configuration is stored in the existing `metadata` JSON column, consistent with how OBS stores its device-specific settings. No new columns are added to `device_connections`.\n\nThe existing `host` and `port` columns are reused for VISCA connectivity:\n- When VISCA is enabled: `host` = camera's IP address, `port` = VISCA port (default 5500)\n- When VISCA is not enabled: `host` = `\"127.0.0.1\"` (placeholder), `port` = `5500` (default). The user never sees these values unless they enable VISCA in the admin form.\n\n**Camera metadata schema** (stored as JSON in `metadata` column):\n\n```typescript\ninterface CameraMetadata {\n  ndiSourceName: string;           // required — NDI source name for video + PTZ\n  fovWideAngle: number;            // default 60 — for tap-to-center math\n  cameraModel: CameraModel;        // \"generic\" | \"tongveo-nvs20a-4kn\"\n  cameraFeatures: CameraFeature[]; // enabled features array\n  viscaEnabled: boolean;            // whether to use host/port for VISCA polling\n  aiHttpCookie?: string;            // encrypted — for AI HTTP API (non-generic models only)\n  aiCredentialId?: string;          // encrypted — for AI HTTP API (non-generic models only)\n}\n```\n\n**OBS metadata schema** (existing, extended with NDI source name for preview):\n\n```typescript\ninterface ObsMetadata {\n  ndiOutputName?: string;  // e.g., \"OBS-MACHINE (OBS)\" — for NDI preview\n  // ... existing OBS fields\n}\n```\n\nNo schema migration needed — the `metadata` column already exists as TEXT. Camera devices simply store a different JSON shape than OBS devices. Validation of `deviceType` values is enforced at the route/TypeScript level.\n\n### New: `camera_presets`\n\nPresets remain in a separate table (not in metadata) because they have independent CRUD lifecycle, benefit from indexing and cascade delete, and avoid read-modify-write race conditions on reorder operations.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE camera_presets (\n  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  cameraId TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES device_connections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  sortOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  storedOnCamera INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  cameraPresetSlot INTEGER,\n  pan REAL,\n  tilt REAL,\n  zoom REAL,\n  focus REAL,\n  autoFocus INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, -- boolean\n  aiTracking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  aiTilt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean (AI controls tilt axis)\n  aiZoom INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean (AI controls zoom axis)\n  createdAt TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_camera_presets_camera ON camera_presets(cameraId);\n```",
                "oldStr": "## Database Schema\n\n### Modified: `device_connections`\n\n```sql\n-- Existing columns remain unchanged. New columns:\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN ndiSourceName TEXT; -- cameras: NDI source for video+PTZ; OBS: NDI output for preview\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN viscaHost TEXT; -- cameras only: optional VISCA IP for position polling\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN viscaPort INTEGER DEFAULT 5500; -- cameras only: optional VISCA port\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN fovWideAngle REAL DEFAULT 60.0; -- cameras only\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN cameraFeatures TEXT; -- cameras only: JSON array of enabled features\n```\n\nCamera devices store `\"127.0.0.1\"` / `0` in the existing `host` / `port` NOT NULL columns (these are used by OBS devices but irrelevant for cameras).\n\nSchema migration uses the existing ad-hoc column-check pattern: at startup, check for missing columns via `PRAGMA table_info(device_connections)` and add them if absent (same pattern as `migrateMetadataTemplates`). Validation of `deviceType` values is enforced at the route/TypeScript level, not via SQL CHECK constraint (SQLite doesn't support altering CHECK constraints on existing tables).\n\n### New: `camera_presets`\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE camera_presets (\n  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  cameraId TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES device_connections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  sortOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n  storedOnCamera INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  cameraPresetSlot INTEGER,\n  pan REAL,\n  tilt REAL,\n  zoom REAL,\n  focus REAL,\n  autoFocus INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, -- boolean\n  aiTracking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean\n  aiTilt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean (AI controls tilt axis)\n  aiZoom INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- boolean (AI controls zoom axis)\n  createdAt TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_camera_presets_camera ON camera_presets(cameraId);\n```\n\n### New columns on `device_connections` for camera model and AI config\n\n```sql\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN cameraModel TEXT DEFAULT 'generic'; -- 'generic' | 'tongveo-nvs20a-4kn'\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN aiHttpCookie TEXT; -- encrypted, for AI tracking HTTP requests\nALTER TABLE device_connections ADD COLUMN aiCredentialId TEXT; -- encrypted, for AI tracking API auth\n```",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/design.md"
              }
            }
          }
        ]

                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "### Widget: `CameraWidget`\n\n```\nWidgetContainer (title: \"Camera\", connections: [{ label: \"Camera\", status }])\n├── CameraDropdown (react-select, darkSelectStyles; disabled if only 1 camera)\n├── FullWidgetOverlay (covers video + controls when offline/connecting)\n│   └── \"Connecting...\" | \"Camera Offline\" | \"Tap to Reconnect\"\n├── CompactMode (when widget too small for controls)\n│   └── VideoContainer (tap opens CameraControlModal)\n│       └── <video> (object-fit: contain, centered)\n└── ExpandedMode (when widget large enough)\n    ├── VideoSection (left, fills available height, double-tap-to-center enabled)\n    │   └── <video> (object-fit: contain, centered)\n    └── ControlsSection (right, ~60% width)\n        ├── VirtualJoystick\n        ├── ZoomSlider (ion-range, vertical)\n        ├── ToggleRow (AI Tracking, AI Tilt, AI Zoom — ADMIN/AvPowerUser only)\n        ├── FocusRow (Auto Focus toggle + ion-range focus slider — ADMIN/AvPowerUser only)\n        └── PresetList (3 visible, scrollable)\n```",
                "oldStr": "### Widget: `CameraWidget`\n\n```\nWidgetContainer (title: \"Camera\", connections: [{ label: \"Camera\", status }])\n├── CameraDropdown (hidden if only 1 camera, IonSelect)\n├── CompactMode (when widget too small for controls)\n│   └── VideoContainer (tap opens CameraControlModal)\n│       ├── <video> (object-fit: contain, centered)\n│       └── ConnectingOverlay | OfflineOverlay\n└── ExpandedMode (when widget large enough)\n    ├── VideoSection (left, ~40% width)\n    │   ├── <video> (object-fit: contain, centered, tap-to-center enabled)\n    │   └── ConnectingOverlay | OfflineOverlay\n    └── ControlsSection (right, ~60% width)\n        ├── VirtualJoystick\n        ├── ZoomSlider (vertical)\n        ├── ToggleRow (AI Tracking, AI Tilt, AI Zoom — ADMIN/AvPowerUser only)\n        ├── FocusRow (Auto Focus toggle + focus slider — ADMIN/AvPowerUser only)\n        └── PresetList (3 visible, scrollable)\n```",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/design.md"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }

    {

      "data": {
        "message_id": "d2074738-924f-409f-b5ac-6e08a0e79825",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Now update the zoom slider CSS to use ion-range:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "tooluse_8Skyl1kB4jVhkB33a2uzDe",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Fix #7: Replace input range with ion-range for zoom slider",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "### Zoom Slider\n\nVertical `<ion-range>` with `orientation=\"vertical\"`. Value 0 (bottom, wide) to 1 (top, telephoto). On `ionChange`, emits `cts:camera:set` with `{ cameraId, zoom }`. Reflects server state from `cameraStates[id].position.zoom`.\n\n```css\n.zoom-slider {\n  min-height: 10rem;\n  width: 2.75rem;\n}\n.zoom-slider ion-range {\n  --bar-height: 4px;\n  --knob-size: 20px;\n}\n```",
                "oldStr": "### Zoom Slider\n\nVertical `<input type=\"range\">` rotated 90° via CSS transform. Value 0 (bottom, wide) to 1 (top, telephoto). On change, emits `CTS_CAMERA_ZOOM_SET`. Reflects server state from `cameraStates[id].position.zoom`.\n\n```css\n.zoom-slider {\n  writing-mode: vertical-lr;\n  direction: rtl; /* 1.0 at top */\n  min-height: 10rem;\n  width: 2.75rem;\n}\n```",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/design.md"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },

            "data": "Now update the requirements doc to match the consolidated event:"

                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "12. THE Backend SHALL expose camera state via Socket.io using the established SocketModule pattern. Events: `stc:camera:state` (full state broadcast), `stc:camera:state:update` (single camera delta), `cts:camera:ptz:move:start`, `cts:camera:ptz:move:keepalive`, `cts:camera:ptz:move:stop`, `cts:camera:set` (partial state update — any undefined field is unchanged), `cts:camera:preset:activate`, `cts:camera:ptz:tap-to-center`. The `cts:camera:set` event accepts a payload of `{ cameraId, zoom?, focus?, autoFocus?, aiTracking?, aiTilt?, aiZoom? }` — only provided fields are applied to the camera. All event name constants SHALL be defined in `packages/shared/src/constants/socketEvents.ts`. THE `stc:camera:state` payload SHALL include per camera: `{ cameraId, connected, position: { pan, tilt, zoom, focus } | null, autoFocus, aiTracking, aiTilt, aiZoom, activePresetId: string | null, features: string[], capabilities: { tapToCenter: boolean }, presets: CameraPreset[] }`. THE `emitInitialState` handler SHALL send the state for all configured cameras. THE `CameraService` SHALL emit `bus:camera:state:changed` on the EventBus whenever camera state changes (position, connection, toggles, active preset). THE `CameraSocketModule` subscribes to this event to broadcast updates — consistent with the EventBus subscription pattern used by all other socket modules.",
                "oldStr": "12. THE Backend SHALL expose camera state via Socket.io using the established SocketModule pattern.                 "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "13. THE Backend SHALL implement AI tracking control via model-specific HTTP APIs. WHEN a camera's model is set to a known supported model (not \"Generic\"), THE `CameraService` SHALL use the model-specific driver to send AI tracking commands. FOR the Tongveo NVS20A-4KN model, THE Backend SHALL send HTTP POST requests to the camera's web interface at `http://{host}/api/aiControl` with JSON body: `{ \"ai_on\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_enable\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_mode\": \"1\", \"ai_auto_zoom\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_auto_tilt\": \"1\"|\"0\" }`. The `ai_on` and `ai_enable` fields map to the `ai-tracking` toggle (both \"1\" when enabled, both \"0\" when disabled). The `ai_auto_zoom` field maps to the `ai-tracking-zoom` toggle. The `ai_auto_tilt` field maps to the `ai-tracking-tilt` toggle. HTTP requests SHALL include the configured cookie (from the device's metadata, decrypted at runtime) in the `Cookie` header. WHEN enabling AI tracking, THE Backend SHALL immediately follow the `aiControl` request with a target selection command: HTTP POST to `http://{host}/api/setPTZCmd` with JSON body `{ \"Channel\": 0, \"PtzCmd\": 15, \"param1\": 7, \"param2\": 0, \"ID\": \"{configured credential ID from metadata}\" }`. This tells the camera to track the first detected subject. THE Backend SHALL NOT send the `setPTZCmd` command when disabling AI tracking — only the `aiControl` command is sent when turning AI off. If a configurable delay is needed between the two requests in the future, THE Backend SHALL support a `AI_ENABLE_DELAY_MS` code constant (default: 0) inserted between the `aiControl` and `setPTZCmd` calls. IF the HTTP request fails (timeout, non-2xx response, network error), THE Backend SHALL emit a Toast-level notification: \"AI tracking command failed — check camera connection and credentials.\" and log the error at WARN level.",

                    "Text": "13. THE Backend SHALL implement AI tracking control via model-specific HTTP APIs. WHEN a camera's model is set to a known supported model (not \"Generic\"), THE `CameraService` SHALL use the model-specific driver to send AI tracking commands. FOR the Tongveo NVS20A-4KN model, THE Backend SHALL send HTTP POST requests to the camera's web interface at `http://{viscaHost}/api/aiControl` with JSON body: `{ \"ai_on\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_enable\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_mode\": \"1\", \"ai_auto_zoom\": \"1\"|\"0\", \"ai_auto_tilt\": \"1\"|\"0\" }`. The `ai_on` and `ai_enable` fields map to the `ai-tracking` toggle (both \"1\" when enabled, both \"0\" when disabled). The `ai_auto_zoom` field maps to the `ai-tracking-zoom` toggle. The `ai_auto_tilt` field maps to the `ai-tracking-tilt` toggle. HTTP requests SHALL include the configured cookie in the `Cookie` header. WHEN enabling AI tracking, THE Backend SHALL immediately follow the `aiControl` request with a target selection command: HTTP POST to `http://{viscaHost}/api/setPTZCmd` with JSON body `{ \"Channel\": 0, \"PtzCmd\": 15, \"param1\": 7, \"param2\": 0, \"ID\": \"{configured credential ID}\" }`. This tells the camera to track the first detected subject. THE Backend SHALL NOT send the `setPTZCmd` command when disabling AI tracking — only the `aiControl` command is sent when turning AI off. If a configurable delay is needed between the two requests in the future, THE Backend SHALL support a `AI_ENABLE_DELAY_MS` code constant (default: 0) inserted between the `aiControl` and `setPTZCmd` calls. IF the HTTP request fails (timeout, non-2xx response, network error), THE Backend SHALL emit a Toast-level notification: \"AI tracking command failed — check camera connection and credentials.\" and log the error at WARN level.\n\n---\n\n### Requirement 4: NDI Camera Video Preview"
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    },

            "data": "Now update Req 7.1 to mention metadata and host/port reuse instead of new columns:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "tooluse_UwSzdgthYYvFeDOmTEpKzK",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Update Req 7.1 to reflect metadata blob and host/port reuse",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "Camera device CRUD uses the existing `/api/admin/devices` endpoints with conditional validation: when `deviceType === \"camera-ptz\"`, the backend validates that `metadata.ndiSourceName` is present (required) and accepts optional `metadata.cameraModel`, `metadata.fovWideAngle`, `metadata.cameraFeatures`, `metadata.viscaEnabled`, `metadata.aiHttpCookie` (encrypted), and `metadata.aiCredentialId` (encrypted) fields. WHEN VISCA is enabled, the `host` and `port` columns store the camera's IP and VISCA port respectively. WHEN VISCA is not enabled, `host` and `port` are stored as `\"127.0.0.1\"` and `5500` (placeholders — the user never sees them unless they enable VISCA). The admin form SHALL show VISCA fields as an optional \"Position Polling (Recommended)\" section with a toggle to enable/disable.",
                "oldStr": "Camera device CRUD uses the existing `/api/admin/devices` endpoints with conditional validation: when `deviceType === \"camera-ptz\"`, the backend validates `ndiSourceName` is present (required) and accepts optional `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, `fovWideAngle`, `cameraFeatures`, `cameraModel`, `aiHttpCookie` (encrypted), and `aiCredentialId` (encrypted) fields. The existing `host`/`port` fields are auto-populated with `\"127.0.0.1\"`/`0` for cameras (not shown in the admin form). The admin form SHALL show VISCA fields as an optional \"Position Polling (Recommended)\" section with a toggle to enable/disable. For camera devices, the existing `host` and `port` columns in `device_connections` SHALL be stored as `\"127.0.0.1\"` and `0` respectively — these columns are NOT NULL and used by OBS devices, but irrelevant for cameras (camera-specific connection details use `viscaHost`, `viscaPort`, and `ndiSourceName` columns).",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/requirements.md"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }

                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "1. THE admin Device Management page (`/admin/devices`) SHALL support a new device type `\"camera-ptz\"`. WHEN adding a camera, the admin SHALL provide: label, Camera Model (dropdown: \"Generic\" or a known supported model, e.g., \"Tongveo NVS20A-4KN\"), NDI source name (required — for video feed and PTZ control; the NDI SDK discovers cameras by name on the LAN via mDNS-like broadcast), optionally VISCA IP address and port (for enhanced position polling accuracy, default port 5500), and wide-angle field of view in degrees (`fovWideAngle`, used for tap-to-center calculations, defaulting to 60°). WHEN a non-Generic camera model is selected, THE admin form SHALL display an additional \"AI Tracking Configuration\" section containing: (a) an HTTP Cookie field (stored encrypted in device config — the admin obtains this from browser dev tools while interacting with the camera's web interface), (b) an API Credential ID field (stored encrypted — the admin obtains this from the request payload in browser dev tools). THE admin form SHALL display a cautionary note: \"The cookie and credential may expire if the camera is rebooted or its session times out. Verify these values remain stable. If they change, AI tracking features will stop working until updated.\" `docs/setup.md` SHALL document how to obtain the cookie and credential ID from the camera's web interface using browser developer tools. WHEN Camera Model is \"Generic\", AI tracking features (`ai-tracking`, `ai-tracking-zoom`, `ai-tracking-tilt`) SHALL NOT appear in the features section and SHALL be unavailable in the widget. Camera device CRUD uses the existing `/api/admin/devices` endpoints with conditional validation: when `deviceType === \"camera-ptz\"`, the backend validates that `metadata.ndiSourceName` is present (required) and accepts optional `metadata.cameraModel`, `metadata.fovWideAngle`, `metadata.cameraFeatures`, `metadata.viscaEnabled`, `metadata.aiHttpCookie` (encrypted), and `metadata.aiCredentialId` (encrypted) fields. WHEN VISCA is enabled, the `host` and `port` columns store the camera's IP and VISCA port respectively. WHEN VISCA is not enabled, `host` and `port` are stored as `\"127.0.0.1\"` and `5500` (placeholders — the user never sees them unless they enable VISCA). The admin form SHALL show VISCA fields as an optional \"Position Polling (Recommended)\" section with a toggle to enable/disable. IF the NDI SDK is not available (Req 1.13), THE admin page SHALL display a warning: \"NDI SDK not installed — camera features are unavailable. Install the NDI SDK to enable cameras.\" `docs/setup.md` SHALL document NDI SDK installation as a prerequisite for camera features. THE Backend SHALL receive NDI video frames via the `grandiose` native module's receiver API and pipe them to FFmpeg (via stdin) for transcoding to fMP4 — this avoids requiring the separate FFmpeg NDI plugin to be compiled.\n2. THE admin device detail panel for cameras SHALL display a \"Features\" section with toggles for each capability: `pan`, `tilt`, `zoom`, `focus`. WHEN the camera model is not \"Generic\", additional toggles SHALL appear: `ai-tracking`, `ai-tracking-tilt`, `ai-tracking-zoom`. All toggles SHALL default to enabled for a new camera. Disabling a feature hides or disables the corresponding control in the volunteer-facing widget.\n3. WHEN no VISCA connection is configured for a camera (NDI-only mode), THE detail panel SHALL display an informational note: \"No VISCA configured — position tracking uses last-commanded values, which may drift if the camera is controlled externally. Adding VISCA provides accurate position feedback for zoom slider and tap-to-center.\"\n4. WHEN the admin saves a camera configuration, THE Backend SHALL attempt to probe the camera on the selected protocol (per Req 3.5). THE admin page SHALL display the probe result: success (green checkmark with \"Connected\") or failure (red X with the error reason). Probe failure SHALL NOT prevent saving — the admin may be configuring a camera that is currently offline.\n5. THE admin device detail panel for cameras SHALL include a \"Presets\" section listing all configured presets for that camera in their display order. Each preset row SHALL display: name and whether it's stored on camera (badge: \"On Camera\" or \"Software Only\"). The list SHALL support drag-to-reorder — the admin drags preset rows into the desired order, and the backend assigns `sortOrder` values (0, 1, 2...) based on the resulting position. Action buttons: Edit, Delete. An \"Add Preset\" button SHALL be available below the list."
                }
              ],
              "status": "success"
            }
          }

The three changes that needed to flow back to requirements:\n\n1. ✅ **Req 4.2** — Dropdown disabled (not hidden) when only 1 camera\n2. ✅ **Req 4.9** — Offline/connecting overlay covers entire widget (video + controls), not just video\n3. ✅ **Req 7.1** — Removed cautionary note from admin UI (kept in setup docs reference only)\n\nThe other design changes (metadata blob, consolidated events, ion-range, react-select) were already updated in the requirements during the earlier batch.     {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "Prompt",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "926c3e24-d6ec-49c4-b635-154fc5957ac1",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "One of the fields we require during setup is the fovWideAngle -- I presume this is the field of view the camera can view when zoomed all the way out. Is there a matematical relationship between that and the field of view when it's completely zoomed in, that makes that not need specified? Or am I not understanding how that field is used overall?"
          }
        ],
        "meta": {
          "timestamp": 1780804932
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "AssistantMessage",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "faa16ee6-dc60-4894-aebb-2de2ef7ec5f6",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "You're understanding it correctly — `fovWideAngle` is the horizontal field of view at full wide (zoom = 0.0).\n\nThe spec currently uses a linear approximation for the effective FOV at any zoom level:\n\n```\neffectiveFov = fovWideAngle * (1.0 - zoomLevel)\n```\n\nThis means at full telephoto (zoom = 1.0), the effective FOV = 0°, which is obviously wrong — the camera still sees *something* at full zoom. A real camera's FOV at full telephoto is determined by its optical zoom ratio. For the Tongveo NVS20A-4KN with 20x optical zoom:\n\n- Wide: ~60° horizontal FOV\n- Telephoto: ~60° / 20 = ~3° horizontal FOV\n\nSo yes, there **is** a mathematical relationship. If we know the zoom ratio (20x for this camera), we can derive the telephoto FOV:\n\n```\nfovAtZoom = fovWideAngle / (1 + zoomLevel * (opticalZoomRatio - 1))\n```\n\nAt zoom = 0: `60 / 1 = 60°`\nAt zoom = 1: `60 / 20 = 3°`\n\nThis is more accurate than the linear formula. The only extra field needed is `opticalZoomRatio` (e.g., 20 for 20x zoom) — which is a fixed property of the camera model, not something that changes. We could either:\n\n1. **Store it in metadata** alongside `fovWideAngle` — admin enters both (or just the zoom ratio, since FOV wide can be looked up per model)\n2. **Derive it from the camera model** — if it's \"Tongveo NVS20A-4KN\", we know it's 20x. Generic cameras would need it specified.\n\nEither way, the admin doesn't need to specify `fovTelephoto` separately — it's `fovWide / zoomRatio`.\n\n**My recommendation:** Replace `fovWideAngle` with two fields in metadata: `fovWideAngle` (default 60) and `opticalZoomRatio` (default 20). Update the tap-to-center formula to the correct one above. Both are easily found on the camera's spec sheet. Want me to make this change?"
          }
        ]
      }
    },

            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Yes, let's make that adjustement."

THE Backend SHALL estimate the effective FOV at the current zoom level using: `effectiveFov = fovWideAngle / (1 + zoomLevel * (opticalZoomRatio - 1))`. At zoom 0.0 (wide), this yields `fovWideAngle`; at zoom 1.0 (telephoto), this yields `fovWideAngle / opticalZoomRatio`. This models the non-linear relationship between zoom position and field of view. The result is still an approximation — the volunteer can tap again or use the joystick for fine adjustment.",
                    "replaceAll": false
                  }
                }
              }
            },

              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Update tap-to-center formula in design to use opticalZoomRatio",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "**Tap-to-center:**\n\n```typescript\nfunction computeTapTarget(\n  currentPan: number,\n  currentTilt: number,\n  tapOffsetX: number, // -1 to 1\n  tapOffsetY: number, // -1 to 1\n  fovWideAngle: number,\n  opticalZoomRatio: number,\n  currentZoom: number,\n): { pan: number; tilt: number } {\n  const effectiveFov = fovWideAngle / (1 + currentZoom * (opticalZoomRatio - 1));\n  const hFovNorm = effectiveFov / 360; // fraction of full pan range\n  const vFovNorm = (effectiveFov * 9 / 16) / 180; // assuming 16:9, fraction of tilt range\n  return {\n    pan: clamp(currentPan + tapOffsetX * hFovNorm, -1, 1),\n    tilt: clamp(currentTilt + tapOffsetY * vFovNorm, -1, 1),\n  };\n}\n```",
                "oldStr": "**Tap-to-center:**\n\n```typescript\nfunction computeTapTarget(\n  currentPan: number,\n  currentTilt: number,\n  tapOffsetX: number, // -1 to 1\n  tapOffsetY: number, // -1 to 1\n  fovWideAngle: number,\n  currentZoom: number,\n): { pan: number; tilt: number } {\n  const effectiveFov = fovWideAngle * (1.0 - currentZoom);\n  const hFovNorm = effectiveFov / 360; // fraction of full pan range\n  const vFovNorm = (effectiveFov * 9 / 16) / 180; // assuming 16:9, fraction of tilt range\n  return {\n    pan: clamp(currentPan + tapOffsetX * hFovNorm, -1, 1),\n    tilt: clamp(currentTilt + tapOffsetY * vFovNorm, -1, 1),\n  };\n}\n```",
                "path": ".kiro/specs/video-control-and-preview/design.md"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }

        "message_id": "95a46305-7ff1-4659-92e5-803b3c9efebd",

            "kind": "toolResult",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "tooluse_p3CkyLX61AZNVEKZKMVjyF",
              "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "---\ninclusion: always\n---\n\n# Testing Strategy\n\nThis document defines how testing is approached across Invisible A/V Booth. It covers tooling, structure, and conventions — not what to test. Specific test cases and correctness properties live in feature specs.\n\n---\n\n## Definition of Done\n\nTests are part of every story's definition of done — not a separate phase. Unit tests follow the unit or component they cover. Integration tests close each backend story. A feature task is not complete until its associated test task passes.\n\n---\n\n## Stack\n\n| Layer            | Tool                           | Scope                                                                  |\n| ---------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Unit & component | Vitest + React Testing Library | Logic, hooks, components — both packages                               |\n| Property-based   | Vitest + fast-check            | Correctness properties (a form of unit test, not a separate layer)     |\n| Backend E2E      | Vitest                         | Full server with fake devices — REST/Socket.io API → services → SQLite |\n| Frontend E2E     | Playwright                     | Full user flows in the browser, mocked backend (HTTP + WebSocket)      |\n\n**Why two E2E layers**: Backend E2E tests (Vitest) verify that routes, services, the database, and socket events work together correctly with fake device clients — no browser involved. Frontend E2E tests (Playwright) verify that the UI drives the correct HTTP and WebSocket calls and responds correctly to server events — no real backend involved. These are complementary, not redundant. Both run via `npm run test:e2e` in their respective packages and are included in root `npm run ci`.\n\n---\n\n## Unit & Component Tests (Vitest + RTL)\n\nEach package manages its own `vitest.config.ts`. Test files live alongside the code they test (`AudioWidget.tsx` → `AudioWidget.test.tsx`).\n\n### Coverage\n\n- Minimum thresholds: **90% lines and statements, 85% branches**\n- Enforced as a hard CI failure\n- Measured per-package, not as a monorepo aggregate\n\n### React Testing Library\n\n- Test behavior, not implementation — query by role, label, or `data-testid`, never by class or internal state\n- Use `@testing-library/user-event` for all interactions (not `fireEvent`)\n- Prefer `screen` queries over destructured render results\n\n### Backend Unit Tests\n\n- Use Vitest with `environment: \"node\"`\n- Mock external device clients at the abstraction layer boundary — never mock internal logic\n- Test state reconciliation, error handling, and command routing\n\n### Property-Based Tests\n\n- Use `fast-check` within Vitest — same test file as the unit under test\n- Apply where the design doc specifies correctness properties (e.g., template interpolation in `SessionManifestService`)\n- Property-based tests are unit tests; they do not require a separate file or test run\n\n---\n\n## Backend E2E Tests (Vitest)\n\nBackend e2e tests exercise the full path from the API boundary (REST endpoint or Socket.io event) through services and down to the database, using fake device clients with configurable responses. No browser or real hardware is involved.\n\n### Architecture\n\nThe tests use a shared `buildApp()` factory (`src/app.ts`) that assembles the full Express + Socket.io application. This is the same factory used by `index.ts` in production, ensuring test and production wiring never drift apart. Tests inject fakes for external dependencies:\n\n| Dependency                       | Production                         | Test                                                                           |\n| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| OBS WebSocket                    | `obs-websocket-js`                 | `createFakeObs()` — mock with event simulation and stateful recording tracking |\n| Platform APIs (YouTube/Facebook) | `YouTubeClient` / `FacebookClient` | `FakePlatformClient` — enqueueable responses and call recording                |\n| RTMP relay (node-media-server)   | Real NMS instance                  | `createFakeNms()` — no-op                                                      |\n| FFmpeg forwarders                | `child_process.spawn`              | `createFakeSpawn()` — emits `close` immediately                                |\n| Database                         | File-backed SQLite                 | In-memory SQLite (`:memory:`) with identical schema                            |\n\n### Fake Response Sequencing\n\n`FakePlatformClient` supports enqueueable responses so tests can configure multi-step scenarios:\n\n```typescript\n// First call succeeds, second call throws\nfakePlatformClient\n  .enqueue(\"createBroadcast\", { broadcastId: \"b1\", ... })\n  .enqueue(\"createBroadcast\", new PlatformError(\"BROADCAST_CREATE_FAILED\", \"quota exceeded\"));\n```\n\nWhen no response is enqueued, the fake returns a sensible default. Errors are thrown when an `Error` instance is enqueued.\n\n### Test Harness\n\nAll e2e tests use a shared harness (`tests/integration/harness.ts`) that provides:\n\n- `buildTestServer(opts?)` — creates an in-memory DB, applies schema, optionally seeds KJV data or platform configs, wires up the full app with fakes, and listens on an ephemeral port. Returns the app context, fakes, port, and a supertest agent.\n- `resetServer(server)` — truncates all tables and resets fakes between tests. Does not restart the server or re-register event bus listeners (~1ms).\n- `destroyServer(server)` — tears down the server, services, and event bus listeners.\n- `loginAs(agent, authService, username, password, role)` — creates a user, logs in, changes password, and returns the auth cookie.\n- `loginAsAdmin(agent, authService)` — shorthand for creating and logging in as an ADMIN.\n- `loginRaw(agent, authService, ...)` — logs in without changing password, for testing password-change enforcement.\n\n### Structure\n\nE2e test files live in `tests/integration/`, separate from unit tests in `src/`:\n\n```\npackages/backend/\n  src/\n    app.ts                              ← shared buildApp() factory\n    routes/\n      authRoutes.ts\n      authRoutes.test.ts                ← unit test\n  tests/\n    integration/\n      fakes.ts                          ← FakePlatformClient, createFakeObs, etc.\n      harness.ts                        ← buildTestServer, resetServer, login helpers\n      routes/\n        auth.test.ts                    ← e2e: full server, real DB, fake devices\n        admin-users.test.ts\n        edge-cases.test.ts              ← expired JWTs, 403 sweep, password enforcement\n        ...\n      gateway/\n        socket.test.ts                  ← Socket.io e2e: OBS commands, manifest, auth\n        streaming.test.ts               ← streaming lifecycle, recording, no_source\n```\n\n### Execution\n\n- **Config:** `vitest.integration.config.ts` — separate from unit test config\n- **Script:** `npm run test:e2e` (backend package), also run by root `npm run ci`\n- **Parallelism:** `fileParallelism: false` — tests run sequentially because the `eventBus` is a module-level singleton shared across files in the same thread pool\n- **Lifecycle:** One server per test file (`beforeAll`), table truncation between tests (`beforeEach`), full teardown (`afterAll`)\n\n### Conventions\n\n- Each test is independent — `resetServer()` between tests ensures no state leakage\n- Tests verify the full wiring path: HTTP request → middleware → route → service → database → response, or socket event → gateway → module → service → event bus → broadcast\n- Streaming lifecycle tests use `afterEach` cleanup to ensure the platform state machine returns to idle, preventing cross-test contamination\n- Socket tests extract the raw JWT from the auth cookie for `socket.io-client` auth; cookie-based socket auth is also tested separately\n- `BCRYPT_ROUNDS=1` in test env keeps password hashing fast (~1ms vs ~200ms)\n\n---\n\n## Frontend E2E Tests (Playwright)\n\nPlaywright handles both HTTP (REST) and WebSocket (Socket.io) mocking natively — no stub server needed.\n\n- HTTP mocked via `page.route()`\n- WebSocket mocked via `page.routeWebSocket()`\n- Test files are named by user flow, not by component: `obs-stream-start-flow.spec.ts`\n\n### Structure\n\n```\npackages/frontend/\n  playwright/\n    e2e/                    ← test files, named by user flow\n    fixtures/\n      payloads/             ← typed payload factories, one file per domain\n    support/\n      routes/               ← shared route handlers (HTTP + WebSocket), one file per domain\n      helpers.ts\n  playwright.config.ts\n```\n\n### Backend Mocking\n\nAll backend communication is mocked — no real backend runs during Playwright tests.\n\n- HTTP (REST) requests are mocked via `page.route()`\n- WebSocket (Socket.io) connections are mocked via `page.routeWebSocket()`\n\nUse shared route handlers for any mock used in more than one test file. If a mock is only used in a single file, it may be defined inline. If an inline mock later becomes shared, lift it to `support/routes/`.\n\n### Payload Factories\n\nEach domain file in `fixtures/payloads/` exports typed factory functions returning a full happy-path payload by default, with an optional partial override. Use the same factory for both the mock and the assertion — the test and mock stay in sync.\n\n```ts\nexport function obsStatePayload(overrides: Partial<ObsStatePayload> = {}): ObsStatePayload {\n  return { ...OBS_STATE_DEFAULTS, ...overrides };\n}\n```\n\n### Shared Route Handlers\n\nEach file in `support/routes/` exports functions that register mocks. Defaults always use the happy-path payload. Return the `WebSocketRoute` handle from socket helpers so tests can push server-initiated events mid-test.\n\n### Domain Files\n\nPayload and route files are organized by domain. Only `obs.ts`, `session.ts`, and `auth.ts` are in scope for the initial release. Future domains (`audio.ts`, `camera.ts`, `overlays.ts`) are created when the corresponding widgets are built.\n\n### Route Conventions\n\n- Shared routes always default to happy-path, no errors\n- Error and edge-case payloads are passed in via factory overrides\n- Never hardcode payload data inline in test files — always use a factory\n\n---\n\n## Testability by Design\n\nIf test code is as complex as (or more complex than) the code it tests, the production code needs to be simplified. Hard to test = hard to read.\n\n### Private by Convention (`_method`)\n\nMethods that are internal implementation details but need direct testing should be prefixed with `_` rather than using TypeScript's `private` keyword. This allows tests to call them directly without routing through complex orchestration flows.\n\nApply this when:\n\n- A method has multiple branches that are hard to reach through the public API\n- Testing the public method requires elaborate multi-step setup just to reach one branch\n- The method is a self-contained \"big idea\" within a larger orchestration\n\n### Decompose Complex Methods\n\nComplex orchestration methods should delegate to smaller, testable pieces:\n\n```ts\nasync startAll(): Promise<void> {\n  const entries = this._getIdlePlatforms();\n  if (entries.length === 0) return;\n\n  const results = await this._createBroadcasts(entries);\n  this._applyBroadcastResults(results, entries);\n\n  if (results.successful.length === 0) return;\n\n  const obsOk = await this._ensureObsStreaming();\n  if (!obsOk) {\n    this._cleanupFailedStart(results.successful);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  this._startForwarders(results.successful);\n}\n```\n\nEach extracted method is independently testable. The orchestration method has minimal branching — it reads like a recipe.\n\n### Control State Directly in Tests\n\nWhen testing behavior that depends on internal state (e.g., a platform being in \"streaming\" or \"error\" status), prefer calling exposed `_` methods to set up state rather than running full flows:\n\n```ts\n// Instead of: await service.startAll() just to get a platform into \"streaming\"\nservice._transitionPlatform(\"yt-1\", \"streaming\");\n\n// Now test the specific behavior that depends on streaming state\neventBus.emit(BUS_RELAY_STATE_CHANGED, { running: true, obsConnected: false });\nexpect(service.getPlatformStates().get(\"yt-1\")?.status).toBe(\"no_source\");\n```\n\nThis eliminates cascading mock requirements and makes each test's intent obvious.\n\n### Use `it.each` with Template Literals for State Machines\n\nWhen a function's behavior varies by input, use interpolated string tables:\n\n```ts\nit.each`\n  pollResult            | expectedStatus\n  ${{ healthy: true }}  | ${\"streaming\"}\n  ${{ healthy: false }} | ${\"error\"}\n  ${new Error(\"fail\")}  | ${\"error\"}\n`(\"recoverPlatform with $expectedStatus outcome\", async ({ pollResult, expectedStatus }) => {\n  service._transitionPlatform(\"yt-1\", \"recovering\");\n  mockClient.pollHealth.mockImplementation(() => (pollResult instanceof Error ? Promise.reject(pollResult) : Promise.resolve(pollResult)));\n  await service._recoverPlatform(\"yt-1\", entry);\n  expect(service.getPlatformStates().get(\"yt-1\")?.status).toBe(expectedStatus);\n});\n```\n\nIf rows get too wide, the function under test is doing too much.\n\n### When to Refactor for Testability\n\n- **New code**: Follow this pattern from the start.\n- **Existing code being heavily modified**: Refactor to match during the modification.\n- **Existing code that works and isn't being touched**: Leave it alone.\n\n---\n\n## data-\\* Attribute Conventions\n\nSee `code-style.md` for the full attribute reference. In tests:\n\n- Use `data-testid` to select elements — never use class names, IDs, or DOM structure\n- Use `data-state` and `data-status` for assertions about UI state\n\n---\n\n## General Rules\n\n- Tests must be deterministic — no reliance on timing, random values, or external network calls\n- Each test is independent — no shared mutable state between tests\n- Prefer testing one behavior per test\n- No live hardware is available during development; all hardware clients are mocked at their abstraction boundary\n\n---\n\n## Frontend Mocking Patterns\n\n### Ionic Component Mocks\n\nIonic components don't render properly in jsdom. A shared mock file at `src/test/ionicMocks.tsx` replaces `IonInput`, `IonButton`, `IonCheckbox`, `IonTextarea`, `IonToggle`, `IonSelect`, and `IonSelectOption` with plain HTML equivalents.\n\n**Important:** This file is NOT loaded via `setupFiles`. Each test file that renders Ionic components must explicitly import it:\n\n```ts\nimport \"../test/ionicMocks\"; // or \"../../test/ionicMocks\" depending on depth\n```\n\nThe mock is hoisted by Vitest so the import order doesn't matter relative to component imports.\n\n### react-select Mock\n\nComponents using `react-select` need a mock that renders a native `<select>`. Use this pattern:\n\n```ts\nvi.mock(\"react-select\", () => ({\n  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any\n  default: ({ options, onChange, value, placeholder }: any) => {\n    const opts = options as Array<{ value: string; label: string }>;\n    return (\n      <select\n        data-testid=\"my-select\"\n        value={value?.value ?? \"\"}\n        onChange={(e: { target: { value: string } }) => {\n          const opt = opts.find((o) => o.value === e.target.value);\n          if (opt) onChange(opt);\n        }}\n      >\n        {opts.map((o: { value: string; label: string }) => (\n          <option key={o.value} value={o.value}>{o.label}</option>\n        ))}\n      </select>\n    );\n  },\n}));\n```\n\nThen interact with it using `fireEvent.change(screen.getByTestId(\"my-select\"), { target: { value: \"option-value\" } })`.\n\n### jsdom Limitations\n\njsdom does not support:\n\n- `AnimationEvent` constructor — animation-end handlers cannot be reliably tested in unit tests. Test these through Playwright e2e instead.\n- `window.location` assignment — cannot test OAuth redirects via `window.location.href = url`. Verify the fetch call was made and trust the redirect in e2e.\n- CSS transitions/animations — elements never actually animate, so `transitionend`/`animationend` events don't fire naturally.\n\n### Overlay Namespace (Socket.IO)\n\nThe `/overlay` namespace is unauthenticated (used by the OBS browser source). Integration tests connect directly without JWT:\n\n```ts\nimport { io as ioClient } from \"socket.io-client\";\n\nconst socket = ioClient(`http://localhost:${port}/overlay`, {\n  transports: [\"websocket\"],\n});\n```\n\nThis is different from the main namespace which requires JWT auth via `socket.io-client`'s `auth` option."

This allows tests to call them directly without routing through complex orchestration flows.\n\nApply this when:\n\n- A method has multiple branches that are hard to reach through the public API\n- Testing the public method requires elaborate multi-step setup just to reach one branch\n- The method is a self-contained \"big idea\" within a larger orchestration\n\n### Decompose Complex Methods\n\nComplex orchestration methods should delegate to smaller, testable pieces:\n\n```ts\nasync startAll(): Promise<void> {\n  const entries = this._getIdlePlatforms();\n  if (entries.length === 0) return;\n\n  const results = await this._createBroadcasts(entries);\n  this._applyBroadcastResults(results, entries);\n\n  if (results.successful.length === 0) return;\n\n  const obsOk = await this._ensureObsStreaming();\n  if (!obsOk) {\n    this._cleanupFailedStart(results.successful);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  this._startForwarders(results.successful);\n}\n```\n\nEach extracted method is independently testable. The orchestration method has minimal branching — it reads like a recipe.\n\n### Control State Directly in Tests\n\nWhen testing behavior that depends on internal state (e.g., a platform being in \"streaming\" or \"error\" status), prefer calling exposed `_` methods to set up state rather than running full flows:\n\n```ts\n// Instead of: await service.startAll() just to get a platform into \"streaming\"\nservice._transitionPlatform(\"yt-1\", \"streaming\");\n\n// Now test the specific behavior that depends on streaming state\neventBus.emit(BUS_RELAY_STATE_CHANGED, { running: true, obsConnected: false });\nexpect(service.getPlatformStates().get(\"yt-1\")?.status).toBe(\"no_source\");\n```\n\nThis eliminates cascading mock requirements and makes each test's intent obvious.\n\n### Use `it.each` with Template Literals for State Machines\n\nWhen a function's behavior varies by input, use interpolated string tables:\n\n```ts\nit.each`\n  pollResult            | expectedStatus\n  ${{ healthy: true }}  | ${\"streaming\"}\n  ${{ healthy: false }} | ${\"error\"}\n  ${new Error(\"fail\")}  | ${\"error\"}\n`(\"recoverPlatform with $expectedStatus outcome\", async ({ pollResult, expectedStatus }) => {\n  service._transitionPlatform(\"yt-1\", \"recovering\");\n  mockClient.pollHealth.mockImplementation(() => (pollResult instanceof Error ? Promise.reject(pollResult) : Promise.resolve(pollResult)));\n  await service._recoverPlatform(\"yt-1\", entry);\n  expect(service.getPlatformStates().get(\"yt-1\")?.status).toBe(expectedStatus);\n});\n```\n\nIf rows get too wide, the function under test is doing too much.\n\n### When to Refactor for Testability\n\n- **New code**: Follow this pattern from the start.\n- **Existing code being heavily modified**: Refactor to match during the modification.\n- **Existing code that works and isn't being touched**: Leave it alone.\n\n---\n\n## data-\\* Attribute Conventions\n\nSee `code-style.md` for the full attribute reference. In tests:\n\n- Use `data-testid` to select elements — never use class names, IDs, or DOM structure\n- Use `data-state` and `data-status` for assertions about UI state\n\n---\n\n## General Rules\n\n- Tests must be deterministic — no reliance on timing, random values, or external network calls\n- Each test is independent — no shared mutable state between tests\n- Prefer testing one behavior per test\n- No live hardware is available during development; all hardware clients are mocked at their abstraction boundary\n\n---\n\n## Frontend Mocking Patterns\n\n### Ionic Component Mocks\n\nIonic components don't render properly in jsdom. A shared mock file at `src/test/ionicMocks.tsx` replaces `IonInput`, `IonButton`, `IonCheckbox`, `IonTextarea`, `IonToggle`, `IonSelect`, and `IonSelectOption` with plain HTML equivalents.\n\n**Important:** This file is NOT loaded via `setupFiles`. Each test file that renders Ionic components must explicitly import it:\n\n```ts\nimport \"../test/ionicMocks\"; // or \"../../test/ionicMocks\" depending on depth\n```\n\nThe mock is hoisted by Vitest so the import order doesn't matter relative to component imports.\n\n### react-select Mock\n\nComponents using `react-select` need a mock that renders a native `<select>`. Use this pattern:\n\n```ts\nvi.mock(\"react-select\", () => ({\n  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any\n  default: ({ options, onChange, value, placeholder }: any) => {\n    const opts = options as Array<{ value: string; label: string }>;\n    return (\n      <select\n        data-testid=\"my-select\"\n        value={value?.value ?? \"\"}\n        onChange={(e: { target: { value: string } }) => {\n          const opt = opts.find((o) => o.value === e.target.value);\n          if (opt) onChange(opt);\n        }}\n      >\n        {opts.map((o: { value: string; label: string }) => (\n          <option key={o.value} value={o.value}>{o.label}</option>\n        ))}\n      </select>\n    );\n  },\n}));\n```\n\nThen interact with it using `fireEvent.change(screen.getByTestId(\"my-select\"), { target: { value: \"option-value\" } })`.\n\n### jsdom Limitations\n\njsdom does not support:\n\n- `AnimationEvent` constructor — animation-end handlers cannot be reliably tested in unit tests. Test these through Playwright e2e instead.\n- `window.location` assignment — cannot test OAuth redirects via `window.location.href = url`. Verify the fetch call was made and trust the redirect in e2e.\n- CSS transitions/animations — elements never actually animate, so `transitionend`/`animationend` events don't fire naturally.\n\n### Overlay Namespace (Socket.IO)\n\nThe `/overlay` namespace is unauthenticated (used by the OBS browser source). Integration tests connect directly without JWT:\n\n```ts\nimport { io as ioClient } from \"socket.io-client\";\n\nconst socket = ioClient(`http://localhost:${port}/overlay`, {\n  transports: [\"websocket\"],\n});\n```\n\nThis is different from the main namespace which requires JWT auth via `socket.io-client`'s `auth` option."
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }

                "content": "# Implementation Tasks — Video Control and Preview\n\nTests are part of each task's definition of done. Unit tests follow the unit or component they cover. Implement WebSocket endpoint registration — `/preview/obs` and `/preview/camera/:cameraId` paths, cookie-based JWT authentication on upgrade, 4401 close code on invalid token, 4503 close code when max streams reached.\n  - _Requirements: 1_\n\n- [ ] 8. Implement FFmpeg lifecycle — lazy spawn on first subscriber, 3-second grace period on last disconnect, fMP4 output flags, init segment (ftyp+moov) caching, fan-out to all subscribers.\n  - _Requirements: 1_\n\n- [ ] 9. Implement FFmpeg failure handling — restart after 2s delay, max 3 consecutive failures then close all subscribers, OS scheduling priority lower than streaming forwarders.\n  - _Requirements: 1_\n\n- [ ] 10.
